title: All About Me: I Can Do It Myself
subject: SEL
description: Preschool day plan from the 'All About Me' thematic week (September): I Can Do It Myself. Focus book: All by Myself — Mercer Mayer. Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: All by Myself — Mercer Mayer

Language Arts — Goal: Sequence what the character does all by himself.
Activity: We will read the focus book and put the character's self-help tasks in order with picture cards — first, next, last. Each child will pick one card showing something they can do by themselves too.
Materials: Focus book; self-help sequence cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A three-card sequence and sentence starters ('First I...') for children who need support.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Test fasteners: zips, buttons, and snaps.
Activity: Children will explore dressing boards with zippers, big buttons, snaps, and buckles, noticing which are easy and which need practice. We will chart our 'can do it' and 'still practicing' discoveries.
Materials: Dressing boards/frames; class chart
Grouping: Small groups — science/practical table
Support: Start with the largest buttons and zippers; extra unhurried time at the boards.

Social Science — Goal: Learn that asking a friend for help is also a skill.
Activity: Pairs will do a two-person job — carrying a tray together without tipping the (empty) cups. We will talk about how doing things ourselves and helping each other are both important.
Materials: Trays; empty plastic cups
Grouping: Pairs — around the classroom; teacher-guided
Support: Clearly defined roles (holder/walker) modeled by the teacher before pairs begin.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Sort clothing and count pairs.
Activity: Children will sort dress-up clothes into baskets — shirts, hats, socks — then find and count the pairs of socks, matching each pair by color or pattern.
Materials: Dress-up clothes; baskets
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: Two categories to sort first, and counting pairs together with a partner.

Creative Art — Goal: Decorate my 'Look What I Can Do' badge.
Activity: Each child will decorate a badge shape with stickers and markers, and the teacher will write the skill the child is proudest of across the middle. We will wear our badges for the rest of the day.
Materials: Badge templates; stickers; markers
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Stickers pre-peeled onto a tray edge and adapted-grip markers for easier control.

Music / Movement — Goal: Sing and act a getting-dressed song.
Activity: We will sing a teacher-led song about putting on shoes, hat, and coat, acting out each step in the right order. A real hat and scarf will be passed around for the verses.
Materials: Teacher-led song; hat and scarf props
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: Action picture cards shown before each verse so children can anticipate the movement.

Motor Activities — Goal: Pour water between cups with control.
Activity: At the pouring station, children will use small pitchers to pour water from cup to cup over a tray, practicing stopping at the line. Spills are part of learning — sponges are ready.
Materials: Small pitchers; cups; trays; sponges; water
Grouping: Centers — practical life table; teacher-supervised
Support: A smaller pitcher, less water, and two hands allowed, with an adult nearby.

Technology — Goal: Direct a photo of a friend doing a skill.
Activity: With the teacher holding the tablet, children will direct photos of classmates zipping, pouring, or tying (practicing on a shoe board). We will add the best photos to our 'We Can' board.
Materials: Class tablet (teacher-held); We Can board
Grouping: Small groups; teacher-led
Support: A picture checklist of skills to photograph, so the director knows what to look for.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Complete an outdoor skills circuit.
Activity: Outside, children will rotate through a skills circuit: hopscotch squares, throwing and catching a ball with a partner, and walking the low balance beam — all things their growing bodies can do.
Materials: Chalk hopscotch; soft balls; low balance beam
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-supervised
Support: Partner support at each station and a shorter circuit for children who tire.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Learn that trying hard things helps me grow.
Activity: We will talk about something that used to be hard and is now easier — like putting on shoes. Each child may name something they are still practicing, and we will cheer for practice, not just success.
Materials: Picture step-cards of a shoe-tying attempt; chart paper
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Picture choices to point to, and specific praise for effort every time a child shares.

title: All About Me: Celebrate Me!
subject: SEL
description: Preschool day plan from the 'All About Me' thematic week (September): Celebrate Me!. Focus book: I Like Myself! — Karen Beaumont. Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: I Like Myself! — Karen Beaumont

Language Arts — Goal: Share my class book page with the whole group.
Activity: We will reread the focus book, then each child will present their self-portrait page from our class book and tell one thing about themselves. The teacher will read dictated words aloud for any child who wants help.
Materials: Focus book; class book from the theme; self-portrait pages
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: The teacher reads the child's page while the child holds it up, if presenting alone feels too big.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Revisit our senses stations and record my favorites.
Activity: Children will rotate through three review stations — a smell station with sealed scent cups, a touch tray, and a sound shaker set — and mark their favorite discovery on a recording sheet with a sticker.
Materials: Scent cups (sealed); touch tray; sound shakers; sticker recording sheets
Grouping: Small groups — science table rotation
Support: A sticker placed by pointing, and fewer stations (two) for children who need a shorter task.

Social Science — Goal: Give a compliment to a classmate.
Activity: In our compliment circle, each child will pass the talking star to a friend and tell them one thing they like — a kind word, a good tower, a funny story. The teacher will start with a model compliment.
Materials: Talking star; compliment starter cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Compliment starter cards ('I like how you...') for children who need the first words.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Graph our favorite activity from the whole theme.
Activity: Children will vote with picture ballots for their favorite activity of the two weeks — handprints, senses, family pages, or pouring. We will graph the votes, count each column, and announce our class favorite.
Materials: Picture ballots; pocket-chart graph
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Counting with a partner, pointing to each ballot as it is counted.

Creative Art — Goal: Decorate my All About Me portfolio cover.
Activity: Children will decorate the cover of their theme portfolio with their favorite colors and drawings of favorite things, so the cover shows who they are before anyone opens it.
Materials: Portfolio covers; crayons; markers; stickers
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: A full choice of materials and adapted tools, so every child can decorate in their own way.

Music / Movement — Goal: Perform our favorite songs from the theme.
Activity: We will put on a mini show for ourselves: the body-parts song and the finger family song, with actions, performed in our celebration line — and recorded (audio) to share with families.
Materials: Teacher-led songs; voice recorder
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: Holding an instrument or prop instead of singing, for children who prefer to join that way.

Motor Activities — Goal: Show my motor skills at celebration stations.
Activity: Children will rotate through favorite motor stations from the theme: the balance beam, playdough face making, and clothespin clipping, showing a teacher one skill they are proud of.
Materials: Low balance beam; playdough and mats; clothespins and plates
Grouping: Small groups — movement area; teacher-supervised
Support: Extra time at each station and no racing — children go at their own pace.

Technology — Goal: Watch a slideshow of our two weeks together.
Activity: The teacher will project the photos we took across the theme — selfies, skills, family work, and celebrations — and children will name what we learned as each photo appears.
Materials: Projector; theme photos
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: The pointer job for a child who engages best with a role, and front seating for visibility.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Parade outdoors wearing my I Can badge.
Activity: We will wear our 'Look What I Can Do' badges on a parade walk around the playground, waving to other classes and ending at our meeting spot for a class cheer.
Materials: Badges from Day 9; playground loop
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: A buddy to walk with and a shorter loop that rejoins the group, for children who need it.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Learn to say kind words about myself.
Activity: Each child will finish the sentence 'I like myself because...' by telling or drawing their answer for the last page of their portfolio. The teacher will write each child's exact words.
Materials: Portfolio pages; sentence-frame card; crayons
Grouping: Large group then independent — carpet/tables
Support: The sentence frame and a drawing option for children not ready to dictate.

title: Autumn Days (Preschool Unit)
subject: Science
description: A 5-day preschool thematic unit on Autumn Days (September), written as an Almanac Original. Each day is a full plan — literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor, technology, outdoor learning, and a life lesson — with goals, materials, groupings, and support strategies, plus four standing centers for the week. Days: Day 1: Signs of Fall; Day 2: Leaves Are Falling; Day 3: Apples in Autumn; Day 4: Animals Get Ready; Day 5: Autumn Celebration. Focus books: Goodbye Summer, Hello Autumn; Leaf Man; The Apple Pie Tree; Fletcher and the Falling Leaves; We're Going on a Leaf Hunt.

title: Autumn Days: Signs of Fall
subject: Science
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Autumn Days' thematic week (September): Signs of Fall. Focus book: Goodbye Summer, Hello Autumn — Kenard Pak. Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: Goodbye Summer, Hello Autumn — Kenard Pak

Language Arts — Goal: Use autumn words: cooler, crisp, harvest, change.
Activity: We will read the focus book and pause at each page to name what is changing. Children will add autumn word cards with pictures to our word wall and use one word in a sentence about fall.
Materials: Focus book; autumn word cards; word wall
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Picture-supported word cards and pointing-and-naming for emerging talkers.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Observe and sort treasures from nature.
Activity: Children will explore a nature tray of leaves, acorns, and pinecones with magnifiers, then sort the items by a rule they choose — color, size, or feel — and explain their groups.
Materials: Nature tray (leaves, acorns, pinecones); magnifiers; sorting trays
Grouping: Small groups — science table
Support: Just two sorting groups to start, for children building classification skills.

Social Science — Goal: Share what my family does in autumn.
Activity: In our sharing circle, children will tell or show one thing their family does in fall — walks, apple picking, cozy dinners, watching leaves. The teacher will chart our ideas on a class web.
Materials: Sharing prompt cards; chart paper
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Picture prompt cards (walk, apples, leaves, food) to spark an idea to share.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Count leaf counters into numbered bags from 1 to 10.
Activity: Children will read the number on a leaf-shaped bag and count exactly that many large leaf counters into it, checking by touching each counter once.
Materials: Numbered leaf bags 1–10; large leaf counters
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: A number line strip and larger counters for children who need a visual and physical anchor.

Creative Art — Goal: Make leaf-rubbing pictures.
Activity: Children will place real leaves under paper and rub with the side of a crayon to reveal the leaf's shape and veins. We will compare rubbings and notice that every leaf is different.
Materials: Real leaves; thin paper; crayons (wrappers off)
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: The leaf taped down under the paper and a chunky crayon for easier rubbing.

Music / Movement — Goal: Float and fall like leaves with scarves.
Activity: We will move with scarves to gentle music — twirling high like leaves in the wind, then floating slowly down to the ground as the music quiets.
Materials: Scarves; recorded gentle music
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: A seated option with scarf movements only, and a defined dance spot.

Motor Activities — Goal: Pick up paper leaves with tongs for hand strength.
Activity: Children will use tongs to pick up paper leaves scattered on a mat and fill their baskets, working slowly to keep their grip all the way to the basket.
Materials: Tongs; paper leaves; baskets; mat
Grouping: Centers — fine motor table
Support: Easy-squeeze tongs and bigger leaves for children developing pinch strength.

Technology — Goal: Photograph signs of fall around our school.
Activity: With the teacher, small groups will use the class tablet to photograph signs of autumn — a changing tree, fallen leaves, a pinecone — then view the photos together and name each sign.
Materials: Class tablet (teacher-guided); projector
Grouping: Small groups — around the school; teacher-led
Support: The teacher holds the tablet while the child chooses and directs each shot.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Take a fall walk and collect one nature treasure.
Activity: We will walk the school grounds looking for signs of fall, and each child will collect one fallen treasure — a leaf, an acorn, a pinecone — for our science table collection.
Materials: Collection bags; school grounds
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: A buddy to walk and hunt with, and a teacher-carried spare bag for treasures found.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Learn that change is a natural and beautiful part of life.
Activity: We will talk about how the trees change in fall just like we grow and change, and change can be beautiful. Each child will share one change they like — cooler days, red leaves, or starting school.
Materials: Focus book (favorite pages); feelings chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Picture choices of autumn changes for children who need help finding an idea.

title: Autumn Days: Leaves Are Falling
subject: Science
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Autumn Days' thematic week (September): Leaves Are Falling. Focus book: Leaf Man — Lois Ehlert. Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: Leaf Man — Lois Ehlert

Language Arts — Goal: Retell where the wind blew the Leaf Man.
Activity: We will read the focus book and sequence the Leaf Man's journey with picture cards — over the marsh, the lake, and the meadow. Children will draw where they think the wind might blow him next.
Materials: Focus book; journey picture cards; drawing paper; crayons
Grouping: Large group then independent — carpet/tables
Support: Journey cards with the places pictured, so retelling can be shown by pointing in order.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Compare a green leaf and a fall leaf up close.
Activity: Children will examine a fresh green leaf and a colored fall leaf with magnifiers, noticing color, softness, and crispness. The teacher will explain simply that leaves stop making green in fall and their other colors show.
Materials: Green and fall leaves; magnifiers; observation sheet
Grouping: Small groups — science table
Support: Extra observation time and larger leaves for children who need to see details clearly.

Social Science — Goal: Work as a team to complete our leaf color chart.
Activity: Partners will be given a color to hunt for in our leaf collection — red, yellow, orange, or brown — and bring matching leaves to glue on the class color chart together.
Materials: Leaf collection; color chart; glue
Grouping: Pairs — science/art area; teacher-guided
Support: Partner pairing with a color card to carry and match against.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Sort leaves by color and graph how many we found.
Activity: Children will sort our collected leaves onto color mats, count each group, and build a graph with the leaves themselves. We will say which color our class found most.
Materials: Collected leaves; color mats; graph mat
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: Counting each color group aloud with a partner, touching every leaf once.

Creative Art — Goal: Create a leaf creature collage.
Activity: Children will arrange real pressed leaves into a person, animal, or bird and glue their design onto card stock, adding drawn details. Each artist will name their leaf creation for our display.
Materials: Pressed leaves; card stock; glue; crayons
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Leaves pre-pressed flat and a glue sponge, plus the option to copy the teacher's example arrangement.

Music / Movement — Goal: Move like leaves in changing wind.
Activity: To music that speeds up and slows down, children will twirl like leaves in strong wind and float gently when the wind calms, freezing as a 'leaf on the ground' when the music stops.
Materials: Recorded music with tempo changes; open rug space
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: A defined space spot and permission to float in place instead of traveling.

Motor Activities — Goal: Crumble dry leaves to build hand strength.
Activity: Children will crumble dry leaves into a tray with their fingers, listening to the crunch, then sprinkle the pieces onto glue shapes to make crunchy leaf art.
Materials: Dry leaves; trays; glue; shape outlines
Grouping: Centers — fine motor/science table
Support: Leaves in a zip bag to crumble for children who prefer not to touch them directly (teacher checks the bag is sealed).

Technology — Goal: Listen to autumn sounds and match them to pictures.
Activity: At the listening center, children will hear a recorded autumn story and a nature-sounds game — crunching leaves, wind, rain — tapping the picture that matches each sound.
Materials: Listening center; recorded story; tablet with nature sounds; picture board
Grouping: Centers — pairs; child-led after setup
Support: Headphones set by the teacher and a two-choice picture board for each sound.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Match real leaves to their silhouette cards outdoors.
Activity: On the playground, children will carry leaf silhouette cards and hunt for a real leaf that matches the shape, bringing matches back to compare with a friend's find.
Materials: Leaf silhouette cards; playground trees
Grouping: Pairs — outdoors; teacher-supervised
Support: A buddy to hunt with and only two silhouettes to match.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Learn to care for nature by taking only what has fallen.
Activity: We will talk about why we collect fallen leaves but leave growing ones on the tree — the tree still needs those. Each child will return one extra leaf to the garden bed as a thank-you to the trees.
Materials: Garden bed; collected leaves
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: The teacher models returning a leaf first, and gives specific praise for gentle hands outdoors.

title: Autumn Days: Apples in Autumn
subject: Science
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Autumn Days' thematic week (September): Apples in Autumn. Focus book: The Apple Pie Tree — Zoe Hall. Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: The Apple Pie Tree — Zoe Hall

Language Arts — Goal: Sequence an apple tree through the four seasons.
Activity: We will read the focus book and order season cards of the apple tree — blossoms, tiny apples, ripe apples, bare branches — using the words grow, ripen, and pick as we retell.
Materials: Focus book; apple-tree season cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Four season cards with strong picture cues and sentence starters for retelling.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Investigate the inside of an apple.
Activity: The teacher will cut an apple across the middle (adults only) to reveal the star of seeds inside. Children will count the seeds with magnifiers and may taste a slice — the teacher will first confirm apples are safe for every child, and any child may choose to observe instead.
Materials: Apple; teacher's cutting board and knife (adult use only); magnifiers; paper towels
Grouping: Small groups — science table; teacher-led demo
Support: An observe-only role with a magnifier job for any child not tasting, with no attention drawn to the difference.

Social Science — Goal: Learn how apples travel from orchard to table.
Activity: Children will arrange a picture journey — tree, picking, washing, crate, store, snack — and talk about all the helpers whose work brings apples to us.
Materials: Apple journey picture cards; pocket chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Arranging just three cards (tree, pick, eat) for children building sequencing skills.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Count apple seeds and compare two halves.
Activity: Using the teacher-cut apple halves, children will count the seeds in each half with tweezers, record the numbers, and say which half had more seeds.
Materials: Apple halves (teacher-cut); tweezers; counting mats; number cards
Grouping: Small group — math/science table
Support: Dot cards to match against the count, and seed-sized large counters for children who need bigger pieces.

Creative Art — Goal: Print patterns with apple halves.
Activity: Children will dip teacher-cut apple halves into paint and print rows of apples on paper, noticing the star shape the seeds leave. We will make a repeating pattern row together.
Materials: Apple halves (teacher-cut); washable paint trays; paper; smocks
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: A fork handle pressed into the apple by the teacher, giving the child a grip to hold while printing.

Music / Movement — Goal: Sing a counting apple-picking song.
Activity: We will sing a counting song about five apples on a tree, acting out picking one each verse and counting down how many are left, holding up fingers to match.
Materials: Teacher-led song; number cards 5–1
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: Number cards held by children as visual cues for each countdown verse.

Motor Activities — Goal: Pick apples with tongs into baskets.
Activity: Children will use tongs to 'pick' red pom-pom apples from a cardboard tree and carry them to a basket without dropping, working at their own pace.
Materials: Cardboard tree; tongs; red pom-poms; baskets
Grouping: Centers — fine motor table
Support: Easy-squeeze tongs and larger pom-poms for a more successful grip.

Technology — Goal: Watch how apples are harvested in an orchard.
Activity: We will watch a short, teacher-selected clip of an orchard harvest — picking, sorting, and crates — pausing to name the jobs and machines we see.
Materials: Projector; teacher-selected orchard clip
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Front-row seating and a job picture card to watch for during the clip.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Visit a tree and draw how it has changed.
Activity: We will return to the courtyard tree we visited earlier in the theme, look for changes in its leaves, and draw the tree as it looks today in our journals to compare with our first drawing.
Materials: Science journals; crayons; clipboards
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: Our first drawing clipped beside the new page, and a photo option to trace for children who tire of drawing.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Learn that waiting helps good things grow.
Activity: We will talk about how apples take all summer to ripen, like we wait for a turn or for paint to dry. Each child will share one thing that was worth waiting for.
Materials: Focus book (apple-growing pages); sharing cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Picture examples of waiting (turns, growing, baking with family) to help children find an idea.

title: Autumn Days: Animals Get Ready
subject: Science
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Autumn Days' thematic week (September): Animals Get Ready. Focus book: Fletcher and the Falling Leaves — Tiphanie Beeke. Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: Fletcher and the Falling Leaves — Tiphanie Beeke

Language Arts — Goal: Retell how Fletcher tried to help his tree.
Activity: We will read the focus book and sequence Fletcher's actions — worrying, trying to catch leaves, and discovering the tree's winter surprise. Children will share which part they liked best and why.
Materials: Focus book; story sequence cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A three-card sequence (worried, trying, surprised) for children who need a shorter retell.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Discover how squirrels gather and store food for winter.
Activity: Children will play scientist-squirrels: burying large acorn counters in the sand table, then digging to find and count their stores. We will look at photos of real squirrels storing nuts and talk about why they hide them.
Materials: Sand table; large acorn counters; photos of squirrels
Grouping: Small groups — science area
Support: A defined digging spot in the sand and a turn timer for sharing the burying space.

Social Science — Goal: Build homes for animals getting ready for winter.
Activity: Children will build dens and nests with blankets, boxes, and stuffed animals — a cozy burrow for a bear, a nest for a bird — and tell a partner which animal their home is for.
Materials: Blankets; boxes; stuffed animals; cushions
Grouping: Centers/large group — building and dramatic areas
Support: Animal picture cards to choose a role, and teacher help draping heavy blankets.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Compare two piles: which squirrel stored more?
Activity: Children will count two piles of acorn counters, write or stamp the numbers, and decide which pile has more, using the words more and fewer. We will check by pairing the counters one-to-one.
Materials: Acorn counters; number stamps; comparison mat
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: A one-to-one pairing line drawn on the mat, and counting together with a partner.

Creative Art — Goal: Make a torn-paper squirrel collage.
Activity: Children will tear brown and orange paper into small pieces and glue them as fur on a squirrel outline, then add an acorn in its paws. Tearing is the art — pieces can be any size.
Materials: Squirrel outlines; brown/orange paper; glue sticks
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Pre-torn paper pieces and a glue sponge for children still building tearing strength.

Music / Movement — Goal: Sing a sleepy bear song with slow movements.
Activity: We will sing a gentle hibernation song, acting out a bear eating berries, growing sleepy, and curling up in its den, then stretching awake in the spring verse.
Materials: Teacher-led song; mats for 'dens'
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: A defined mat 'den' for each child so curling up feels safe and bounded.

Motor Activities — Goal: Crawl like animals through a den obstacle course.
Activity: Children will move through a course: crawl through the tunnel den, tiptoe across the cushion 'forest floor,' and hop like a rabbit to the burrow hoop at the end.
Materials: Play tunnel; cushions; hoop
Grouping: Small groups — movement area; teacher-supervised
Support: A shorter course with the tunnel propped fully open and an adult at the tunnel exit.

Technology — Goal: Watch real squirrels prepare for winter.
Activity: We will watch a brief, teacher-selected video of squirrels gathering and burying nuts, then compare what the real squirrels did with our sand-table game.
Materials: Projector; teacher-selected squirrel clip
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Pause-and-tell support: the teacher pauses at key moments so children can comment.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Search outdoors for animal homes and food stores.
Activity: On a nature-detective walk, children will look (without touching) for nests, holes, and acorns gathered under trees, checking finds off a picture list with a partner.
Materials: Magnifiers; picture checklist; clipboards
Grouping: Pairs — outdoors; teacher-supervised
Support: A buddy and a picture checklist with just four things to find.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Learn that preparing ahead helps us feel ready.
Activity: We will connect the animals' preparing to our own: we get our cubbies and backpacks ready, too. Each child will share one way they get ready — for school, for bed, or for winter weather.
Materials: Getting-ready picture cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Picture choices (backpack, pajamas, coat) for children who need help finding an example.

Activity: We will walk a story route around the playground, stopping at stations to act out pages of the focus book — over the leaf pile, around the tree, up the hill — finishing back at our classroom door.

Activity: In our gratitude circle, each child will name one autumn gift they are thankful for — crunchy leaves, apples, cooler days, time together — and add a paper leaf to our Thankful Tree display.

Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A sentence frame ('I am thankful for...') and a picture leaf card to place instead of speaking.

Focus book: The Kissing Hand — Audrey Penn

Language Arts — Goal: Listen to a story and talk about how the character felt.
Activity: We will read the focus book slowly, pausing to notice how Chester feels about starting school. Children will share or point to a feeling they have about our classroom, too.
Materials: Focus book; feelings face cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Feelings cards to point to for children not ready to share out loud.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Explore the science corner with magnifiers for the first time.
Activity: Children will visit the science corner, choose shells, pinecones, and stones to examine with magnifiers, and draw one interesting thing they found in a science notebook.
Materials: Magnifiers; shells, pinecones, stones; science notebooks; crayons
Grouping: Small groups — science corner
Support: A partner to explore with and a picture hunt card showing three things to find.

Social Science — Goal: Learn my classmates' names with a rolling-ball game.
Activity: Sitting in a circle, we will roll a ball to a friend and say, 'Hello, my name is...' Each child will hear their name sung back by the class so we begin to know each other.
Materials: Soft ball; name cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A wave and a smile instead of speaking; the teacher says the child's name with them.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Count how many friends are in our class today.
Activity: We will count everyone at circle time, pointing to each child once, then find the matching number card. We will count again after lunch to check whether the number stayed the same.
Materials: Number cards 1–20; pointer
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Counting together with a partner and a number line to follow along.

Creative Art — Goal: Make a handprint keepsake with a heart in the middle.
Activity: Just like the story, children will press a painted handprint onto card stock and place a heart sticker in the palm — one to keep at school and the idea to share at home.
Materials: Washable paint; card stock; heart stickers; wipes
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: A sponge-hand print option for children who dislike paint on their palms.

Music / Movement — Goal: Learn a hello song that uses everyone's name.
Activity: We will sing a hello song verse by verse, adding each child's name while the child waves or stands. By the end of the week everyone will know the tune and many names.
Materials: Teacher-led song; name cards
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: Holding up the child's name card as a cue, so each child knows when their verse comes.

Motor Activities — Goal: Practice carrying a tray with two hands.
Activity: Children will carry a tray with an empty cup along a taped path, walking slowly with two hands, like we will carry our lunch trays. We will practice setting the tray down gently, too.
Materials: Trays; empty cups; taped floor path
Grouping: Small groups — movement area; teacher-supervised
Support: A shorter path and an adult walking alongside for children still building balance.

Technology — Goal: Hear my name in our class welcome recording.
Activity: The teacher has recorded a welcome song naming every child in the class. At the listening center, children will listen and raise a hand or smile when they hear their own name.
Materials: Listening center; teacher-made welcome recording; headphones
Grouping: Centers — pairs; child-led after setup
Support: Volume-limited headphones set by the teacher, and the replay button shown to each child.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Tour the playground and learn its boundaries.
Activity: We will walk the whole playground together, name the equipment, and practice stopping at the boundary cones. Children will learn where we may go and where we stop and wait.
Materials: Playground; boundary cones
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: A buddy to walk with and the option to hold a teacher's hand for the first tour.

Activity: We will talk about how Chester's mother helped him feel brave, meet our calm-down corner, and practice what to do when we miss someone: tell a teacher, hug our class stuffed animal, or look at our handprint heart.
Materials: Calm-down corner; class stuffed animal; feelings chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A picture help card any child can hand to a teacher when words are hard to find.

Language Arts — Goal: Sequence a school day from first to last.
Activity: After reading about Maisy's day, children will order picture cards of a school day — arrive, play, snack, story, go home — and tell the day back using first, next, and last.

Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A three-card sequence to start, with sentence starters ('First we...').

Grouping: Centers — science area; teacher-guided

Support: A pile of just five cards to search, for children who need a smaller set.

Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5

Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: A defined dance spot on the rug and a visual stop sign for children who listen with their eyes.

Grouping: Small groups — bathroom/sink area; teacher-supervised
Support: A step stool to reach comfortably and the picture strip at eye level.

title: Back to School / Routines: Our Day, Step by Step
subject: SEL
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Back to School / Routines' thematic week (September): Our Day, Step by Step. Focus book: The Pigeon HAS to Go to School! — Mo Willems. evidence:
Focus book: The Pigeon HAS to Go to School! — Mo Willems

Language Arts — Goal: Retell a funny story and name the character's school worries.
Activity: We will read the focus book with big voices, then chart the Pigeon's worries on one side and what school is really like on the other. Children will add one thing they actually like about our school.
Materials: Focus book; two-column chart; markers
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Worry/like picture cards to place on the chart instead of thinking of words on the spot.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Make our first class science journal entry about our plant.
Activity: Children will observe our class plant closely — leaves, stem, soil — and draw exactly what they see in a science journal. The teacher will date each page and write one dictated observation.
Materials: Class plant; science journals; crayons
Grouping: Small groups — science table
Support: A photo of the plant to look at while drawing, for children who lose their place.

Social Science — Goal: Read our visual schedule and tell what comes next.
Activity: We will practice using our picture schedule: a helper will move the clothespin to the current activity, and children will answer 'What comes next?' at several points in the day.
Materials: Picture schedule; clothespin marker
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: The schedule-helper job given with a partner, so the steps are shared and supported.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Order the parts of our day and use first, second, third.
Activity: Children will arrange our schedule cards in order on a pocket chart and label the first three with ordinal word cards. We will count how many parts our whole day has.
Materials: Schedule cards; ordinal word cards; pocket chart
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: Ordering just three cards (morning, lunch, home) for children new to sequencing.

Creative Art — Goal: Draw my favorite part of the school day.
Activity: Each child will draw their favorite moment — centers, story, playground — and dictate a caption. The pages will be bound into a class book called 'Our School Day' for the library corner.
Materials: Paper; crayons; book rings
Grouping: Independent/small group — tables
Support: A photo prompt of the centers to look at, and a sentence frame ('I like ___ because...').

Music / Movement — Goal: Learn the transition songs we will use all year.
Activity: We will practice our clean-up song and our line-up song, using them for real transitions between activities today so children connect each song with what their bodies should do.
Materials: Teacher-led songs; visual transition cards
Grouping: Large group — throughout the day
Support: A visual transition card shown before each song ends, so no change is a surprise.

Motor Activities — Goal: Practice pencil grasp by tracing my name.
Activity: Children will trace their names and straight and curvy lines on dry-erase boards, then wipe and try again. The teacher will help with grip and starting at the top.
Materials: Dry-erase boards; name cards; dry-erase markers
Grouping: Centers — writing table; teacher-guided
Support: Triangular grips and larger letter cards for children building grasp and control.

Technology — Goal: Watch a visual timer help us with a transition.
Activity: During clean-up, the teacher will project a visual countdown timer. We will watch the color shrink as we tidy and talk about how the timer helps us know how much time is left.
Materials: Projector; visual timer app
Grouping: Large group — classroom; teacher-led
Support: A seat where the timer is easy to see, and a verbal warning one minute before it ends.

title: Back to School / Routines: Our Classroom Promises

Language Arts — Goal: Sort kind and not-yet choices from a story.

Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Promise picture cards to vote on, for children who cannot yet think of words to suggest.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Graph our favorite center in the classroom.
Activity: Children will look at photos of our centers and place a picture ballot for their favorite. We will build the graph together, count each column, and find the class favorite.

Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Counting each column with a partner, pointing at every ballot.

Creative Art — Goal: Add a handprint border to our promises poster.
Activity: Children will press painted handprints around the border of our promises poster and draw one picture of kind hands in action. The poster will hang by our door all year.
Materials: Promises poster; washable paint; paper; wipes
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: A sponge hand-stamp option for children who dislike paint on their hands.

Music / Movement — Goal: Learn our promise song with motions.
Activity: We will learn a short teacher-created song to a familiar tune — one verse about kind hands, one about listening ears — with a motion for each promise, and sing it at closing circle.

Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: Holding the action card for a verse instead of singing, for children who join by moving.

Motor Activities — Goal: Practice gentle hands with a bubble game.
Activity: Children will move around the rug holding an imaginary bubble around their body, freezing when the music stops without 'popping' anyone else's bubble — learning personal space with our bodies.

Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: A smaller, slower movement group for children who need more room and time.

Technology — Goal: Record our promises in our own voices.
Activity: Small groups will record themselves saying our class promises into the class recorder, echoing the teacher line by line. We will play the recording at closing circle and hear our class speaking together.

Grouping: Small groups — quiet corner; teacher-guided
Support: Echoing in a group recording so no child has to speak alone.

Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: A defined blanket spot and a buddy to sit with during the picnic and game.

Activity: We will revisit our poster, and each child will choose one promise to practice — kind hands, listening ears, walking feet, or kind words. Teachers will notice and name promise-keeping out loud all day.
Materials: Promises poster; promise picture cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: One picture promise card to keep in the cubby as a reminder, chosen with the teacher's help.

title: Bats and Spiders: Meet the Bat

Focus book: Stellaluna — Janell Cannon

Language Arts — Goal: Retell a story's beginning, middle, and end.
Activity: We will read about the baby bat who lands in a birds' nest, pausing to wonder how she feels. Children will retell the beginning, middle, and end with three picture cards.

Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Preferential seating near the book and a feelings card to answer with a point.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Compare bats and birds and name their differences.
Activity: Children will compare bat and bird picture cards — wings, feathers or fur, beaks or teeth — and sort features onto a 'bat / bird' chart, learning a bat is a mammal, not a bird.
Materials: Bat and bird photo cards; sorting chart; magnifiers
Grouping: Small groups — science table; teacher-guided
Support: A photo comparison sheet for children who need help spotting differences.

Social Science — Goal: Identify ways bats help our world.
Activity: We will learn that bats help people by eating mosquitoes and pollinating plants, then make a class list 'Thank You, Bats' and choose a pretend job: fruit bat, bug catcher, or cave sleeper.
Materials: Bat helper picture cards; chart paper
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Choosing a job by pointing to its picture for children less verbal.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Count nighttime animals one-to-one up to 10.
Activity: Children will count plastic bats onto numbered cave mats and line the caves up from 1 to 10, saying which cave holds more bats.
Materials: Plastic bats; numbered cave mats 1–10
Grouping: Small group — math center; teacher-guided
Support: Larger counting pieces and a number strip for children building one-to-one skills.

Creative Art — Goal: Create a night-sky background using sponge painting.
Activity: Children will sponge-paint a deep blue-purple night sky on black paper and add a white chalk moon and sticker stars — our bats' sky.
Materials: Black paper; blue/purple paint; sponges; chalk; star stickers
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Paint in a darkened tray area with a smock and a glitter-glue sponge option for children avoiding drips.

Music / Movement — Goal: Move slowly and gracefully like a bat gliding at night.
Activity: To quiet night music, children will fly slowly around the rug as bats with scarves for wings, swooping low and gliding, and freeze hanging 'asleep' when the music stops.
Materials: Recorded gentle music; scarves
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: A defined movement spot and dimmer energy option (tiptoe mode) for children who get overstimulated.

Motor Activities — Goal: Practice balance walking a narrow line like a branch.
Activity: Children will walk a taped 'branch' line heel-to-toe carrying a stuffed bat, then hang (with feet on the floor leaning back) from the low bar for a 'bat stretch' with teacher help.
Materials: Floor tape line; stuffed bats; low bar/mat
Grouping: Small groups — movement area; teacher-supervised
Support: A low, wide line and a spotter partner for children still developing balance.

Technology — Goal: Match recorded animal sounds to the correct animal.
Activity: At the listening center, children will hear bat and other night-animal sounds on the tablet and match each sound to its animal picture card.
Materials: Tablet with teacher-selected sound clips; animal picture cards; headphones
Grouping: Small group — listening area; teacher-guided
Support: Headphones fitted by the teacher and a bat picture to tap when the sound is heard.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Look for daytime hiding places of night animals.
Activity: On a daytime walk we will look for where night animals rest by day: under eaves, in tree holes, and under bark, noting that bats sleep somewhere safe and dark.
Materials: Clipboards; picture clue cards; playground/trees
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: A buddy to search with and a picture card of the three things to find.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Learn that friends can be different from us and still be friends.
Activity: We will talk about how Stellaluna and the birds are different, yet become friends. Children will name one way they are different from a friend and one way they are the same.
Materials: Focus book; feelings chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Partner talk so children rehearse their answer with one friend first.

Grouping: Large group — carpet/tables
Support: A sentence starter ('The spider uses her web to...') on a card.

Activity: Children will build AB patterns along a paper web line with spider and fly counters (spider-fly-spider-fly), clap their pattern, and have a friend continue it.

Grouping: Centers — math area; child-led after demo

Activity: Children will make web art by dipping yarn in white glue-paint and pressing spiral and spoke lines onto black paper, then add a thumbprint spider.

Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: A web template with pre-drawn spokes for children who want a starting frame.

Music / Movement — Goal: Sing a spider song with coordinated finger actions.
Activity: We will sing a spider song with finger actions — creeping fingers, spinning hands, and a big stretch for the finished web — sung softly, then with bouncing energy.
Materials: Teacher-led song; action picture cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Action picture cards shown ahead of each verse for non-readers following along.

Grouping: Centers — fine motor table; teacher-supervised
Support: Loop scissors and a pre-started snip for children developing cutting skills.

Support: Teacher-held device; children press the shutter with hand support as needed.

Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: A found-web photo card in hand so children know the shape to look for.

Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A picture of a finished web to hold as the goal in mind while working.

Focus book: Bats — Gail Gibbons

Language Arts — Goal: Tell fact from make-believe about bats.

Materials: Focus book; fact/story sorting cards; chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Fact cards with one bold picture each for children overwhelmed by full pages.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Explore how bats use sound and big ears to navigate (echolocation).
Activity: Teacher will play recorded (quiet) bat calls sped down so we can hear them, and children will cover and uncover their ears to notice how big ears help hearing, using paper-cup 'bat ears.'
Materials: Teacher-selected slowed bat-call audio; paper-cup ear cones; speaker
Grouping: Small groups — science table; teacher-led
Support: Sound level kept comfortable; an adult stays close for reassurance.

Social Science — Goal: Learn how bats survive winter: hibernation and migration.
Activity: We will learn some bats sleep all winter (hibernate) and some fly to warmer places (migrate). Groups will sort bat picture cards and choose which winter plan their bat uses.
Materials: Bat picture cards; winter/summer mats
Grouping: Small groups — carpet; teacher-guided
Support: A hibernation/migration choice picture to decide their group's answer.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Compare quantities: more, fewer, equal.
Activity: Children will count groups of bug counters 'eaten' by each bat puppet, compare two bats' catches, and decide which bat ate more and which ate fewer.
Materials: Bat puppets; bug counters; comparing mats
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: A number line and larger pieces for children counting with support.

Creative Art — Goal: Cut a symmetrical shape by folding and cutting.
Activity: Children will fold paper, cut a bat silhouette along a drawn line, unfold to see the matching wings, and hang their bats upside down from our branch.
Materials: Black paper; scissors; drawn cutting lines; string; branch
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5; teacher-supervised cutting
Support: Pre-cut bat silhouettes available for children still building cutting confidence.

Music / Movement — Goal: Echo rhythm patterns like a bat's echo calls.
Activity: We will echo-clap rhythms like bat calls: teacher claps a short pattern, children send it back, in a call-and-echo game that gets longer across rounds.
Materials: Hands/rhythm sticks (optional)
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Visual hand signals with the recorded sounds so no child is startled.

Motor Activities — Goal: Track a moving object and catch with two hands.
Activity: Children will toss and catch a balloon 'moth' keeping it in the air like a bat hunting, counting catches with a partner and trying to beat their own count.
Materials: Balloons; open space
Grouping: Pairs — gym/rug area; teacher-supervised
Support: A plush ball option for children not ready to catch a balloon.

Technology — Goal: Study real animal photographs using zoom.
Activity: We will look at real photographs of bat colonies, bat babies, and a bat house on the classroom screen, zooming in on one photo to study the bat's face and wings.
Materials: Projector/screen; teacher-selected bat photos
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Front seating near the screen with a pause after each photo for processing time.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Map sheltered animal resting spots on the playground.
Activity: On our walk we will notice every dark, sheltered spot — hollow logs, drain covers, under the slide roof — and mark with stickers each place a bat or spider could rest, then report our map.

Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: A two-choice picture card at each stop for children answering nonverbally.

Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: The option to listen quietly without being called on.

Activity: Children will hunt for spiders' homes on our playground — webs, leaf curls, and under-bench corners — and place a small flag near (not on) each find for friends to visit on a spider tour.

Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: An adult-proximity buddy and a clipboard 'job' for children who wander.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Practice kindness and gentleness toward small living things.
Activity: We will talk about being gentle with small creatures: we look with our eyes, we don't squash. Children will practice what to say and do when they find a spider: step back, tell a teacher, watch it work.
Materials: Spider photo; feelings chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A 'show don't squash' picture reminder card to take to the playground.

title: Bats and Spiders: Nighttime Celebration
subject: Science
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Bats and Spiders' thematic week (October): Nighttime Celebration. Focus book: Bat Loves the Night — Nicola Davies. Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: Bat Loves the Night — Nicola Davies

Language Arts — Goal: Sequence the week and dictate a class book in order.
Activity: We will look at photos from our week and put them in order, dictating our class book 'Our Night Animal Week' one page per day, and read the whole book together.
Materials: Week photos (printed); class book paper; markers
Grouping: Large group then small groups — carpet/tables
Support: Photo set limited to three days for an easier sequence choice.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Review the week's science and share conclusions.
Activity: We will review our charts — bats vs. birds, spider parts, float of night words — vote for our favorite investigation, and the teacher will graph our science votes.
Materials: Week charts; graph paper; crayons
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A simple two-box choice card to cast each vote.

Social Science — Goal: Express thanks to animals that help us, in words and pictures.
Activity: Children will make a night-animal thank-you card — drawing a bat eating bugs or a spider guarding the garden — and dictate one thank-you sentence for the card.
Materials: Card paper; crayons; word bank cards
Grouping: Small groups — tables; teacher-guided
Support: A thank-you sentence frame and picture word bank for drawing-first communicators.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Create and read a bar graph of favorite night animals.
Activity: Children will vote for their favorite night animal (bat, spider, owl, moth) with a picture card, build the class graph, and tell which animal got most and fewest.
Materials: Pocket-chart graph; animal picture ballots
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Picture ballots for voting and partner counting to verify the graph.

Creative Art — Goal: Contribute one element to a collaborative night mural.
Activity: Together we will assemble our night mural: sponge-painted sky, cut bats hanging from a branch, yarn webs in the corners, and thumbprint spiders — everyone signs with a star.
Materials: Mural paper; paint; cut shapes; yarn; star stickers
Grouping: Large group in shifts — art area
Support: A defined area on the mural and apron pockets holding their chosen tools.

Music / Movement — Goal: Perform the week's poem and dance as a group.
Activity: We will perform our spider poem and bat gliding dance together one final time, taking a bow as a class of night-animal experts.
Materials: Spider puppet; recorded music; open space
Grouping: Large group; teacher-led
Support: An end-of-line place and the option to hold the poem puppet instead of performing.

Motor Activities — Goal: Complete a night-animal obstacle course combining the week's motor skills.
Activity: Children will complete the night course: fly the scarf path as a bat, walk the web line, toss flies to the web target, and hang 'asleep' (lean-hang) at the finish mat.
Materials: Scarves; tape line; beanbags and web target; mat
Grouping: Small groups — gym/outdoor; teacher-supervised
Support: Stations may be shortened and extra time allowed; no timing pressure.

Technology — Goal: Connect a nature video to facts learned this week.
Activity: We will watch a short teacher-selected clip of bats leaving a cave at dusk and spiders web-building, pausing to call out facts we already know when we see them.
Materials: Projector/screen; teacher-selected clips
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Children who prefer not to watch may hold the 'question card' job.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Teach a partner about night animals' homes outdoors.
Activity: On our final walk, pairs will give a mini-tour: show a friend a spider home we flagged, the big resting tree, and one web, teaching what they learned like real guides.
Materials: Flagged spider homes; playground route
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; pairs
Support: Buddy pairs with one confident guide per pair.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Feel curious and appreciative about creatures we once found scary.
Activity: We will close by sharing one new fact that made bats or spiders less scary and more interesting, and thank the night animals for their jobs in our world.
Materials: Night mural; feelings chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: The option to point to a mural animal instead of speaking.

title: Construction: Building Starts with a Plan
subject: Social Studies
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Construction' thematic week (October): Building Starts with a Plan. Focus book: Building a House — Byron Barton. Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: Building a House — Byron Barton

Language Arts — Goal: Sequence the steps of building a house.
Activity: We will read the focus book and order step cards of a house going up — dig the hole, build the frame, add walls, add the roof, paint. Children will draw the house they would build at the end.
Materials: Focus book; building-step cards; drawing paper; crayons
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Step cards with helper numbers on the back, and sentence starters ('First they...').

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Test which blocks stack best.
Activity: Children will build towers with wooden blocks, foam blocks, and cardboard blocks, and we will record which kind stacked tallest before falling and which felt steadiest. Everyone gets to test all three kinds.
Materials: Wooden, foam, and cardboard blocks; recording sheet
Grouping: Small groups — science/building area
Support: A flat base board to build on and a partner builder for children who need a steadier start.

Social Science — Goal: Identify construction workers and their jobs.
Activity: We will match photo cards of builders to the jobs they do — digging, lifting, measuring, painting — and talk about how a house needs many workers doing different jobs together.
Materials: Worker-and-job photo cards; pocket chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Partner talk before sharing, so every child rehearses a match with a friend first.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Count blocks in a tower and compare two towers.
Activity: Children will build a tower, count its blocks one by one, then build or find a second tower and compare using more, fewer, taller, and shorter.
Materials: Blocks; counting cubes; number cards
Grouping: Small group — math/building center
Support: Lining counting cubes one-to-one beside the tower for children who need a matching guide.

Creative Art — Goal: Draw a blueprint of a building.
Activity: Children will draw a house plan with white crayon on blue 'blueprint' paper — walls, doors, windows, and a roof — just like the drawings real builders follow.
Materials: Blue paper; white crayons; shape stencils
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Shape stencils to trace and chunky crayons for children building drawing control.

Music / Movement — Goal: Sing a building song with tool actions.
Activity: We will sing verses of 'This is the way we...' with building actions — hammer the nails, saw the wood, dig the hole — keeping the beat with our whole bodies.
Materials: Teacher-led song; action picture cards
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: Action cards held up before each verse so children can prepare the movement.

Motor Activities — Goal: Carry foam bricks to build a wall.
Activity: Children will carry foam 'bricks' one at a time along a path and stack them into a class wall, using strong arms and careful stacking until the wall reaches the tape line.
Materials: Foam blocks; taped path; tape line on the wall
Grouping: Small groups — movement area; teacher-supervised
Support: Lighter bricks and a shorter carrying path so every child can add to the wall.

Technology — Goal: Photograph our block buildings before cleanup.
Activity: With the teacher guiding, children will use the class tablet to photograph the buildings they made today, so our work is saved even after the blocks are put away. We will view the gallery together.
Materials: Class tablet (teacher-guided); projector
Grouping: Small groups — building area; teacher-led
Support: The teacher holds the tablet while the child frames and directs each photograph.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Hunt for building shapes on a walk outside.
Activity: On a walk around our school, children will hunt for shapes in real buildings — rectangle windows, a triangle roof, a round vent — and check each shape off a picture list.
Materials: Shape hunt cards; clipboards
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: A buddy to hunt with and a photo card showing exactly which shape to find next.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Learn that good building starts with a plan and patience.
Activity: We will talk about how builders draw a plan before they build, just like we think before we build with blocks. Each child will share one thing they plan to build this week.
Materials: Focus book (blueprint pages); sharing cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Picture choices of buildable things for children who need help thinking of a plan.

title: Construction: Machines That Build
subject: Social Studies
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Construction' thematic week (October): Machines That Build. Focus book: Mighty, Mighty Construction Site — Sherri Duskey Rinker. Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: Mighty, Mighty Construction Site — Sherri Duskey Rinker

Language Arts — Goal: Name construction vehicles and the jobs they do.
Activity: We will read the focus book and match each vehicle card to its job picture — the excavator digs, the crane lifts, the mixer spins. Children will make the machine's sound and movement for each match.
Materials: Focus book; vehicle and job picture cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Vehicle cards to hold and match physically instead of naming from memory.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Explore how ramp height changes how far trucks roll.
Activity: Children will roll toy trucks down ramps at a low height and a high height, marking with tape where each truck stops. We will compare the marks and talk about what made the truck roll farther.
Materials: Ramps; toy trucks; masking tape
Grouping: Small groups — science area
Support: Larger trucks that are easy to grip and a defined rolling lane to keep turns organized.

Social Science — Goal: Learn that big jobs need a whole team.
Activity: Children will each take pieces of a large construction floor puzzle and work together to complete it, noticing that the picture only works when every piece — and every person — joins in.
Materials: Large floor puzzle with a construction scene
Grouping: Small groups — rug; teacher-guided
Support: Edge pieces offered first and a partner to search with, for children new to big puzzles.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Sort toy vehicles by size and count their wheels.
Activity: Children will sort toy vehicles into big and small groups, then count the wheels on several vehicles and match them to number cards, comparing which vehicle has the most wheels.
Materials: Toy construction vehicles; number cards; sorting mats
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: Two sorting groups only, and counting wheels together with a partner.

Creative Art — Goal: Paint roads with vehicle wheels.
Activity: Children will dip toy truck wheels in paint and drive them across large paper to leave tracks, crossing roads, making hills, and noticing the different tread patterns each wheel leaves.
Materials: Toy trucks; washable paint trays; large paper; smocks
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: A shallow paint tray and a truck with a handle for children who need more control.

Music / Movement — Goal: Move like machines to music cues.
Activity: We will move like machines around the rug — dig like an excavator, lift like a crane, roll like a roller — freezing in machine poses when the music stops.
Materials: Recorded music; machine action cards
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: Seated machine movements and a defined space spot for children who need one.

Motor Activities — Goal: Scoop and dump to fill a truck.
Activity: Children will use big scoops to fill dump trucks with shredded-paper 'dirt,' drive them along a short road, and dump the load in the pile zone, again and again.
Materials: Shredded paper bin; large scoops; dump trucks
Grouping: Centers — sensory/building area
Support: Larger scoops and a defined spot at the bin for children who need elbow room.

Technology — Goal: Match recorded machine sounds to vehicle pictures.
Activity: Children will listen to short, teacher-selected sound clips — a beeping truck, a rumbling mixer, a digging excavator — on the tablet and tap the picture of the machine making each sound.
Materials: Tablet with teacher-selected sound clips; vehicle picture board
Grouping: Small group — listening area; teacher-guided
Support: Headphones and a two-picture choice board for children who need fewer options.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Drive trikes on a chalk road with signs.
Activity: Outside, children will ride trikes and push-cars along a chalk road course, stopping at the stop sign and waiting at the crossing before they go, just like real drivers.
Materials: Trikes and push-cars; chalk road; stop and crossing signs
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-supervised
Support: A push-along car option and a shorter course for children not yet pedaling.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Learn that every job on a team matters.
Activity: We will talk about how the construction site needs the digger AND the sweeper, the driver AND the flag holder. Each child will name one classroom job that helps our team and thank a classmate who did it.
Materials: Classroom job chart; thank-you sentence frame
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Job picture cards to choose from, and a thank-you frame ('Thank you for...').

title: Construction: Build It Tall, Build It Strong
subject: Social Studies
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Construction' thematic week (October): Build It Tall, Build It Strong. Focus book: Iggy Peck, Architect — Andrea Beaty. evidence:
Focus book: Iggy Peck, Architect — Andrea Beaty

Language Arts — Goal: Retell how a young builder solves a problem.
Activity: We will read the focus book and chart the surprising materials the builder uses. Children will suggest one material they would build with and tell why, and we will add their ideas to the chart.
Materials: Focus book; chart paper; material picture cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A material picture bank to choose from, for children who need help generating an idea.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Test which tower bases are strongest.
Activity: Children will build towers on a wide base and on a narrow base, then the teacher will turn a fan on low (teacher-controlled) as 'wind.' We will observe which towers stand and talk about why wide bases help.
Materials: Blocks; fan (teacher only); observation sheet
Grouping: Small groups — science/building area; teacher-led demo
Support: Building with a partner and a drawn base template to start from.

Social Science — Goal: Build one class tower together, one piece at a time.
Activity: In a circle, each child will add one block to our shared tower in turn until it falls or reaches our goal line. We will count the blocks together and cheer for careful hands.
Materials: Blocks; goal line tape on the wall; name cards for turn order
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-guided
Support: Magnet tiles as an alternative piece for children who need a more forgiving material, and a name-card turn order so waiting is predictable.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Measure a tower's height with cubes.
Activity: Children will stack cubes beside their tower until the cube stack matches its height, count the cubes, and record the number to compare towers at the math center.
Materials: Cubes; towers; recording sheet
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: A counting strip to line the cubes on, and counting aloud with a partner.

Creative Art — Goal: Make a skyline collage of shape buildings.
Activity: Children will glue rectangle and square buildings onto a skyline strip, add drawn windows and doors, and choose a crayon sky. Every skyline will be different — tall, short, wide, and thin buildings side by side.
Materials: Pre-cut rectangles and squares; glue; skyline strips; crayons
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Pre-cut shapes and a glue sponge for children still building cutting skills.

Music / Movement — Goal: Tap block rhythms along with music.
Activity: Children will tap wooden blocks together to recorded music, following the teacher's conductor cards for loud and soft, fast and slow, and stopping exactly when the stop card appears.
Materials: Wooden blocks (pairs); recorded music; conductor cards
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: Lighter rhythm sticks and large visual conductor cards for clear cues.

Motor Activities — Goal: Screw and unscrew big nuts and bolts.
Activity: Children will match large plastic nuts to bolts by color and screw them together and apart, building the hand strength builders need for real tools.
Materials: Large plastic nuts-and-bolts sets; trays
Grouping: Centers — fine motor table
Support: The largest bolts first, and a hand-over-hand start from the teacher for the twisting motion.

Technology — Goal: Build shadow buildings with light and shapes.
Activity: At the light table, children will arrange translucent shapes to compose a city of buildings and bridges, watching how the light shines through their skyline. The teacher will photograph favorites to display.
Materials: Light table; translucent building shapes
Grouping: Small groups — light area; teacher-guided
Support: Bigger shapes that are easy to place and a turn-taking timer so everyone gets a turn.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Build a class fort and bridge outdoors.
Activity: Outside, small groups will work together to build with big outdoor blocks — a fort for one group, a low bridge for another — carrying pieces as a team and testing the bridge by walking across it carefully with a teacher beside them.
Materials: Big outdoor blocks; low planks; open outdoor space
Grouping: Small groups — outdoors; teacher-supervised
Support: Defined carrying jobs (holder, stacker) and adult proximity at the bridge at all times.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Learn that falling towers teach builders to try again.
Activity: We will talk honestly about how towers fall for every builder, and falling shows us what to change. Each child will share a 'try again' moment, and we will practice saying, 'I'll build it stronger.'
Materials: Feelings chart; try-again sentence card
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Specific praise from the teacher for every retry a child describes or shows.

title: Construction: Roads, Bridges, and Tunnels
subject: Social Studies
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Construction' thematic week (October): Roads, Bridges, and Tunnels. Focus book: Building Bridges — — a simple nonfiction picture book about how bridges help people cross water and valleys (substitute any bridge title on hand). Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: Building Bridges — — a simple nonfiction picture book about how bridges help people cross water and valleys (substitute any bridge title on hand)

Language Arts — Goal: Use position words: over, under, across, and through.
Activity: We will read the focus book, then use a toy car and our block bridge to act out each position word. Children will complete the frame 'The car goes ___ the bridge' with the right word and the action.
Materials: Focus book; toy car; block bridge; position word cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Gesture cues for every position word and picture choices to point to before speaking.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Test how folding makes a paper bridge stronger.
Activity: Children will lay a flat paper bridge between two blocks and count how many toy cars it holds, then try a fan-folded paper bridge (teacher demonstrates the fold). We will compare the counts and feel the difference.
Materials: Paper (flat and fan-folded); blocks; toy cars; counting cubes
Grouping: Small groups — science table; teacher-guided
Support: A pre-folded bridge ready to test, for children who find the folding frustrating.

Social Science — Goal: Connect our block town with roads.
Activity: Children will build houses and buildings, then lay road pieces and tape roads to connect them, talking about who travels the roads — families, buses, firefighters — and why towns need to be connected.
Materials: Blocks; road tape or road pieces; toy people and vehicles
Grouping: Centers — building area; child-led
Support: Toy people figures to act out the traveling, for children who express ideas through play first.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Tally cars crossing our bridge by color.
Activity: As children drive toy cars across the class bridge in turn, we will tally each crossing by car color on a chart. At the end we will count each color's tally marks together.
Materials: Toy cars; tally chart; class bridge
Grouping: Small group — math/building area
Support: Sticker tallies instead of drawn marks, and counting the finished column with a partner.

Creative Art — Goal: Paint a river scene with a bridge.
Activity: Children will paint a blue river across their paper, then draw or glue a bridge over it with roads on both sides, adding a car or boat. We will talk about the bridge's job as we work.
Materials: Paper; blue paint; bridge strips; crayons; glue
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: A pre-painted river sheet and bridge strips to place, for children who want to focus on assembling.

Music / Movement — Goal: Play a gentle bridge traveling game with music.
Activity: Two children will hold raised arms to make a 'bridge' while the line travels under it to a familiar bridge song (teacher-led). When the verse ends, the bridge gently lowers and a new pair becomes the bridge.
Materials: Teacher-led song; open rug space
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: The option to be a bridge holder or a watcher first, and gentle hands reminded before we start.

subject: Social Studies
