Focus book: From Seed to Pumpkin — Wendy Pfeffer

Language Arts — Goal: Sequence the pumpkin life cycle.
Activity: We will read the focus book and order life-cycle cards — seed, sprout, vine, flower, green pumpkin, orange pumpkin. Children will act the cycle out, curling up as seeds and slowly growing into big round pumpkins.
Materials: Focus book; life-cycle picture cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Cards with numbers on the back to check the order, and growing actions modeled by the teacher.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Investigate the seeds and pulp inside a pumpkin.
Activity: The teacher will open a pumpkin (adults cut; children scoop). Children will scoop seeds and pulp into bowls, wash the seeds with the teacher, spread them to dry for later counting, and describe the smell and feel of the inside.
Materials: Pumpkin (teacher-cut); bowls; spoons; water basin; paper towels
Grouping: Small groups — science table; teacher-supervised
Support: A big spoon, gloves if wanted, and an observe-and-describe role for children who dislike the texture.

Social Science — Goal: Learn that growing food takes care and time.
Activity: We will plant seeds in cups today — pumpkin seeds we saved and fast-sprouting beans — and set up a class watering job. Children will learn that our job is to give water and light, then wait and watch.
Materials: Cups; potting soil; pumpkin and bean seeds; watering can; job chart
Grouping: Small groups — science/garden area; teacher-guided
Support: A picture job chart and a watering partner so the daily job is shared and remembered.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Count seeds onto ten-frames in groups of five and ten.
Activity: Using our washed, dried seeds (or large seed counters), children will fill ten-frames one space at a time, count the total, and match it to a number card.
Materials: Dried seeds or large counters; ten-frames; number cards
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: Ten-frames as the guide itself, plus larger counters for children who need bigger pieces to handle.

Creative Art — Goal: Draw two pictures for a life-cycle wheel.
Activity: Children will draw a tiny seed on one section of a wheel and a big orange pumpkin on another; the teacher will assemble the wheels so children can turn them and retell the cycle.
Materials: Wheel templates; crayons; brass fasteners (teacher-assembled)
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Seed and pumpkin stencils to trace for children who want a starting shape.

Music / Movement — Goal: Sing and move a growing song.
Activity: We will sing a teacher-led growing song — starting curled small as seeds, sprouting up through the soil, spreading vines, and opening as flowers — growing a little more with each verse.
Materials: Teacher-led song; open rug space
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: A seated growing option (arms grow instead of bodies) and slow verses first.

Motor Activities — Goal: Transfer seeds with spoons and control.
Activity: Children will spoon dried beans and large seeds between bowls and jars over a tray, practicing a steady hand and stopping to check their grip — the same careful hands farmers use for seeds.
Materials: Spoons; bowls and jars; dried beans and large seeds; trays
Grouping: Centers — fine motor table; teacher-supervised
Support: A bigger scoop and a wider bowl for children who need an easier target.

Technology — Goal: Watch a pumpkin grow in a time-lapse.
Activity: We will watch a short, teacher-selected time-lapse of a pumpkin plant growing from sprout to pumpkin, pausing to name each stage as it appears and compare it with our life-cycle cards.
Materials: Projector; teacher-selected time-lapse clip; life-cycle cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Front-row seating and the teacher pausing at every stage so nobody misses a change.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Measure a garden bed with our steps.
Activity: Outside, we will walk the school garden bed heel-to-toe and count our steps across it, talking about how much room a pumpkin vine needs to sprawl and where the sun shines longest.
Materials: School garden bed; step-count chart
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: A buddy to count steps aloud together, and a shorter side of the bed to measure.

Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Picture choices (pet, plant, sibling, toy) to help children think of something they care for.

Language Arts — Goal: Retell the story of one pumpkin's whole year.
Activity: We will read the focus book and sequence three big story moments — the pumpkin shines, the pumpkin rests in the garden all winter, and new sprouts grow in spring. Children will tell what they think happens next year.
Materials: Focus book; three-part story cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A three-card sequence (shine, rest, grow) and sentence starters for the retell.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Compare pumpkins by size, weight, and skin.
Activity: Children will handle several pumpkins and gourds, order them by size, predict which is heaviest, and check with a balance scale. We will feel the ridges and chart our observations.
Materials: Pumpkins and gourds of different sizes; balance scale; observation chart
Grouping: Small groups — science table; teacher-supervised
Support: Smaller gourds that are easy to hold with two hands, and a partner to heft and compare together.

Social Science — Goal: Run a pretend pumpkin patch.
Activity: In our classroom patch, children will take turns as patch helpers and customers: choosing a pumpkin, carrying it to the stand, weighing it on the toy scale, and exchanging play money.

Grouping: Centers — dramatic play; child-led
Support: Role cards with pictures (helper, customer) and defined jobs so everyone can join the play.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Measure how big around a pumpkin is with string.
Activity: Children will wrap a ribbon around a pumpkin's middle, cut or mark the length with the teacher's help, then compare ribbons on a chart to find the pumpkin that is biggest around.
Materials: Pumpkins; ribbons; comparison chart
Grouping: Small group — math center; teacher-assisted
Support: A partner to hold the pumpkin steady while the child wraps, and pre-cut ribbon for the comparing step.

Creative Art — Goal: Make yarn-wrapped pumpkin art.
Activity: Children will wind orange yarn around and around a pumpkin outline on card, following its round shape, then add a brown stem and a green leaf. Slow, careful winding is the whole job.
Materials: Pumpkin outlines on card; orange yarn (pre-cut lengths); glue; stem and leaf pieces
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Thicker yarn, a larger outline, and a glue sponge to hold the yarn's starting end.

Music / Movement — Goal: Sing a five-little-pumpkins counting rhyme.
Activity: We will sing the traditional five little pumpkins rhyme with five pumpkin props on our 'gate' (a box), counting down as each pumpkin rolls away in the verses, using our fingers to track the numbers.
Materials: Five pumpkin props; box 'gate'; number cards
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: Holding a pumpkin prop and counting along with fingers, for children who join best by doing.

Motor Activities — Goal: Roll pumpkins down a ramp with aim.
Activity: Children will roll soft orange balls down a ramp toward the 'patch' target, adjusting their push — gentle or strong — to land in the patch zone, then fetch and roll again.
Materials: Ramp; soft orange balls; patch target mat
Grouping: Small groups — movement area; teacher-supervised
Support: Lighter balls and a shorter ramp for children building pushing control.

Technology — Goal: Look at a pumpkin's skin and seeds through a microscope.
Activity: With the teacher, small groups will use the digital microscope to examine pumpkin skin and a dried seed up close on the screen, describing the bumps, lines, and patterns they can suddenly see.
Materials: Digital microscope; screen; pumpkin skin piece and seeds
Grouping: Small groups — science table; teacher-led
Support: A turn-taking timer and adult proximity so each child gets an unhurried look.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Carry pumpkins to build an outdoor patch display.
Activity: Outside, children will carry light pumpkins and gourds, one at a time with two hands, along the garden path and arrange them into a class patch display, counting our pumpkins when it is finished.
Materials: Light pumpkins and gourds; garden path; display spot
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-supervised
Support: Carrying the smallest gourd with a buddy walking alongside, for children who need a lighter job.

Activity: We will talk about how the story's pumpkin went back to the garden and fed new plants — nature uses everything again. Each child will share one thing from nature we can reuse or return to the earth.
Materials: Focus book (garden pages); reuse picture cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Picture cards (leaves to soil, seeds to plants, food scraps to compost) to choose and explain.

The teacher will check first for wheat or gluten allergies: any child affected will explore a rice-flour dough instead, or observe — everyone gets the same kneading job with a safe material.
Materials: Flour tray (and rice flour alternative); mixing bowl; water; teacher-prepared dough
Grouping: Small groups — science table; teacher-led demo
Support: An observe-first turn and dough tools (roller, cutter) for children who prefer not to touch with bare hands.

Social Science — Goal: Practice offering help like a good friend.
Activity: We will talk about how the hen asked for help and nobody came, then chart the helping jobs children can do in our classroom. Each child will practice saying 'I can help' and choose one helping job for today.
Materials: Helping job picture cards; chart paper
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A sentence frame card ('I can help with...') and picture choices for the job.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Count eggs into nests to match number cards.
Activity: Children will draw a number card and place exactly that many plastic egg counters into a nest bowl, counting aloud as they place each egg, then check by recounting.
Materials: Plastic egg counters; nest bowls; number cards 1–10
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: Larger egg counters and a number line strip to follow while counting.

Creative Art — Goal: Make a handprint hen with a torn-paper wheat field.
Activity: Children will print a painted handprint (fingers as tail feathers) to make a hen, add a drawn beak and eye, and glue torn yellow paper strips below as the wheat field she worked in.
Materials: Washable red/brown paint; paper; yellow paper strips; glue; wipes
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: A sponge-stamp hen shape option and pre-torn wheat strips for children who need them.

Music / Movement — Goal: Sing a farm-helpers song in the story's order.
Activity: We will sing verses of a helpers' song in the hen's job order — planting, watering, cutting, carrying — with a big action for each job, remembering the sequence from the story.
Materials: Teacher-led song; job action cards
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: Job action cards held in order by children at the front, as a visual sequence for everyone.

Motor Activities — Goal: Carry eggs on spoons to the hen house.
Activity: Children will carry a plastic egg on a spoon along a walking path to the hen house box, going slowly and steadily. If an egg falls, we just pick it up and keep going — practice, not a race.
Materials: Spoons; plastic eggs; taped path; hen house box
Grouping: Small groups — movement area; teacher-supervised
Support: A larger spoon with a rim, a shorter path, and the option to carry the egg in two cupped hands.

Technology — Goal: Record our class retelling with sound effects.
Activity: In small groups, children will record our retelling of the tale into the class recorder — narrating a page each and adding animal sound effects. We will listen to the finished story at closing circle.
Materials: Voice recorder or tablet with recording app; focus book
Grouping: Small groups — quiet corner; teacher-guided
Support: Joining the group refrain and animal sounds, so no child has to narrate alone.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Do pretend farm chores in an outdoor circuit.
Activity: Outside, children will rotate through chore stations: carry a half-full cup of water to 'water the plants' (pouring onto the garden), sweep the patio 'barn' with child brooms, and deliver an egg basket to the coop corner.
Materials: Water cups; garden; child brooms; egg baskets
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-supervised
Support: Lighter water cups and a clearly defined single chore for children who need a simpler circuit.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Learn that helping earns a share in good results.
Activity: We will talk kindly about the story's ending — the hen teaches us that helping matters — and each child will name one way they will help today. Teachers will notice and name helpers out loud all afternoon.
Materials: Focus book; helping promise cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Helping-choice picture cards to pick a doable promise, chosen with the teacher.

title: Farmers and Pumpkins: Harvest Celebration
subject: Social Studies
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Farmers and Pumpkins' thematic week (October): Harvest Celebration. Focus book: Pumpkin Soup — Helen Cooper. Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: Pumpkin Soup — Helen Cooper

Language Arts — Goal: Retell how friends cook together and solve a problem.
Activity: We will read the focus book and sequence the soup-making steps, then talk about the friends' problem — everyone wanted a turn — and how they made it right. Children will share a time they took turns with a friend.
Materials: Focus book; soup-step picture cards; feelings cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Step cards and feelings cards to show the story instead of only telling it.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Plant our saved seeds in clear cups and predict growth.
Activity: Children will revisit the pumpkin seeds we washed on Day 2, plant a few in clear cups against the side so roots will show, water them, and draw a prediction of what will grow first.
Materials: Clear cups; potting soil; saved pumpkin seeds; prediction sheets
Grouping: Small groups — science table
Support: Pre-moistened soil and the largest seeds, with a partner helping to hold the cup.

Social Science — Goal: Run a pretend harvest soup kitchen.
Activity: In dramatic play, children will take every role in our soup kitchen — washing vegetables (play), chopping with toy knives, stirring the big pot, and serving bowls to friends with a thank-you. Pretend only; no real food is used.
Materials: Play vegetables; toy pot and ladles; bowls; role cards
Grouping: Centers — dramatic play; child-led
Support: Role picture cards (washer, stirrer, server) so every child can find and keep a job.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Graph our favorite pumpkin-week activity.
Activity: Children will vote with picture ballots for their favorite activity — the patch, seed counting, pumpkin art, or the soup story. We will graph the votes, count each column, and announce the result together.
Materials: Picture ballots; pocket-chart graph
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Counting each column with a partner, pointing to every ballot as it is counted.

Creative Art — Goal: Assemble our harvest mural from the week's work.
Activity: Children will arrange their pumpkins, hens, and field art from across the week onto a big field mural, add drawn details — a sun, a fence, the patch rows — and sign their section.
Materials: Week's art pieces; large mural paper; glue; crayons
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: A defined space on the mural and glue help from the teacher for heavy pieces.

Music / Movement — Goal: Perform our farm songs for an audience.
Activity: We will perform the farmer's morning song and the growing song — with all our actions — for another class or record them for families, standing tall and bowing at the end.
Materials: Action cards; open space; voice recorder (optional)
Grouping: Large group; teacher-led
Support: Holding a farm prop and joining only the movements for children who prefer not to sing.

Motor Activities — Goal: Complete the harvest obstacle course.
Activity: Children will move through our harvest course: crawl through the 'vine tunnel,' carry a soft pumpkin across the patch, and scoop seeds into a jar at the finish — one station at a time.
Materials: Play tunnel; soft pumpkins; scoops and seeds; jar
Grouping: Small groups — gym/movement area; teacher-supervised
Support: A shortened course with the tunnel fully open and extra time at every station.

Technology — Goal: Watch our farm week slideshow and celebrate learning.
Activity: The teacher will project the photos from our week — gardens, pumpkins, hens, and our patch — and children will name something farmers or pumpkins taught us as each photo appears.
Materials: Projector; week photos
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: The pointer job for a child who focuses best with a role, and front-row seating.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Take a harvest walk and water our garden plants.
Activity: We will walk to the school garden with small watering cans, check how the garden looks since Day 1, water the plants carefully, and look for any changes in the bed we measured.
Materials: Small watering cans; school garden
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: A buddy to walk with and a lighter, half-filled watering can.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Feel grateful for food, farmers, and friends.
Activity: In our closing gratitude circle, we will pass a small pumpkin hand to hand; whoever holds it names one food, farmer job, or friend they are thankful for. Every child will get a turn to hold the pumpkin.
Materials: Small pumpkin; gratitude sentence frame
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A pass-and-point option: hold the pumpkin and point to a picture instead of speaking.

evidence:

Language Arts — Goal: Retell a story in order using first, next, and last.
Activity: We will read the focus book at circle time, pausing to name each thing the firefighters do. Children will sequence three picture cards (alarm rings, truck drives, firefighters help) and retell the story to a partner.
Materials: Focus book; sequence picture cards; chart paper
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Preferential seating near the teacher for children who need support focusing; sentence-starter cards ('First... next... last...') available.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Observe and describe how materials change with heat (teacher demonstration only).
Activity: Teacher will safely demonstrate how warm air makes a paper spiral spin above a lamp (no flame). Children will observe, predict what will happen, and describe what they see using new words: warm, rise, spin.
Materials: Paper spirals; string; desk lamp; observation sheet
Grouping: Small groups — science table; teacher-led demo
Support: Extra wait time before answering so every child can form a prediction; magnifiers offered for a closer look.

Social Science — Goal: Identify community helpers and the jobs they do.
Activity: We will sort picture cards into 'firefighter jobs' and 'not firefighter jobs' and talk about how firefighters help our neighborhood. Children will share one way a helper has helped their family.
Materials: Community helper picture cards; pocket chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Partner talk before whole-group sharing, so quieter children rehearse their idea first.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Count objects one-to-one up to 10 and compare more and fewer.
Activity: Children will count toy fire trucks onto numbered garage mats and say which garage has more trucks. We will finish by lining the trucks up in order from 1 to 10.
Materials: Toy fire trucks; numbered garage mats 1–10
Grouping: Small group — math center; teacher-guided
Support: Larger counters and a number line strip for children who need a visual anchor while counting.

Creative Art — Goal: Explore color mixing to make new colors.
Activity: Children will finger-paint with red and yellow to discover orange — our 'fire colors' picture. We will talk about what happened where the colors met.
Materials: Red and yellow finger paint; finger-paint paper; smocks; wipes
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5; process-focused
Support: Chunky-handled brushes and a paint-in-a-bag option for children who avoid messy textures.

Music / Movement — Goal: Move in different ways — fast, slow, freeze — in response to music cues.
Activity: We will play a fire-truck freeze dance: children 'drive' around the rug while siren music plays and freeze with hands up when it stops.
Materials: Recorded siren/instrumental music; open rug space
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: A defined personal space spot on the rug for children who need a clear movement boundary.

Motor Activities — Goal: Strengthen hand muscles by squeezing and aiming a spray bottle.
Activity: Children will 'put out fires' by spraying water at chalk flames drawn on the easel board until the flames wash away.
Materials: Spray bottles; chalk; outdoor easel board; water
Grouping: Small groups — outdoor/art area; teacher-supervised
Support: Two-hand squeeze bottles and a shorter spraying distance for children building hand strength.

Technology — Goal: Use a listening center to follow a story independently.
Activity: At the listening center, children will follow along with a recorded fire-safety story, turning pages at the chime and pointing to each helper's tool as it is named.
Materials: Listening center; recorded story + picture book copies; headphones
Grouping: Centers — pairs; child-led after setup
Support: Volume-limited headphones adjusted by the teacher; a page-number bookmark for children who lose their place.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Practice moving quickly and calmly along a planned route.
Activity: We will walk our fire-drill route together — out the door, along the path, to our meeting tree — practicing quiet voices and staying with the group, then time how smoothly we did it.
Materials: Class route; meeting-point sign; whistle (teacher only)
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: An adult hand or buddy partner for children who need support staying with the group.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Understand that being safe is a way we care for ourselves and others.
Activity: We will read a short story moment about a child who remembers the safety rule when the alarm sounds, and talk about how following rules keeps everyone safe — it is a kindness to the whole class.
Materials: Focus book (reread a favorite page); feelings chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Specific praise for children who share a rule in their own words.

evidence:
Focus book: Stop, Drop, and Roll — — a picture book that teaches the stop, drop, and roll routine (substitute any fire-safety title on hand)

Language Arts — Goal: Learn new vocabulary and use it in a sentence: alarm, exit, meeting place.
Activity: After reading, we will add three new words to our word wall with pictures. Children will use one word in a sentence about our classroom safety plan.
Materials: Focus book; word cards with pictures; word wall
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Picture-supported word cards and a chance to point-and-name instead of speaking for emerging talkers.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Sort materials by property: what is safe to touch and what is not.
Activity: Children will sort real classroom objects and picture cards into 'safe to touch' and 'ask a grown-up first' trays, explaining their thinking for tricky items like a cold stove picture.
Materials: Sorting trays; object and picture card set
Grouping: Small groups — science table
Support: Fewer items per round (start with 4) for children who are still building sorting stamina.

Social Science — Goal: Practice a safety routine as a team.
Activity: On the rug we will practice stop, drop, and roll with a soft mat, one small group at a time, while classmates cheer the steps in order: stop — drop — roll, roll, roll.
Materials: Gym mat; step picture cards
Grouping: Large group then small groups — rug; teacher-led
Support: A visual step strip at the mat and the option to demonstrate with a stuffed animal first.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Recognize and extend AB patterns.
Activity: Children will build patterns with red and yellow unifix 'flames' (red-yellow-red-yellow) and clap the pattern, then challenge a friend to continue theirs.
Materials: Red and yellow unifix cubes; pattern strips
Grouping: Centers — math area; child-led after demo
Support: Completed example strips to copy for children new to patterning; extra cubes for an extension challenge (ABC patterns).

Creative Art — Goal: Use collage to represent an idea.
Activity: Children will tear red, orange, and yellow tissue paper and glue the pieces onto a flame outline, overlapping colors to show how flames flicker and change.
Materials: Tissue paper; flame outlines; glue sticks; trays
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Pre-torn tissue pieces and a glue sponge for children still building tearing and squeezing strength.

Music / Movement — Goal: Sing a simple safety song with actions.
Activity: We will learn a call-and-response song about calling for help and moving to our meeting place, adding hand motions for each line and singing it fast, then slow.
Materials: Teacher-led song; action picture cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Action cards held up as cues for children who need a visual reminder of the next motion.

Motor Activities — Goal: Develop balance and body control on a low beam path.
Activity: Children will walk a taped 'escape path' on the floor — heel-to-toe along the line, around the cone 'door,' and to the meeting-place hoop — staying low under a streamer 'smoke line.'
Materials: Floor tape path; cones; hula hoop; crepe-paper streamer
Grouping: Small groups — movement area; teacher-supervised
Support: A wider tape path and a partner's hand for children still developing balance.

Technology — Goal: Take and view photos to document learning.
Activity: With the teacher, small groups will use the class tablet to photograph our safety signs around the room (exit sign, meeting-place poster), then we will view the photos together and name each sign.

Grouping: Small groups; teacher-led
Support: Teacher holds the tablet while children direct the shot, for children still learning to handle devices carefully.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Identify our outdoor meeting place and how to get there.
Activity: Outside, children will find our meeting tree, stand in our line-up spots, and play a gentle game of 'walk to the tree' from different starting points on the playground.

Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: Buddy pairs so no child walks the route alone.

Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A feelings card to point to for children who find it hard to say how they feel.

Grouping: Large group then independent — carpet/tables
Support: Word bank cards with tool names and pictures for children labeling their drawings.

Grouping: Centers — science area; child-led
Support: A smaller pouring cup and a defined turn-taking timer for children working on sharing equipment.

Activity: In dramatic play, children will run our classroom fire station: one answers the 'phone,' others dress up, drive the 'truck,' and roll out the hose to help a stuffed animal in trouble.
Materials: Dress-up gear (helmets, jackets); play phone; hose (rope); stuffed animals
Grouping: Centers — dramatic play; child-led
Support: Role cards with pictures so every child can choose and keep a job; teacher joins briefly to model a new role.

Activity: Children will measure our toy fire truck and a paper 'ladder' using unifix cubes, record how many cubes long each is, and compare which is longer.
Materials: Toy fire truck; paper ladder; unifix cubes; recording sheet
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: A pre-drawn cube outline strip for children who need a guide to line units up without gaps.

Creative Art — Goal: Print with found objects to create texture.
Activity: Children will dip toy truck wheels in paint and drive them across paper to make tracks, noticing the patterns different wheels leave.
Materials: Toy trucks; washable paint trays; large paper; smocks
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: A shallow paint tray and a truck with a handle grip for children who need more control.

Music / Movement — Goal: Keep a steady beat with rhythm instruments.
Activity: We will play shakers and drums along to a marching fire-truck song, following the teacher's start/stop signals and trying a loud verse and a quiet verse.

Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: Instruments with handles and a visual start/stop sign for children who need cues.

Motor Activities — Goal: Build arm and core strength through pulling and carrying.
Activity: Children will pull a wagon 'hose cart' along a path, then carry soft 'water buckets' (beanbags) to fill the pretend truck tank without spilling.

Grouping: Small groups — gym/outdoor area; teacher-supervised
Support: A shorter path and lighter beanbags so every child can complete the course successfully.

Technology — Goal: Explore recorded sounds and match them to their sources.
Activity: Children will listen to short recorded sounds (siren, alarm bell, truck engine, water spray) on the tablet and tap the matching picture on our sound board.
Materials: Tablet with teacher-selected sound clips; picture board
Grouping: Small group — listening area; teacher-guided
Support: Headphones and a two-choice board for children who need fewer options at once.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Observe our school building from outside and find safety features.
Activity: On a walk around the school, children will spot and count exit doors, look for the fire hydrant near our building, and sketch one safety feature in their nature journals.
Materials: Clipboards; nature journals; crayons
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led

title: Fire Safety: Stay Safe at Home
subject: Social Studies
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Fire Safety' thematic week (October): Stay Safe at Home. Focus book: No Dragons for Tea — Jean E. Pendziwol. evidence:
Focus book: No Dragons for Tea — Jean E. Pendziwol

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Investigate which objects float and sink in water.

Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: One-attribute sorting only, with the rule card shown, for children building classification skills.

Creative Art — Goal: Draw and label a plan of a familiar place.
Activity: Children will draw a simple map of our classroom showing the door and our path out, adding a star at the meeting place — our first map-making.

Grouping: Independent/small group — tables
Support: A pre-drawn classroom outline for children to mark the route on instead of drawing the whole room.

Music / Movement — Goal: Respond to a signal quickly and safely.
Activity: We will play 'Alarm and Go': children move to music, and when the (gentle) alarm sound plays, everyone walks calmly to the meeting-place mat and sits — practicing without rushing or pushing.

Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led

Motor Activities — Goal: Strengthen pincer grasp with tongs and small objects.
Activity: Children will use tongs to move red and yellow pom-pom 'flames' into buckets of 'water' (blue paper), racing only against their own last try.

Grouping: Centers — fine motor table
Support: Spring-loaded easy-squeeze tongs and larger pom-poms for children developing grip strength.

Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Picture rule cards to choose from for children who can't yet think of one to say.

Language Arts — Goal: Sequence a story's events using first, next, and last.
Activity: We will read the focus book and follow the seed's journey on the wind. Children will place three journey cards in order (seed travels, seed lands, flower grows) and retell the trip to a partner.

Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Sentence-starter cards ('First... next... last...') and preferential seating near the book.

Activity: We will look at photos of gardeners and farmers planting rows of seeds and talk about the jobs planting takes. Children will share something they have seen growing in a yard or park.
Materials: Gardener and farmer photo cards; chart paper
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Partner talk first so every child rehearses an idea before sharing aloud.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Count seeds one-to-one up to 10.
Activity: Children will count sunflower seeds onto numbered leaf mats, checking each mat by touching and moving seeds one at a time. We will find which leaf has the most seeds.
Materials: Sunflower seeds; leaf number mats 1–10
Grouping: Small group — math center; teacher-guided
Support: A ten-frame strip to line seeds up on for children who need a counting anchor.

Creative Art — Goal: Create a picture using seeds as a collage material.
Activity: Children will glue different seeds inside a big seed outline to make a seed mosaic, choosing colors and textures and noticing how each seed feels as they place it.
Materials: Seed outline paper; assorted dry seeds; glue; trays
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5; process-focused
Support: Glue sponge and a smaller outline for children building gluing stamina.

Music / Movement — Goal: Move like a growing plant through a sequence of shapes.
Activity: To slow music, children will curl up small as seeds, push up as sprouts, stretch tall as stems, and open their arms as flowers. We will freeze at each stage when the music pauses.
Materials: Recorded gentle instrumental music; open rug space
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: A carpet square marking personal space for children who need a clear spot.

Motor Activities — Goal: Strengthen finger muscles picking up small objects with tweezers.
Activity: Children will use tweezers to move pumpkin seeds from a 'garden bed' tray into tiny pots, filling each pot and counting how many they moved.
Materials: Tweezers; pumpkin seeds; mini pots; trays
Grouping: Centers — fine motor table; child-led after demo
Support: Easy-squeeze tweezers and bigger seeds for children still building grip strength.

Technology — Goal: Use a digital microscope to see details the eye cannot.
Activity: With the teacher, children will place a bean seed under the digital microscope and describe the magnified skin, spots, and sprout bump on the screen.
Materials: Digital microscope; screen/tablet; bean seeds
Grouping: Small groups — science area; teacher-led
Support: Adult proximity and a turn card so waiting children know when their turn comes.

Activity: On a seed walk, children will hunt for seeds outside — acorns, maple helicopters, pinecones, and seed heads — and collect three kinds in their nature bags to bring back and compare.

Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: A picture hunt card showing the three seed types for children who need a visual target.

Activity: We will revisit the tiny seed's long journey and talk about how being small does not mean being unimportant. Each child will name one thing they are learning to do that will grow with practice.
Materials: Focus book; feelings chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Specific praise naming each child's idea so contributions are noticed.

Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Choice of drawing or telling their caring idea.

title: Seeds, Acorns and Tree Study: Trees Through the Seasons
subject: Science
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Seeds, Acorns and Tree Study' thematic week (October): Trees Through the Seasons. Focus book: Tell Me, Tree: All About Trees for Kids — Gail Gibbons. evidence:
Focus book: Tell Me, Tree: All About Trees for Kids — Gail Gibbons

Language Arts — Goal: Use describing words for how trees change across seasons.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Measure tree parts with nonstandard units.
Activity: Children will measure a branch, a leaf, and our classroom plant using unifix cubes and record 'how many cubes long' on a measuring sheet.

Grouping: Small group — math center

Activity: Children will paint a trunk with brown, then choose their season's colors for the leaf canopy — pink blossoms, summer green, fall orange, or bare branches with snow dots.

Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Chunky brushes and a season color palette card for children deciding colors.

Music / Movement — Goal: Use the whole body to show a tree in wind and seasons.
Activity: Children will sway as trees in a gentle breeze, shiver off 'leaves' in fall shakes, stand still and bare in winter, and bloom open in spring, following the narrated story.

Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led

Motor Activities — Goal: Develop balance walking a winding 'root path.'
Activity: Children will walk a curvy taped path like tree roots spreading out, heel-to-toe, then carry a leaf card to the 'canopy' hoop at the end without dropping it.
Materials: Floor tape path; leaf cards; hoop
Grouping: Small groups — movement area; teacher-supervised
Support: A wider path and a partner's hand for children still building balance.

Technology — Goal: View time-lapse video to see slow growth speeded up.
Activity: We will watch a short teacher-selected time-lapse of a seed sprouting and a tree budding, pausing to notice changes that real trees take weeks to make.

Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led

Activity: We will sit (indoors) after our tree visit and each share one thing a tree gives us that we are glad for, building a thankful chain of paper leaves for the door.
Materials: Paper leaves; markers; string
Grouping: Large group — carpet/tables
Support: Sentence frame ('I am glad trees give us...') for children starting their thought.

Grouping: Large group in shifts — art area

Grouping: Large group; teacher-led

Motor Activities — Goal: Complete a growing-garden obstacle path using the week's skills.

Grouping: Small groups — gym/outdoor; teacher-supervised

Technology — Goal: Record our voices telling the seed story.
Activity: Using the voice recorder with the teacher, each child will record one line of our class seed story. We will listen to the whole story together and hear our own voices as narrators.

Grouping: Small groups; teacher-led
Support: The option to record with a partner's voice alongside for shy speakers.

Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: The option to show their seed cup instead of speaking.

Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A talking leaf passed hand to hand so turns are visible and fair.

Activity: Children will count paper leaves for our gratitude tree, bundle them in groups of five, and tell how many leaves our tree needs to look full.

Grouping: Small groups — tables; teacher-guided
Support: A counting strip to place each leaf on as it is counted.

Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: A sentence strip with the starter printed so children focus on their idea.

Music / Movement — Goal: Sing a gratitude song with coordinated hand motions.
Activity: We will learn a simple gratitude action song — hands to heart for thankful, reach wide for family, point to the sky for sunshine — and sing it twice, slow and joyful.
Materials: Teacher-led song; motion cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Picture motion cards shown before the song begins.

Grouping: Centers — fine motor table; teacher-supervised
Support: Adaptive crayons with chunky grips for comfortable control.

Support: Headphones set by the teacher and a one-page tracker for keeping place.

Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A pointer card to indicate their choice on the feelings chart if speaking is hard.

title: Senses: All Five Senses
subject: Science
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Senses' thematic week (November): All Five Senses. Focus book: My Five Senses — Aliki. Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: My Five Senses — Aliki

Language Arts — Goal: Learn the names and jobs of the five senses.
Activity: We will read the focus book and build our five-senses word wall: seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting (we will learn about it safely — no surprise tastes), and touching, each with a picture clue.
Materials: Focus book; word/picture cards; chart paper
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Picture-supported word cards matched to real objects before reading the words.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Identify objects by touch and describe textures accurately.
Activity: Children will reach into mystery feely boxes and describe objects by touch alone — smooth, rough, soft, bumpy — then check by looking, amazed at what their fingers knew.
Materials: Feely boxes; familiar objects; texture word cards
Grouping: Small groups — science table; teacher-guided
Support: A prediction picture card to guess before each reveal.

Social Science — Goal: Use observation to notice how friends are feeling.
Activity: We will practice using senses to read friends: looking at faces, hearing voices, and noticing when a friend seems sad or excited, then choosing a kind response.
Materials: Emotion photo cards; mirror
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Extra turns in a smaller group for children who need more processing time.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Sort objects by the sense used to explore them.
Activity: Children will sort picture cards (drum, lemon, sandpaper, rose, bell) under the sense that detects each one, justifying tricky cards like ice cream, which uses several senses.
Materials: Sense sorting mats; picture cards
Grouping: Small group — math/science area; teacher-guided
Support: A sorting mat with sense picture icons in each section.

Creative Art — Goal: Represent the five senses in a collage face.
Activity: Children will build a five-senses collage face: magazine eyes, yarn hair to touch, a tissue nose, and textured paper ears and mouth, naming the sense each part gives us.
Materials: Face outline paper; magazine pictures; yarn; tissues; texture papers; glue
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Glue sponge and pre-torn paper pieces for children building gluing stamina.

Music / Movement — Goal: Respond to sound cues by moving or stilling the body.
Activity: We will play a senses movement game: 'If you hear the drum, march; when it stops, cover your ears and listen for the bell' — alternating loud actions and quiet listening.
Materials: Hand drum; bell; open space
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: Picture cue cards held up before each new instruction.

Motor Activities — Goal: Use touch and two-hand coordination to string beads.
Activity: Children will string big beads to make a 'senses bracelet,' feeling each bead's texture — smooth, bumpy, soft — and choosing their favorites by touch without looking.
Materials: Large textured beads; laces; tray
Grouping: Centers — fine motor table
Support: Larger beads and a stiffened lace tip for children learning to thread.

Technology — Goal: Match recorded everyday sounds to their sources.
Activity: At the listening center, children will listen to a sound-story — rain, birds, a door, a dog — and point to the matching sound-maker picture as each sound arrives.
Materials: Listening center; sound-story recording; picture board
Grouping: Centers — pairs; child-led after setup
Support: Volume-limited headphones and a partner to share first impressions with.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Use four senses to explore the outdoors systematically.
Activity: On a senses walk, children will collect one thing for each sense on their hunt card: something to see (color), hear (shake a seed pod), smell (herb leaf), and touch (bark) — nothing goes in mouths outdoors.
Materials: Senses hunt cards; nature bags; clipboards
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: A two-item starter list for children who find open-ended hunts overwhelming.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Understand that our senses help keep us safe.
Activity: We will talk about how our senses keep us safe — smoke smells, alarms sound, hot stoves feel hot — and each child will name one way a sense protected them.
Materials: Focus book; feelings chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A feelings card option for children answering by pointing.

Activity: We will graph our class's eye colors, noticing the many shades of brown, blue, green, and hazel, and talk about how eyes can be different while working the same way.

Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A choice of eye-color cards to hold up instead of answering aloud.

Activity: Children will build a color pattern train of bears (red, blue, red, blue) following our story order, then make their own two-color pattern for a friend to extend.

Grouping: Centers — math area; child-led after demo
Support: A color line strip to match bears against for support.

Creative Art — Goal: Mix and match a chosen color on purpose.
Activity: Children will choose one story animal and draw it in its book color, then mix paints to try to match that exact color, testing dabs on a swatch strip.

Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Chunky crayons and a pre-drawn animal outline option.

Music / Movement — Goal: Listen for a color word and locate it visually in the room.

Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: A picture sequence strip showing the song's order of colors.

Grouping: Small groups — movement area; teacher-supervised
Support: Wider tape lines and a wall within reach for balance support.

Grouping: Small groups; teacher-led
Support: Teacher-held tablet; children direct which photo to zoom.

Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; pairs

Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: An unbreakable mirror and a teacher-held option for children shy about mirrors.

title: Senses: Hearing and Listening
subject: Science
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Senses' thematic week (November): Hearing and Listening. Focus book: The Listening Walk — Paul Showers. evidence:
Focus book: The Listening Walk — Paul Showers

Language Arts — Goal: Learn sound words (onomatopoeia) and use them expressively.
Activity: We will read about a quiet listening walk and its wonderful onomatopoeia words. Children will choose a sound word (tap, swish, hum) and act its sound for the class to guess.
Materials: Focus book; sound word cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Sound picture cards to sequence for children building oral language.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Compare how different materials carry sound.
Activity: Children will test which materials make sounds louder or softer — tapping a wooden block, a metal lid, a foam pad — and sort them by volume on our loud/soft chart.
Materials: Blocks; lids; foam pads; drumsticks; loud/soft chart
Grouping: Small groups — science table
Support: A two-choice test format (loud/soft) for children new to comparing.

Social Science — Goal: Hear and practice greetings in more than one language.
Activity: We will hear 'hello' in several languages spoken by families in our school community, practice saying two of them, and learn that ears let us welcome everyone.
Materials: Greeting word cards with pictures; world map
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Picture choices for greetings in different languages to select from.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Tally sounds heard in a set time and compare totals.
Activity: During a quiet minute indoors, children will tally every distinct sound they hear (clock, footsteps, birds outside) and compare tallies — why did we hear different numbers?
Materials: Tally sheets; pencils; timer
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A counting frame to tap once per sound heard.

Creative Art — Goal: Represent sounds as drawn lines and marks.
Activity: With eyes closed for one minute of listening, children will then draw the sounds they heard — wavy lines for water, dots for drips, zigzags for a zipper — inventing marks for noises.
Materials: Paper; crayons; quiet timers
Grouping: Small groups — tables; teacher-guided
Support: A listening-drawing template with three boxes for three sounds.

Music / Movement — Goal: Follow visual conducting to build and calm a body-percussion storm.
Activity: We will build a class rain storm with our bodies: finger taps (drizzle), palm rubs (wind), hand claps (rain), thigh pats (thunder), then calm back down in reverse — following the teacher's hands, not words.
Materials: (Body percussion — no materials)
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A front spot near the teacher to watch lips and gestures.

Motor Activities — Goal: Control body movements in response to auditory signals.
Activity: Children will follow a listening obstacle path: when they hear one drum tap they hop, two taps they tiptoe, and the bell means freeze — ears leading the whole way.
Materials: Drum; bell; floor path markers
Grouping: Small groups — movement area; teacher-supervised
Support: Partner echoes beside the child for confidence in the movement sequence.

Technology — Goal: Record, play back, and identify sounds we made ourselves.
Activity: Using the voice recorder, children will record their own sound-word imitations, play them back, and guess each other's recorded sounds as a class game.
Materials: Voice recorder/tablet; sound word cards
Grouping: Small groups; teacher-led
Support: Headphones fitted by the teacher; child controls pause with support.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Practice silent listening outdoors and map the sounds heard.
Activity: We will take silent listening posts outdoors: sit for one full minute with eyes closed, then draw or name every sound — near and far, nature and people — on our sound maps.
Materials: Sound-map papers; crayons; sit spots
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: A buddy and a shorter listening post rotation for children with hearing or attention needs.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Learn that listening carefully is a way to show friends they matter.
Activity: We will practice being listeners for friends: bodies still, eyes watching, mouths quiet, hearts caring — then try it in pairs, each telling about their morning while the other truly listens.
Materials: Listening stone; feelings chart
Grouping: Large group then pairs — carpet
Support: A small 'listening stone' to hold as a turn-to-talk reminder.

Grouping: Large group then pairs — carpet

Activity: Children will match loose texture squares (sandpaper, velvet, foil, cotton, burlap) to identical squares on a board, then sort all squares from roughest to smoothest.
Materials: Texture squares and board; ordering strip
Grouping: Small group — science/math area
Support: A matching mat with texture outlines glued in place as guides.

Creative Art — Goal: Create prints with contrasting textures using varied tools.
Activity: Children will make texture paintings: dragging a comb, a sponge, a feather, and a fork through paint and stamping textures side by side, labeling each print by how it would feel.
Materials: Paint; combs; sponges; feathers; forks; paper
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Adapted brush handles and a paint tray with raised edges.

Music / Movement — Goal: Match movement quality to music: smooth versus bumpy.
Activity: We will move with scarves to music that changes character — smooth flowing music means slow waves; bumpy staccato music means short hops and shakes — feeling the music's texture with our whole body.
Materials: Scarves; recorded contrasting music
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: A soft-textured scarf option for children sensitive to standard ribbon wands.

Motor Activities — Goal: Trace shapes with fingertips, building tactile and fine motor control.
Activity: Children will trace textured shapes with two fingers — a sandpaper star, a velvet heart — first with eyes open, then trying with eyes closed like reading with fingertips.

Grouping: Centers — fine motor table
Support: Larger shapes and raised-line cards for children refining finger control.

Technology — Goal: Use close-up photography to study texture detail.

Grouping: Small groups; teacher-led
Support: Teacher sets up the tablet stand; children choose which texture to photograph.

Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: The choice to watch first and join when ready, no hands forced into materials.

subject: Science

evidence:
Focus book: Seven Blind Mice — Ed Young

Language Arts — Goal: Use clues from more than one sense to identify a mystery object.
Activity: We will read the mystery of the mice who each feel one part of something big, then play our own version: one child feels an object hidden in the feely box, another hears its sound shaken, and together they guess what it is.
Materials: Focus book; feely box; mystery objects
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Puzzle piece clues limited to two senses per round for a smaller decision.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Combine senses to make and test a prediction.
Activity: Children will hunt the classroom mystery object using combined clues — listen to it shake, feel it in the box, peek at its color — and draw the object before the reveal, checking their prediction.
Materials: Mystery objects; clue cards; drawing paper
Grouping: Small groups — science table
Support: A two-sense clue card for children who need the search narrowed.

Social Science — Goal: Teach another group what we learned about senses.
Activity: Children will share our senses learning with a visitor (or the class next door) by demonstrating the feely box, the sound shakers, and the texture board — being the teachers for ten minutes.
Materials: Feely box; sound shakers; texture board
Grouping: Whole/part group; teacher-supported
Support: A job card to carry showing their sharing role in the demonstration.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Graph favorite senses and compare quantities.
Activity: Children will vote for the sense they would miss most, build our graph, and figure out which sense 'won' and by how many votes — counting up the difference together.
Materials: Pocket-chart graph; sense picture ballots
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Counting each column with a partner and pointing to each vote.

Creative Art — Goal: Combine the week's learning in a collaborative senses mural.
Activity: Together we will paint our senses mural: a giant face outline where each child adds one sense feature — big listening ears, a smelling nose with flower scents drawn, watching eyes — and signs their part.
Materials: Mural paper; paints; brushes; mirrors for reference
Grouping: Large group in shifts — art area
Support: A defined panel on the mural and labeled paint cups.

Music / Movement — Goal: Perform the week's songs with each child leading a part.
Activity: We will perform our listening-walk song and sound-word actions one last time, with each child leading the sound for one verse while classmates echo.

Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A map with the route pre-drawn for children tracing rather than planning.

Activity: Children will line up picture cards of everyone who chased the Gingerbread Man in story order and count the chasers, checking their line against the book.

Grouping: Small group — carpet; teacher-guided
Support: A sequence strip with boxes for the order of chasers.

Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: A glue sponge for children who find squeeze bottles tiring.

Music / Movement — Goal: Remember and perform a cumulative movement song.
Activity: We will learn a chase song: each verse adds an animal's movement (cow stomp, pig wiggle, horse gallop) while everyone chants the gingerbread refrain between verses.

Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: Picture cue cards for each chaser's movement shown before each verse.

Motor Activities — Goal: Move through an obstacle path with speed control and safe stopping.

Grouping: Small groups — gym/outdoor; teacher-supervised
Support: A shorter course and a walking (not running) option for children who need a steadier pace.

Support: Headphones fitted by the teacher and tracking cards for page turns.

Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A compare chart with picture columns for each book's ending.

Grouping: Small groups — science table; teacher-guided
Support: A ramp with pre-set height marks so testing stays manageable.

Grouping: Small groups — carpet; teacher-guided
Support: A feelings face card to signal how their character feels at each scene.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Sort animals by number of legs and count groups.
Activity: Children will count the animals on the Gingerbread Girl's farm, then sort the animal counters by legs — two legs or four — and count each group's total.
Materials: Animal counters; sorting mats; counting string
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: An abacus-style counting string to slide a bead per animal.

Creative Art — Goal: Design an original character with drawn details.
Activity: Children will design their own gingerbread character — girl, boy, or animal — drawing its outfit, icing hair, and candy buttons, then give it a name and a clever talent.
Materials: Gingerbread outlines; crayons; markers; stickers
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: A gingerbread outline with hair guide dots for children wanting a starting path.

Music / Movement — Goal: Alternate energetic movement with thoughtful stillness on cue.
Activity: We will learn a clever-plan freeze dance: boogie like runaway cookies while music plays, freeze into a 'thinking pose' when it stops, and call out a plan word (climb! swim! build!).
Materials: Recorded music; open rug
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: A mirrored partner to copy movements from in real time.

Motor Activities — Goal: Lace a complete outline with hand-eye coordination.
Activity: Children will lace around gingerbread shapes through punched holes, following the edge all the way around to 'sew' their cookie's icing border.
Materials: Gingerbread lacing cards; laces
Grouping: Centers — fine motor table
Support: Easy-grip laces and a pre-punched first hole to start from.

Technology — Goal: Create a photo sequence to retell a story.
Activity: Children will arrange their gingerbread puppets into three story scenes while the teacher photographs each, making a photo sequence they can retell from the screen in order.

Grouping: Small groups; teacher-led
Support: Teacher operates the tablet while children arrange and direct the scenes.

Activity: We will walk to our playground 'river' (blue mat or chalk stream) and practice safe crossing choices: the stepping-stone bridge or the log balance — never the deep part — linking back to the story's choice.

Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: A pre-walked shorter route option with the same two crossings.

Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A problem card with two possible solutions to choose between.

Grouping: Small group — math center

Activity: Children will drive toy car wheels through shallow paint and across long paper 'roads,' noticing the different track patterns each vehicle leaves.

Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: A vehicle with a handle grip and a smaller paper road for more control.

Music / Movement — Goal: Sing a traveling song with a steady beat.

Grouping: Small group — listening area; teacher-guided
Support: Two sound choices at a time for children who need a smaller listening set.

Support: A fidget or a favorite book in hand for children who find waiting hardest.

Support: Front seating close to the screen for children who need a clearer view.

Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led

Support: Buddy pairs for the walk; the teacher leads the first house visit as a model.

Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Specific praise naming the polite word each child shares.

Focus book: Hershel and the Hanukkah Goblins — Eric Kimmel

Language Arts — Goal: Recall story events and sequence the nights of Hanukkah.
Activity: After reading, we will place eight candle cards in a row as we retell Hershel's nights, and children will explain that Hanukkah lasts eight nights and a candle is added each night.
Materials: Focus book; candle number cards; felt menorah board
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Number cards with dots under each numeral for children matching quantity to number.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Investigate light and shadow with candles as our theme (battery candles only).
Activity: Children will explore how a battery candle's glow looks near and far, and make shadows with their hands on the wall, describing what happens when the light is covered and uncovered.
Materials: Battery candles; flashlight; white wall or sheet
Grouping: Small groups — darkened corner of the room
Support: Extra turns at the light source for children who need more time to experiment.

Social Science — Goal: Learn what Hanukkah celebrates and how families mark it.
Activity: We will look at photos of a menorah (called a hanukkiah), a dreidel, and latkes, and learn that families light candles, sing songs, play games, and remember a story of oil that lasted eight days long ago.
Materials: Photo cards of Hanukkah items; classroom menorah model (battery candles)
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Photo cards to hold and name for children who learn best with something in hand.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Play a dreidel-inspired counting game with counters.
Activity: Children will spin a dreidel (or spin-and-count cards) and take or return the matching number of pretend gelt counters, counting aloud with the group. We use pretend coins only — no food treats.
Materials: Dreidels; pretend coin counters; small bowls
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: Counting with a partner and a number line strip for support.

Creative Art — Goal: Make a menorah collage with nine candle flames.
Activity: Children will glue nine paper candles onto a menorah outline — eight for the nights and one taller helper candle (the shamash) in the middle or side — and add foil flames.
Materials: Menorah outlines; paper candles; foil pieces; glue
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Pre-cut candles and a glue sponge for children building cutting and squeezing skills.

Music / Movement — Goal: Sing and move to a gentle candle-lighting song.
Activity: We will sway like candle flames to a slow recorded Hanukkah song, then march lightly in place for a livelier verse, freezing when the music pauses.
Materials: Recorded Hanukkah music; open rug space
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: A spot marker to sway on for children who need a defined space.

Motor Activities — Goal: Strengthen fine motor control spinning and rolling.
Activity: Children will practice spinning dreidels and top spinners, and roll small balls of playdough into 'oil lamp' shapes, building finger strength and control.
Materials: Dreidels and tops; playdough; trays
Grouping: Centers — fine motor table
Support: Larger, easy-grip tops for children still mastering the spin motion.

Technology — Goal: Listen to Hanukkah songs at the listening center.
Activity: Children will listen to recorded Hanukkah songs (including the dreidel song) and follow along in a picture book about the holiday, turning pages at the chime.

Grouping: Centers — pairs; child-led after setup
Support: Headphones fitted by the teacher and a bookmark to hold the page.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Take a winter 'lights walk' outdoors.
Activity: Outside we will walk the school grounds looking for lights — windows, pathway lamps, decorations — and talk about why lights feel special on dark winter days.

Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: Buddy pairs and a picture checklist to check off together.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Learn that light can stand for hope and remembering.
Activity: We will talk about how the Hanukkah story remembers a hard time that ended well, and how lighting candles helps families remember and feel hopeful. Children may share something that makes them feel hopeful.
Materials: Feelings chart; battery candle
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: The option to hold the battery candle while sharing, as a talking light.

Social Science — Goal: Learn what Kwanzaa is and when families celebrate it.
Activity: We will learn that Kwanzaa is a celebration created in 1966 to honor African heritage and family, held from December 26 to January 1, where families light seven candles in a holder called a kinara and talk about the seven principles.
Materials: Kinara model (battery candles); calendar chart; photos of Kwanzaa items
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A simple timeline strip (Dec 26 → Jan 1) to show where the days fall.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Count and order the seven kinara candles.
Activity: Children will place seven battery candles — three red, three green, one black in the center — into our kinara model in order, counting them and naming the colors as they go.
Materials: Kinara model; seven battery candles (red, green, black)
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: A color-order card showing where each candle belongs.

Creative Art — Goal: Weave a paper mkeka mat with Kwanzaa colors.
Activity: Children will weave red, green, and black paper strips over and under a base mat, making their own version of the mkeka — the mat that holds the Kwanzaa symbols.
Materials: Paper strips; base mats; glue at edges
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Wider strips and a started first row for children new to weaving.

Music / Movement — Goal: Move to drum rhythms, copying the leader's pattern.
Activity: We will listen to recorded drumming, clap and stomp simple copied rhythms — slow, fast, stop — and take turns being the rhythm leader for four beats.
Materials: Recorded drumming; rhythm sticks
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: Visual beat cards (big dot = loud, small dot = soft) for children who need to see the pattern.

Motor Activities — Goal: Build wrist and hand strength drumming and shaking.
Activity: Children will play hand drums and shakers in a circle, practicing starting and stopping together and passing instruments carefully to a neighbor.
Materials: Hand drums; shakers; circle seating
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: Instruments with handles and a shorter turn for children building stamina.

Technology — Goal: Record our voices saying the principles.
Activity: Using the class voice recorder, each child who wishes will say one principle word or a kind sentence about family, and we will listen to our class recording together.

Grouping: Small group then large group; teacher-guided
Support: Children may record with a partner speaking together if they prefer.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Gather outdoors in a unity circle and play a cooperative game.
Activity: Outside we will stand in a big circle, hold a parachute together, and keep a ball bouncing in the middle — it only works if everyone holds on and helps, like the principle of unity.
Materials: Parachute; soft ball; outdoor space
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: A spot beside the teacher on the parachute for children who need a secure grip position.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Practice the principle of unity: we are stronger together.
Activity: We will talk about Umoja (unity) in classroom words — sticking together and helping our class family — and each child will name one way they helped a classmate this week.
Materials: Principle card; class chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Specific praise as the teacher names each helpful act a child shares.

title: Holidays Around the World: Diwali — A Fall Festival of Lights
subject: Social Studies
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Holidays Around the World' thematic week (December): Diwali — A Fall Festival of Lights. Focus book: Binny's Diwali — Thrity Umrigar. evidence:
Focus book: Binny's Diwali — Thrity Umrigar

Language Arts — Goal: Sequence Binny's celebration and name its special items.
Activity: After reading, children will sequence picture cards — new clothes, diya lamps, sweets, fireworks in the sky (pictures only) — and learn the words diya and rangoli.
Materials: Focus book; Diwali picture cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Four-card sequence only for children who need a shorter set.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Explore color mixing for rangoli designs.
Activity: Children will mix colored sand and chalk dust in trays, noticing how red and yellow make orange, and predict what blue and yellow will make before they try.
Materials: Colored sand and chalk in trays; spoons; color chart
Grouping: Small groups — science table
Support: Pre-mixed example cups to compare against while predicting.

Social Science — Goal: Learn when and why Diwali is celebrated — accurately.
Activity: We will explain that Diwali is a festival of lights celebrated in the fall (October or November) by Hindu families and others, often included in winter-holiday units. Families light small oil lamps called diyas to celebrate light winning over darkness and remember the story of Rama and Sita coming home.
Materials: World calendar; photo cards of diyas and rangoli; map showing India
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A season chart showing Diwali in the fall leaves section, so the timing is clear and correct.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Create number patterns in a rangoli border.
Activity: Children will build repeating patterns with colored gems and beans around a rangoli outline — two red, one gold, two red, one gold — and read their pattern aloud.
Materials: Rangoli outlines; gems and beans; pattern cards
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: A started pattern strip to continue for children learning the repeat.

Creative Art — Goal: Make rangoli art with colored sand and glue.
Activity: Children will draw glue lines on a rangoli outline and sprinkle colored sand, shaking off the extra to reveal bright patterns. (Sand stays on trays; no food materials used.)
Materials: Rangoli outlines; colored sand; glue bottles; trays
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Squeeze-bottle glue with a wide tip and a damp sponge for sticky fingers.

Music / Movement — Goal: Dance with scarves to recorded Indian music.
Activity: We will move flowing scarves in big circles and gentle waves to recorded music, copying the teacher's slow and fast movements and freezing in a statue pose at the end of each phrase.
Materials: Scarves; recorded music
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: A scarf on a short ribbon wand for children who need an easier grip.

Motor Activities — Goal: Strengthen pincer grasp placing gems and beans.
Activity: Children will use fingers and then tweezers to place gems one by one onto rangoli dot grids, filling each dot before moving to the next row.
Materials: Dot grids; gems; tweezers; small bowls
Grouping: Centers — fine motor table
Support: Larger gems and fingertip placement only for children not yet ready for tweezers.

Technology — Goal: Look at photographs of Diwali celebrations on the projector.
Activity: We will view teacher-selected photos of diyas, rangoli, and family celebrations, and children will point out the lights and patterns they recognize from our book.
Materials: Projector; teacher-selected photo set
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Front-row seating and time to look before questions begin.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Decorate our outdoor path with chalk rangoli (weather permitting).
Activity: Outside, children will draw big rangoli-inspired chalk patterns on the pavement near our door, working in small teams on circles, dots, and petal shapes.
Materials: Thick chalk; pavement area; pattern cards
Grouping: Small teams — outdoors; teacher-guided
Support: A large pre-drawn circle to fill in for children who want a starting shape.

Activity: We will talk in simple words about Diwali's message — being kind and good is like turning on a light — and each child will name a kind act that 'lights up' our classroom.
Materials: Feelings chart; battery diya (teacher-made)
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Kind-act picture cards to choose from for children thinking of an idea.

title: Holidays Around the World: Las Posadas — Asking for Welcome
subject: Social Studies
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Holidays Around the World' thematic week (December): Las Posadas — Asking for Welcome. Focus book: The Legend of the Poinsettia — Tomie dePaola. evidence:
Focus book: The Legend of the Poinsettia — Tomie dePaola

Language Arts — Goal: Retell the story's gift-giving lesson in our own words.
Activity: After reading, children will retell how Lucida worries about having no gift and learns that a gift given with love is enough, sequencing three story pictures as we talk.
Materials: Focus book; story picture cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Picture prompts for beginning, middle, and end placed left to right.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Observe a poinsettia plant closely and describe its parts.
Activity: Children will examine a real poinsettia (looking only — we do not eat any part), noticing that the red parts are special leaves, and draw what they observe in science journals.
Materials: Poinsettia plant; magnifiers; journals; crayons
Grouping: Small groups — science table
Support: Extra observation time and a leaf-shape stencil for journals.

Social Science — Goal: Learn what Las Posadas is: nine nights of welcome in Mexico.
Activity: We will learn that in Mexico, from December 16 to 24, families and neighbors walk in processions remembering Mary and Joseph looking for a place to stay (posada means a lodging or inn), singing at doors until they are welcomed in for food, music, and celebration.
Materials: Photo cards of posadas; map showing Mexico; battery candle
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A nine-night counting strip to make the nine evenings concrete.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Count to nine on our posadas night-counting strip.
Activity: Children will add a star sticker for each of the nine nights of Las Posadas, counting aloud and circling the number 9 on our strip when it is complete.
Materials: Counting strip 1–9; star stickers; crayons
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: Numbers with dots beneath them for children counting with one-to-one support.

Creative Art — Goal: Make a paper poinsettia flower.
Activity: Children will layer red and green paper 'leaves' around a center circle to build a poinsettia, arranging the red bracts in a star shape like the flower in our story.
Materials: Red and green paper shapes; circles; glue sticks
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Pre-cut shapes sorted in trays for children focusing on arranging and gluing.

Music / Movement — Goal: Practice a welcome procession with a call-and-response song.
Activity: Carrying battery candles, we will walk slowly around the rug in a line while the teacher sings a question line and children answer with the response line, arriving at our 'welcome door' at the end.
Materials: Battery candles; doorway prop; teacher-led song
Grouping: Large group — rug and classroom path; teacher-led
Support: A place near the front with the teacher for children who need a steady pace model.

Motor Activities — Goal: Build arm strength carrying the star lantern (hand-over-hand option available).
Activity: Children will take turns carrying our lightweight paper star lantern along the procession path, holding it high with both hands and walking heel-to-toe on the line.
Materials: Paper star lantern; floor tape line
Grouping: Small groups — movement area
Support: A lighter star on a short stick and a partner walking alongside.

Technology — Goal: Listen to a recorded posadas song and clap the response parts.
Activity: At the listening center, children will hear a recorded Las Posadas song in Spanish and English, clapping when the welcoming answer comes and learning to say 'bienvenidos' (welcome).

Grouping: Centers — pairs; child-led after setup
Support: The teacher models the clap cue once before children listen independently.

Support: Role-play in pairs first for children who want to rehearse the words.
