Activity: After reading, children will match word cards (with pictures) to items in the story — the white dress, the candle crown, the tray of buns — and use one word in a sentence.
Materials: Focus book; picture word cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Point-and-name matching for children building spoken language.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Explore darkness and light: how early winter darkens the north.
Activity: Using a globe and a flashlight 'sun,' the teacher will show how winter days are short and dark in Sweden, and children will test which materials let light shine through (translucent) and which block it.
Materials: Globe; flashlight; translucent and opaque materials
Grouping: Small groups — science table; teacher-led demo
Support: Children take turns holding the flashlight with hand-over-hand help if needed.

Social Science — Goal: Learn what St. Lucia Day is and how Swedish families celebrate.
Activity: We will learn that on December 13 in Sweden, children take part in candlelight processions; a Lucia wears white with a crown of candles (we will use battery candles), and songs and saffron buns are shared to bring light to the darkest days.
Materials: Photo cards of Lucia processions; battery candle crown (teacher-made)
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Photo cards passed hand to hand so every child sees them up close.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Count candles on the Lucia crown and compare sets.
Activity: Children will count the battery candles on our pretend crown (seven), then build sets of seven with candle counters and check a partner's set with one-to-one counting.
Materials: Battery candle crown; candle counters; number cards
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: A seven-dot strip to place counters on for a counting guide.

Creative Art — Goal: Make a paper candle crown.
Activity: Children will decorate a paper crown band with drawn candles and foil flames, measuring it (with the teacher's help) to fit their head for our procession play.
Materials: Paper bands; crayons; foil; glue; stapler (teacher only)
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Pre-measured bands and sticker flames for children who need fewer steps.

Music / Movement — Goal: Sing a procession song while walking slowly in a line.
Activity: We will learn a simple Lucia procession song (in English translation), walking slowly in a line with hands together, swaying gently as we sing about bringing light.
Materials: Teacher-led song; open pathway
Grouping: Large group — classroom; teacher-led
Support: A steady partner beside children who find slow walking tricky.

Motor Activities — Goal: Develop balance walking the procession path with a tray.
Activity: Children will carry a tray with two soft pretend buns along a taped path without letting them slide off, walking slowly like the Lucia procession.
Materials: Trays; soft pretend buns; floor tape
Grouping: Small groups — movement area
Support: One bun only and a wider path for children building balance.

Technology — Goal: Use a tablet to view a short Lucia procession clip (teacher-selected).
Activity: We will watch a brief clip of a real St. Lucia procession, listening to the singing and watching the candles, then name two things we noticed that matched our book.
Materials: Tablet or projector; teacher-selected clip
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Seating close to the screen and a pause to talk midway.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Take a dark-day walk and look for signs of winter light outdoors.
Activity: Outside we will notice how low the sun sits and how early the shadows stretch, find our classroom windows glowing, and talk about why people love candles in winter.
Materials: Playground; winter sky observation
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: A partner to walk and look with; hats and mittens checked before going out.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Learn that one person's light and kindness can cheer a whole room.
Activity: We will talk about how Lucia brings light, songs, and treats to others, and each child will share one small kind thing they could bring to a friend — a song, a drawing, a kind word.
Materials: Kindness picture cards; feelings chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Choosing a picture card counts as sharing for quieter children.

title: Holidays Around the World: Chinese New Year — A Preview
subject: Social Studies
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Holidays Around the World' thematic week (December): Chinese New Year — A Preview. Focus book: Bringing in the New Year — Grace Lin. Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: Bringing in the New Year — Grace Lin

Language Arts — Goal: Sequence the family's New Year preparations.
Activity: After reading, children will order picture cards of getting ready — sweeping, hanging decorations, cooking together, watching the dragon dance — and learn that this celebration is also called Lunar New Year or Spring Festival.
Materials: Focus book; preparation picture cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Five-card sequence with first/last cards already placed as anchors.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Explore red: shades, sorting, and why red matters for luck.
Activity: Children will sort red objects and paper by shade from light to dark, and learn that red is a lucky color for the New Year, used on lanterns, envelopes, and banners to wish for good fortune.
Materials: Red objects and paper in many shades; sorting tray
Grouping: Small groups — science table
Support: Three shades only for children starting with a simpler ordering task.

Social Science — Goal: Learn when Chinese New Year comes and what it celebrates.
Activity: We will explain that Chinese New Year begins on a new moon in late January or February — so it is a celebration still coming this winter — welcoming spring, family reunions, and a fresh start, with a new zodiac animal each year.
Materials: Calendar; zodiac animal wheel (picture version); map showing China
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: The class calendar with a star on the coming weeks so 'not yet' is visible.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Count gold coins into lucky red envelopes (pretend).
Activity: Children will count pretend gold coins and place the correct number into envelopes marked with numerals, 'packing luck' for pretend family gifts. (Pretend coins only — no food.)
Materials: Red envelopes; pretend coins; numeral cards
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: Envelopes 1–5 and a counting mat for children securing early numbers.

Creative Art — Goal: Make a paper lantern with cut fringe.
Activity: Children will decorate red paper, fold it with the teacher's help, and snip fringe along the edge (teacher pre-scores the lines) to make a lantern to hang in our room.
Materials: Red paper; crayons; safety scissors; glue; string
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Loop scissors and pre-scored cut lines for children building scissor skills.

Music / Movement — Goal: Move like a dragon dance team under a ribbon dragon.
Activity: Working together under a long ribbon 'dragon' held on sticks (teacher-led ends), children will practice moving as one team — slow waves, a dip, and a rise — to recorded festival music.
Materials: Ribbon dragon or fabric streamer; recorded music
Grouping: Large group — movement area; teacher-led
Support: A middle spot with neighbors close for children who need support moving in a line.

Motor Activities — Goal: Strengthen hands squeezing glue and placing gold dots.
Activity: Children will squeeze glue dots onto a banner outline and press gold foil circles in a row, making a good-luck banner for our door.
Materials: Banner outlines; glue bottles; gold foil circles
Grouping: Centers — fine motor table
Support: Glue sponges instead of bottles for children working on squeezing control.

Technology — Goal: Take a photo hunt for red around our classroom.
Activity: With the teacher, small groups will use the class tablet to photograph red things in our room — books, blocks, clothing — then count the photos together on screen.
Materials: Class tablet (teacher-held); projector
Grouping: Small groups; teacher-led
Support: Children point out and direct each photo; the teacher operates the tablet.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Hang our lanterns outside the door and observe them move.
Activity: We will hang our paper lanterns along the outdoor entry (weather permitting), watch them sway in the winter air, and talk about how moving air makes them dance.
Materials: Finished lanterns; string; outdoor entry
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: Step-stool turns supervised one at a time; a partner holds each lantern until it is tied.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Learn that a new year is a chance for fresh starts and family time.
Activity: We will talk about how families clean, gather, and wish each other well for the New Year, and each child will share one wish or fresh start they hope for this year.
Materials: Wish picture cards; class chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Drawing a wish instead of saying it is warmly welcomed.

title: Holidays Around the World: Celebration Wrap-Up — Lights We Share
subject: Social Studies
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Holidays Around the World' thematic week (December): Celebration Wrap-Up — Lights We Share. Focus book: Celebrating Together — — a picture book visiting many winter celebrations around the world (substitute any world-celebrations title on hand). Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: Celebrating Together — — a picture book visiting many winter celebrations around the world (substitute any world-celebrations title on hand)

Language Arts — Goal: Compare our celebrations and retell a favorite moment.
Activity: We will revisit our celebration photo wall and each child will pick one celebration moment to retell — what the lights were, who gathered, what we ate or sang — using our sentence frame 'I remember when...'
Materials: Celebration photo wall; sentence frame cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Pointing to a photo and naming one thing counts as a full retell for emerging speakers.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Investigate candles and lamps: safe light sources in our classroom.
Activity: Children will compare our battery candles, a lamp, a flashlight, and window daylight, testing which lights up a book page best for reading and sorting them by 'plugs in,' 'batteries,' and 'the sun.'
Materials: Battery candles; small lamp; flashlight; book page
Grouping: Small groups — science table
Support: Testing in pairs so children share the tools and the talking.

Social Science — Goal: Sort celebration items to the celebrations they belong to.
Activity: Children will sort our week's item cards — dreidel, kinara candle, diya, poinsettia, Lucia crown, lantern — onto the matching celebration mats, naming each celebration as they place its items.
Materials: Celebration item cards; labeled mats with photos
Grouping: Large group then small groups — carpet
Support: Fewer cards (one per celebration) in the first round for children building memory.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Graph our favorite celebration discovery.
Activity: Children will place their name card under the celebration they most enjoyed learning about, and we will count each column together and say which has the most and which has the fewest.
Materials: Pocket chart graph; name cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Counting each column aloud with a pointing partner.

Creative Art — Goal: Create a class 'festival of lights' mural.
Activity: Together, children will add a paper light for every celebration we studied — candles, diyas, lanterns, stars — onto a big night-sky mural, writing or dictating the celebration's name beside their light.
Materials: Butcher paper; paper lights in many shapes; glue; markers
Grouping: Large group in shifts — art area
Support: A defined mural space and pre-cut light shapes to decorate.

Music / Movement — Goal: Sing our celebration songs — a gentle medley and movement review.
Activity: We will move through our week's songs one by one — swaying like candles, drumming a beat, waving scarves, marching in procession — remembering which celebration each song belongs to.
Materials: Recorded songs from the week; scarves; rhythm sticks
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: Song picture cards shown before each song as a memory cue.

Motor Activities — Goal: Complete a celebration obstacle path using the week's skills.
Activity: Children will move through a course that revisits our week: spin a dreidel, weave between cones like a procession, carry a tray of pretend buns, and hang a lantern on the finish line.
Materials: Dreidel; cones; tray and pretend buns; paper lantern
Grouping: Small groups — movement area; teacher-supervised
Support: Stations shortened and extra time allowed; the course is for fun, not speed.

Technology — Goal: Make a class slideshow of our celebration week.
Activity: The teacher will show our week's photos — art, cooking-free tastings of pictures, processions, lanterns — and children will narrate what is happening in each photo for our class slideshow captions.
Materials: Projector; week's class photos
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Children may narrate with a partner or point while the teacher narrates.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Take a final winter walk and hang a class lantern outdoors.
Activity: Outside, we will hang one big class lantern by our door as a symbol of all the lights we learned about, and walk once around the grounds sharing our favorite outdoor discovery of the week.
Materials: Class lantern; string; playground route
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: Buddy pairs; the teacher ties the lantern while children hold and watch.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Learn that different families celebrate in different ways, and every way deserves respect.
Activity: We will close the unit by naming what all our celebrations shared — light, family, food, songs, and kindness — and practice respectful words: 'Tell me about your celebration.' Each child will share one thing they are glad they learned.
Materials: Celebration mats; feelings chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Specific praise for respectful questions and careful listening.

title: Caring, Kindness, and Resolutions: What Is Kindness?
subject: SEL
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Caring, Kindness, and Resolutions' thematic week (January): What Is Kindness?. Focus book: The Kindness Book — Todd Parr. Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: The Kindness Book — Todd Parr

Language Arts — Goal: Learn kindness vocabulary and use it in a sentence.
Activity: After reading, we will add picture word cards — help, share, hug, listen, wait — to our word wall, and each child will finish the sentence 'Kindness is...' with their own idea.
Materials: Focus book; word cards; word wall; chart paper
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Picture cards to point to and a sentence frame for children who need the words started.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Observe living things that need our care: our class plant.
Activity: Children will examine our class plant closely — leaves, soil, new growth — and make a care plan: who waters, how much, and how we will know it is thirsty.
Materials: Class plant; magnifier; watering can; care chart
Grouping: Small groups — science table
Support: A picture care chart with steps to follow in order.

Social Science — Goal: Sort actions into 'kind' and 'unkind' with reasons.
Activity: Using scenario picture cards (helping up a friend, grabbing a toy, comforting someone sad), children will sort them onto our kind/unkind mats and tell why each one belongs there.
Materials: Scenario picture cards; sorting mats
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Partner talk first so children can rehearse their reason before sharing.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Count acts of kindness on our kindness graph.
Activity: Every time we catch a kindness today we will add a heart counter to our jar chart; at day's end children will count the hearts and compare today's total with our goal of ten.
Materials: Heart counters; jar chart; number line
Grouping: Whole class, gathered at day's end
Support: Counting in pairs with one child pointing and one counting aloud.

Creative Art — Goal: Make a kindness handprint wreath.
Activity: Children will trace and cut (or tear) handprints and arrange them in a circle wreath for our door, each hand standing for a helping hand in our class.
Materials: Paper; crayons; safety scissors; glue; wreath circle
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Pre-cut handprints for children still building scissor skills; hand-over-hand help available.

Music / Movement — Goal: Move gently: mirror a partner's kind movements.
Activity: To slow music, children will mirror a partner's gentle movements — waving, swaying, offering a hand — practicing watching another person carefully.
Materials: Recorded gentle music; open rug space
Grouping: Large group in pairs — rug; teacher-led
Support: Teacher pairs children thoughtfully and models the first round.

Motor Activities — Goal: Strengthen hands squeezing and wringing a helping sponge.
Activity: As 'kindness helpers,' children will carry a dripping sponge on a tray to a plant or table, squeeze it out, and wipe a small spill — real helping with real tools.
Materials: Sponges; trays; small buckets of water
Grouping: Small groups — practical area; teacher-supervised
Support: A smaller sponge and a shorter carry for children building grip and balance.

Technology — Goal: Listen to a kindness story at the listening center.
Activity: Children will follow along with a recorded story about helping, turning pages at the chime and pointing to the kind act on each page.
Materials: Listening center; recorded story; book copies
Grouping: Centers — pairs; child-led after setup
Support: A page-marker ribbon for children who lose their place.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Show care for our outdoor space on a tidy-up walk.
Activity: Outside, we will walk the playground with a teacher, picking up litter with tongs and putting it in the bin, and check that our garden area has water.
Materials: Tongs; bucket; litter bin; watering can
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: Gloves and tongs sized for small hands; handwashing right after.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Learn our week's big idea: kindness is something we do.
Activity: We will introduce our caring unit: this week we will practice kindness on purpose, and in January many people make fresh-start promises — ours will be kindness promises we choose on Friday.
Materials: Feelings chart; promise teaser chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Specific praise for every example of kindness a child names.

title: Caring, Kindness, and Resolutions: Filling Each Other's Buckets

description: Preschool day plan from the 'Caring, Kindness, and Resolutions' thematic week (January): Filling Each Other's Buckets. Focus book: Have You Filled a Bucket Today? — Carol McCloud. Language Arts — Goal: Explain the bucket idea in our own words.
Activity: After reading, children will retell the book's idea — everyone carries an invisible bucket, and kind words and actions fill it — and act out one filling and one dipping example with puppets.
Materials: Focus book; puppets; class bucket prop
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Puppet acting for children who would rather show than tell.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Investigate filling and emptying with water and measuring cups.
Activity: At the water table, children will fill buckets with cups of water, count how many cups fill each size, and pour out to 'empty' — saying which bucket holds more.

Grouping: Centers — science area; child-led
Support: Numbered cup lines on the bucket for children counting the fills.

Social Science — Goal: Practice bucket-filling words with a partner.
Activity: Children will practice giving a real compliment — 'I like how you...' — to a partner, then switch, building a class list of kind things we can say.
Materials: Compliment starter cards; class bucket
Grouping: Large group then pairs — carpet
Support: Compliment starters with pictures for children who need a beginning.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Fill a ten-frame bucket with counters for each kind act.
Activity: In our math game, children will roll a die, say a kind act, and add that many counters to a bucket ten-frame, racing to fill exactly ten.
Materials: Dice; counters; bucket ten-frame mats
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: Dice with dots only up to 3 for children working with smaller numbers.

Creative Art — Goal: Decorate a personal paper bucket for kind notes.
Activity: Children will decorate a paper bucket with their name and favorite colors; through the week, classmates' kind notes and drawings will be dropped inside.
Materials: Paper buckets; crayons; stickers
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Name cards to copy from and chunky crayons for a comfortable grip.

Music / Movement — Goal: Sing a bucket-filling song with filling motions.
Activity: We will learn a cheerful song about filling buckets, adding scoop-and-pour arm motions on the chorus and a gentle 'dip no more' shake on the verse.
Materials: Teacher-led song; bucket prop
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: Motion picture cards held up at each part of the song.

Motor Activities — Goal: Build finger strength clipping kind notes to our line.
Activity: Children will clip paper hearts and kind notes onto our classroom kindness line with clothespins, stretching up and squeezing each pin open.
Materials: Clothespins; paper hearts; low clothesline
Grouping: Centers — fine motor table
Support: Spring-easy clothespins and a lower line section within easy reach.

Technology — Goal: Record a compliment to play back.
Activity: Using the voice recorder, children may record a short compliment for the class ('You are a good builder!'), and we will listen to our recordings together at circle.

Grouping: Small group then large group; teacher-guided
Support: Recording with a partner's voice alongside for shy speakers.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Spread kindness outdoors: chalk messages on the path.
Activity: Outside, children will draw chalk hearts and suns on the walkway where other classes pass, to surprise them with something cheerful (teacher checks school rules first).

Support: A drawn heart outline to color in for children who want a starting shape.

Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A feelings-face card to show how each moment feels.

title: Caring, Kindness, and Resolutions: Sharing and Taking Turns
subject: SEL
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Caring, Kindness, and Resolutions' thematic week (January): Sharing and Taking Turns. Focus book: Should I Share My Ice Cream? — Mo Willems. Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: Should I Share My Ice Cream? — Mo Willems

Language Arts — Goal: Make a prediction and revisit it after the story.
Activity: Before reading we will predict whether Gerald will share his ice cream in time; children will show predictions with thumbs cards, and after the story we will check what really happened and why sharing felt hard.
Materials: Focus book; prediction thumbs cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Two picture choices to point to instead of explaining a prediction.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Explore melting: watch an ice cube change (no food activity).
Activity: Children will observe ice cubes in warm and cool spots, predict which melts first, and check every few minutes, learning that some treats cannot wait — just like Gerald's ice cream.
Materials: Ice cubes; two trays; timer; observation chart
Grouping: Small groups — science table
Support: A picture timeline to mark 'still ice / melting / water' at each check.

Social Science — Goal: Take turns fairly in a sharing game.
Activity: We will practice a turn-taking board game in small groups — rolling, moving, waiting, and cheering for friends — with the teacher modeling how to wait and what to say when we want a turn.
Materials: Simple board games; dice; movers
Grouping: Small groups — tables; teacher-guided
Support: A turn-order picture strip so children can see whose turn is next.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Divide a set fairly: share counters between two friends.
Activity: Children will share 10 pretend 'berries' between two stuffed friends, dealing one for you, one for me, and count to check both piles are equal.
Materials: Counters; two stuffed animals; plates
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: Even, smaller sets (6) first for children learning fair sharing.

Creative Art — Goal: Create a sharing picnic collage.
Activity: Children will cut or tear pictures of foods and picnic items and glue them onto a shared blanket picture, making room for everyone's choices on one blanket. (Pictures only — no real food.)
Materials: Magazines and picture cards; blanket outline; glue
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Pre-cut pictures sorted in trays for children focusing on arranging.

Music / Movement — Goal: Play a cooperative parachute game where everyone shares the work.
Activity: Holding the parachute together, the class will bounce a soft ball gently and keep it from rolling off — if anyone lets go, the ball escapes, so everyone matters.
Materials: Parachute; soft ball; open space
Grouping: Large group — movement area; teacher-led
Support: A grip spot next to the teacher and a lighter ball.

Motor Activities — Goal: Strengthen turn-taking hands: pass-and-squeeze relay.
Activity: Pairs will pass a soft ball hand to hand down a line, squeezing it once before passing, practicing 'my turn, your turn' with their hands and words together.
Materials: Soft balls; line markers
Grouping: Small groups — movement area
Support: A shorter line and a slower pace set by the teacher.

Technology — Goal: Photograph sharing in action around our room.
Activity: With the teacher, children will use the class camera to catch real sharing moments — a passed crayon, a shared book — and we will view them at circle and celebrate each one.
Materials: Class camera or tablet (teacher-held); projector
Grouping: Small groups then large group; teacher-led
Support: Children spot and direct the photo while the teacher holds the camera.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Practice playground sharing on the bikes and slide.
Activity: Outside, we will set a sand-timer for popular equipment and practice the handoff: when the sand runs out, we smile, say 'your turn,' and trade places kindly.
Materials: Sand timer; playground equipment
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: The teacher stays near the timer for children who need support with the trade.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Learn that sharing can feel hard — and still be worth it.
Activity: Like Gerald, we will name how sharing can feel tricky (we want it all!) and how it feels after, and each child will share one thing that is easy for them to share and one that is hard.
Materials: Feelings chart; focus book
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Two picture choices ('easy to share / hard to share') to sort and talk from.

title: Caring, Kindness, and Resolutions: Including Everyone
subject: SEL
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Caring, Kindness, and Resolutions' thematic week (January): Including Everyone. Focus book: Enemy Pie — Derek Munson. Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: Enemy Pie — Derek Munson

Language Arts — Goal: Recall how the story's friendship changed and why.
Activity: After reading, we will chart what the narrator first thought about his 'enemy' and what he learned after spending a day together, and children will retell the turning point in their own words.
Materials: Focus book; chart paper; markers
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Beginning/end picture cards to anchor the retell.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Investigate friendship ingredients: what makes a good playmate? (A science-style sort.)
Activity: Like a recipe investigation, children will sort 'friendship ingredient' cards — listening, laughing together, bossiness, sharing, teasing — into 'goes in our pie' and 'leave it out,' and defend their choices.
Materials: Ingredient picture cards; pretend pie tin; sorting mats
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Sorting with a partner so ideas can be tested in conversation first.

Social Science — Goal: Practice inviting someone new to play.
Activity: With puppets and then in pairs, children will practice the words and body language of inviting: walk over, smile, say 'Would you like to play with us?' and make room in the game.
Materials: Puppets; play props
Grouping: Large group then pairs — carpet
Support: Invitation sentence strip displayed and practiced chorally first.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Count and compare: how many friends can play?
Activity: Children will build block towers in pairs and count how many blocks two builders can stack together versus alone, noticing that together-towers can grow taller — then graph the two heights.
Materials: Blocks; counting chart
Grouping: Small groups — building area
Support: Counting together aloud with the teacher after each tower.

Creative Art — Goal: Make friendship bracelets to give away.
Activity: Children will string beads onto pipe cleaners to make a bracelet for someone else in class, choosing colors they think that friend would love. (Bracelets are gifts, not for keeping.)
Materials: Pipe cleaners; large beads; name cards of recipients
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Beads with larger holes and a tray to keep them from rolling.

Music / Movement — Goal: Dance with everyone: a mixer movement game.
Activity: To music, children will dance around the rug; when it stops, everyone finds a partner nearby for a friendly move (wave, high-five, spin), then dances again to meet someone new.
Materials: Recorded music; open rug space
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: The teacher joins the game so every round includes and models warm greetings.

Motor Activities — Goal: Build hand strength threading and lacing friendship cards.
Activity: Children will lace yarn through hole-punched friendship cards, following the holes in order to 'sew' a heart outline for a classmate.
Materials: Lacing cards; yarn with taped ends
Grouping: Centers — fine motor table
Support: Cards with fewer, larger holes for children starting lacing.

Technology — Goal: Use the listening center to hear a story about an unlikely friendship.
Activity: Children will listen to a recorded friendship story and draw the moment the characters became friends, then share their drawing with a partner.
Materials: Listening center; recorded story; paper and crayons
Grouping: Centers then pairs
Support: A partner share instead of a group share for children who prefer a smaller audience.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Include everyone in an outdoor circle game.
Activity: Outside we will play a circle passing game where the beanbag must visit every child before it can return, practicing watching for who has not had a turn yet.
Materials: Beanbag; circle space outdoors
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: The teacher calls gentle reminders ('Who is still waiting?') to support noticing.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Learn that people we don't know yet can become friends.
Activity: We will talk about how the narrator almost missed a friendship, and each child will name one way to give a new person a chance — play together once before deciding.
Materials: Feelings chart; focus book
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Specific praise for kind and thoughtful suggestions.

title: Caring, Kindness, and Resolutions: Our Kindness Promises
subject: SEL
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Caring, Kindness, and Resolutions' thematic week (January): Our Kindness Promises. Focus book: How Full Is Your Bucket? For Kids — Tom Rath and Mary Reckmeyer. Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: How Full Is Your Bucket? For Kids — Tom Rath and Mary Reckmeyer

Language Arts — Goal: Retell the bucket story and connect it to our whole week.
Activity: After reading, children will retell Felix's day of bucket filling and dipping, matching each story moment to moments from our own week — sharing, including, complimenting.
Materials: Focus book; our week's photo cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Week photos as memory anchors for the retell.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Review our plant care plan and observe growth.
Activity: We will revisit the class plant we planned to care for on Monday, measure its height with cubes, check the soil, water it together, and record what changed.
Materials: Class plant; unifix cubes; care chart; watering can
Grouping: Small groups — science table
Support: Cube measuring done hand-over-hand with a partner if needed.

Social Science — Goal: Choose a kindness promise (our January resolution).
Activity: Each child will choose one caring promise for the new year — 'I will help clean up,' 'I will invite friends to play,' 'I will use kind words' — and the teacher will write it on their promise leaf for our kindness tree.
Materials: Promise picture cards; paper leaves; markers
Grouping: Large group then small groups — tables
Support: Three picture choices offered so choosing is manageable; the teacher scribes every promise.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Count our week's kindness hearts and celebrate the total.
Activity: We will count all the hearts on our kindness graph from the week, compare the days, and find which day our buckets were fullest — then set a kind goal for next week.
Materials: Kindness graph; heart counters; number line
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Counting in chunks with a partner pointing along.

Creative Art — Goal: Add promise leaves to our kindness tree.
Activity: Children will decorate their promise leaf and place it on our big paper tree, building a class display of the caring goals we chose for January.
Materials: Paper tree; decorated leaves; glue or tape
Grouping: Art center / large group in shifts
Support: Pre-cut leaves and a low branch space for every child's reach.

Music / Movement — Goal: Perform our bucket song and kindness moves for a finale.
Activity: We will sing our bucket-filling song one more time with all its motions, then add a final kindness freeze dance, ending frozen in a kind pose — a hug, a wave, a helping hand.
Materials: Teacher-led song; recorded music
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: A pose picture card to copy for children who want an idea.

Motor Activities — Goal: Finish strong: our helping-hands obstacle course.
Activity: Children will move through a kind-helpers course: carry a sponge to water a plant, deliver a kind note across the room, clip a heart to the line, and return for a high-five.
Materials: Sponges; kind notes; clothespins and line; cones
Grouping: Small groups — movement area; teacher-supervised
Support: Stations shortened; the course is untimed so helping stays the focus.

Technology — Goal: Make a slideshow of our caring week to share with families.
Activity: The teacher will show our week's photos and recordings; children will help choose the order and dictate one caption about kindness for the class slideshow.
Materials: Projector; week's photos and recordings
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Children may point to their photo and say one word for the caption.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Take a gratitude walk outdoors.
Activity: Outside, we will walk slowly and name things we are thankful for in our schoolyard — the tree, the slide, the birds — practicing gratitude for the places we share.
Materials: Playground route; gratitude picture cards
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: A partner to name gratitudes with along the way.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Learn that a promise kept a little each day grows into a habit.
Activity: We will close our unit by hearing our promises read aloud, and talk about how doing one kind thing each day is how resolutions come true; the teacher will name a specific caring moment from each child this week.
Materials: Promise leaves on the tree; feelings chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Every child hears their own caring moment named — the teacher keeps a simple list from the week.

title: Friends Around the World (Preschool Unit)

Days: Day 1: Children Everywhere Are Like Us; Day 2: Hello in Many Languages; Day 3: Same, Same but Different; Day 4: Our Names Matter; Day 5: Friends Celebration Day. Focus books: Whoever You Are; All Are Welcome; Same, Same but Different; The Name Jar; Friends Near and Far.

Sensory: Texture world tray: children explore natural materials — sand, smooth stones, leaves, shells — sorting and describing what children everywhere might find outdoors. Materials: Sand tray; stones; leaves; shells; scoops and sorting cups
Fine Motor: Name and greeting work: bead name strands, lace greeting cards, stamp hello in different scripts (teacher-made stamps), and clip flags onto a world line. Materials: Beads and cords; lacing cards; letter stamps; clothespins and flag cards

title: Friends Around the World: Children Everywhere Are Like Us
subject: Social Studies
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Friends Around the World' thematic week (January): Children Everywhere Are Like Us. Focus book: Whoever You Are — Mem Fox. Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: Whoever You Are — Mem Fox

Language Arts — Goal: Understand the book's message: different outside, same inside.
Activity: After reading, children will retell the book's gentle refrain in their own words — children everywhere may look, eat, and speak differently, but smiles, laughter, and love are the same — and give a thumbs-up example from a page.
Materials: Focus book; feelings chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Page pictures to point to as examples for children still forming sentences.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Observe how our hands are alike and different (science of us).
Activity: Children will compare handprints — size, lines, fingerprints with magnifiers — noticing every print is unique and every hand works the same way: holding, helping, waving.
Materials: Ink pads and paper (washable); magnifiers; wipes
Grouping: Small groups — science table
Support: Stamping done with hand-over-hand help if wanted; extra prints to take time on.

Social Science — Goal: Find our homes on a globe and see how far children live.
Activity: Using a globe, the teacher will spin slowly while children watch the lands and oceans pass, then place a sticker on our home and talk about children waking up, eating breakfast, and playing all around that same globe.
Materials: Globe; stickers; world pictures
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Children take turns spinning gently with the teacher's guidance.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Count children in our class and in book pictures, comparing sets.
Activity: Children will count the children pictured on two book pages and count our own class photo, saying which set has more and how we know.
Materials: Focus book; class photo; counters
Grouping: Large group then small groups — carpet
Support: Counting rows with a pointing partner for one-to-one support.

Creative Art — Goal: Make a handprint wreath of many skin-tone colors.
Activity: Children will paint handprints using a palette of skin-tone paints and arrange them in a circle — many colors, one class wreath — for our door.
Materials: Skin-tone paint set; paper; brushes; wreath backing
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Children choose their own paint color; adaptive brush handles available.

Music / Movement — Goal: Greet and move: a hello circle warm-up.
Activity: We will pass a greeting around the circle — each child says hello in our class way and adds a friendly move (wave, bow, spin) that the next child copies, celebrating many ways to say the same kind word.
Materials: Open rug space; greeting picture cards
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: The teacher starts the chain slowly so the copying pattern is clear.

Motor Activities — Goal: Build cooperative strength in a partner carry.
Activity: Pairs will carry a big soft ball together across the room — two children, four hands, one job — trading partners for a second trip.
Materials: Large soft balls; cones
Grouping: Small groups in pairs — movement area
Support: A lighter ball and a shorter trip for pairs who need an easier start.

Technology — Goal: Look at photographs of children around the world on the projector.
Activity: We will view teacher-selected photos of children in many places — going to school, eating with family, playing — and children will name what looks the same as their lives and what looks new.
Materials: Projector; teacher-selected photo set
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Extra looking time before questions; front seating for a clear view.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Take a friendship walk and notice our own neighborhood outdoors.
Activity: Outside we will walk our school grounds greeting the people we meet — other classes, our custodian, families arriving — practicing that friends and neighbors are everywhere, starting here.
Materials: Outdoor route; greeting practice
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: Buddy pairs; greetings rehearsed once indoors first.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Learn that every person deserves a friendly hello.
Activity: We will introduce our unit's promise: whoever you are, you are welcome here. Each child will practice the words with a smile to a partner.
Materials: Class promise chart; feelings chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Specific praise for warm greetings and brave first tries.

title: Friends Around the World: Hello in Many Languages
subject: Social Studies
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Friends Around the World' thematic week (January): Hello in Many Languages. Focus book: All Are Welcome — Alexandra Penfold. Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: All Are Welcome — Alexandra Penfold

Language Arts — Goal: Learn 'hello' in several languages and match each to its flag card.
Activity: After reading, children will practice greetings — hola, bonjour, jambo, ni hao, konnichiwa, shalom, namaste — clapping the syllables and matching each greeting card to its picture of children who might say it.
Materials: Focus book; greeting cards with pictures; flag cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Two greetings taught first, then more added for children ready to extend.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Explore sound: how words and music differ and delight.
Activity: Children will listen to short recorded greetings and song clips from several countries, raise a hand when the language changes, and describe which sounds were new to their ears.
Materials: Recorded clips (teacher-selected); picture cards
Grouping: Small groups — listening area; teacher-guided
Support: Clips replayed as often as children wish; volume kept comfortable.

Social Science — Goal: Learn that our school welcomes families from many places.
Activity: We will walk our hallway (in our minds and on our chart) naming the places our school families come from — languages spoken, foods loved, holidays kept — and add them to a class welcome map. (Families may share voluntarily; the chart celebrates what we know.)
Materials: Class welcome chart; map; markers
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Children may share about their own family or about a friend's — both are celebrated.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Play a matching game: greetings and the children who say them.
Activity: Children will match greeting word cards to picture cards of children around the world, counting their matches and comparing totals with a partner.
Materials: Matching card set; counting mat
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: A six-pair game for children starting out; twelve pairs as a challenge.

Creative Art — Goal: Create a welcome banner with hello in many words.
Activity: As a class art project, children will stamp, trace, or sticker the word hello in several languages onto a long banner, decorating the spaces with handprints and hearts for our doorway.
Materials: Banner paper; letter stamps; stickers; crayons
Grouping: Large group in shifts — art area
Support: Stampers with chunky handles and letters already placed as guides.

Music / Movement — Goal: Dance to music from around the world.
Activity: We will move to short clips of music from several countries — swaying, stepping, spinning as the music suggests — freezing and naming the country when each clip ends (teacher tells us).
Materials: Recorded world music clips; scarves
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: A scarf to hold for children who like a movement prop.

Motor Activities — Goal: Develop rhythm copying drum patterns from near and far.
Activity: Children will copy simple rhythms on drums and shakers the way children in many places make music together — slow beats, fast beats, and a resting silence.
Materials: Hand drums; shakers
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: Visual beat cards shown while rhythms are played.

Technology — Goal: Hear our own voices say hello in many languages (recording).
Activity: Using the voice recorder, children who wish will record a greeting in any language they know or are learning, and we will play our class greeting chorus at circle.
Materials: Voice recorder or tablet
Grouping: Small group then large group; teacher-guided
Support: Recording together with a friend is always an option.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Practice greetings outdoors with a greeting parade.
Activity: Outside, we will parade along the path stopping at 'country stations' (picture signs) to say that place's greeting together with a wave, bow, or hands-together thank-you.
Materials: Station signs with pictures; outdoor path
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: Station cards carried by helpers; the pace stays slow and joyful.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Learn that learning someone's hello is a way to say 'you matter.'
Activity: We will talk about how it feels when someone greets us in words from our own home, and each child will choose one new greeting to keep practicing this week.
Materials: Greeting cards; feelings chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Choosing a card to hold makes the choosing easier and prouder.

evidence:
Focus book: Same, Same but Different — Jenny Sue Kostecki-Shaw

Language Arts — Goal: Compare the two pen pals' lives and chart same and different.
Activity: After reading about Elliot and Kailash, children will help fill a two-column chart — both boys draw, climb trees, and love their families; their homes, foods, and landscapes differ — and add one idea of their own.
Materials: Focus book; two-column chart; markers
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Picture choices for children adding their idea by pointing.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Investigate trees around the world and right here.
Activity: Elliot and Kailash both climb trees — children will examine leaves and bark rubbings from our schoolyard tree and compare them with photos of trees in India, noticing shapes, sizes, and colors.
Materials: Leaves; bark rubbing supplies; tree photo cards
Grouping: Small groups — science table
Support: Rubbing done with the paper taped down for steady hands.

Social Science — Goal: Learn that pen pals and faraway friends can know each other through letters and drawings.
Activity: We will set up a class post office: children will 'write' a drawing-letter to an imaginary friend in another country, telling about their favorite food, game, and tree, and mail it in our class mailbox.
Materials: Paper; crayons; envelopes; class mailbox
Grouping: Large group then centers — writing area
Support: Drawing counts fully as writing; the teacher helps address envelopes.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Sort picture cards into 'same' and 'different' for two children.
Activity: Children will sort cards of daily life (breakfast, school, play, bedtime) into things both story boys do the same and things they do differently, counting each pile at the end.
Materials: Daily-life picture cards; sorting mats
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: Sorting in pairs so counting and deciding are shared work.

Creative Art — Goal: Paint a two-panel picture: my world and my friend's world.
Activity: Children will paint their own home or street on one panel and imagine a faraway friend's on the other, using photo cards for ideas and keeping the same sun shining over both.
Materials: Two-panel paper; paints; photo cards
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Photo ideas spread out for children who want a starting picture.

Music / Movement — Goal: Play a 'same and different' movement game.
Activity: When the teacher names something both friends do (jump! eat! sleep!), everyone does the action; when she names a different-clothes item, children mime putting it on — listening carefully is the game.
Materials: Teacher-led game; open rug space
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: Actions shown on picture cards at the same time as they are named.

Motor Activities — Goal: Build finger strength with a mailbox slot drop.
Activity: Children will post shape 'letters' through matching slots in our class mailbox, turning and trying until each shape fits — persistence with a happy purpose.
Materials: Shape mailbox; shape letters
Grouping: Centers — fine motor table
Support: Larger shapes with fewer choices for children building the skill.

Technology — Goal: Use the class camera to photograph 'our world' for a faraway friend.
Activity: With the teacher, children will photograph the things they would show a pen pal — our tree, our classroom door, our lunch table — and view the photo letter together.
Materials: Class camera or tablet (teacher-held); projector
Grouping: Small groups; teacher-led
Support: Children choose and direct each shot; the teacher holds the camera.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Climb and play on our own schoolyard 'tree' (the climbing structure).
Activity: Outside, children will play on our climbing structure and swings like the story boys do, then rest in its shade and look up at our real tree's leaves moving.
Materials: Playground climbing structure; shade tree
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: Ground-level pretend tree play for children not climbing today.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Learn that differences are interesting, not strange.
Activity: We will revisit the boys' favorite line — same, same but different — and each child will name one difference between friends that they think is wonderful.
Materials: Feelings chart; focus book
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Sentence frame provided: 'I like that you...' to a classmate.

title: Friends Around the World: Our Names Matter
subject: Social Studies
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Friends Around the World' thematic week (January): Our Names Matter. Focus book: The Name Jar — Yangsook Choi. Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: The Name Jar — Yangsook Choi

Language Arts — Goal: Retell how Unhei decides about her name and why names are special.
Activity: After reading, we will retell Unhei's story — a new girl from Korea worries about her name, collects name ideas in a jar, and finally chooses her own real name — and share why our names are gifts from our families.
Materials: Focus book; jar prop; name cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Story picture cards in order as retell supports.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Explore stamping and printing: Unhei's name stamp (dojang).
Activity: Children will examine how a name stamp works — the teacher shows a stamp pressing ink to paper — then make their own initial stamp art by pressing sponge letters into paint and printing.
Materials: Teacher stamp demo; sponge letters; paint pads; paper
Grouping: Small groups — art/science table
Support: Pre-inked pads and big sponge letters for a successful print.

Social Science — Goal: Learn that new friends can come from far away and feel nervous at first.
Activity: We will talk about what it is like to be new — in a class, a neighborhood, a country — and list what we can do to help: learn their name, smile, show them around, save them a seat.
Materials: Class chart; welcome picture cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Ideas rehearsed in pairs before the group list is written.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Count the letters in our names and compare lengths.
Activity: Children will build their name with letter tiles, count the letters, and place it on our class graph from shortest to longest names, finding who has the most and fewest letters.
Materials: Letter tiles; name cards; class graph
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: Name card to copy from; counting done with a partner pointing at each tile.

Creative Art — Goal: Make a name art piece to treasure.
Activity: Children will decorate the letters of their own name with patterns, stickers, and drawings of things they love, making a name plate for their cubby or our wall.
Materials: Name outlines; crayons; stickers; collage bits
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Letters pre-outlined large; adaptive crayons available.

Music / Movement — Goal: Move to a name rhythm game.
Activity: We will clap and stomp the syllables of our names around the circle — two claps for a short name, more for a long one — then dance a freeze game where the teacher calls a name rhythm to copy.
Materials: Open rug space; name cards
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: The teacher claps each name first; children join when ready.

Motor Activities — Goal: Strengthen hands beading name patterns.
Activity: Children will string beads in a pattern matching the colors on their name card — one bead per letter — building a name bracelet or bookmark strand.
Materials: Beads; stringing cords; name cards
Grouping: Centers — fine motor table
Support: Larger beads and a stiff cord tip for easier threading.

Technology — Goal: Listen to names pronounced with care (teacher-recorded greeting chain).
Activity: We will listen to our class greeting recording, and the teacher will help us practice saying every classmate's name correctly and warmly — because saying a name right is a kindness.
Materials: Voice recorder with class greetings; name cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Names practiced in a friendly chorus, never as a solo test.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Welcome a pretend new friend on an outdoor tour.
Activity: Outside, pairs will give a stuffed 'new friend' a tour of our playground — showing the slide, the door, the meeting spot — practicing the words 'This is where we... come, I'll show you.'
Materials: Stuffed animal; playground route
Grouping: Whole class in pairs — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: The teacher models the first tour stop for everyone.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Learn that everyone's name deserves to be learned and said right.
Activity: Unhei chose her own name proudly — we will promise to learn each other's names and correct mistakes kindly, and each child will tell the class how their name should be said.
Materials: Class promise chart; focus book
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Specific praise for careful listening and brave correcting.

title: Friends Around the World: Friends Celebration Day
subject: Social Studies
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Friends Around the World' thematic week (January): Friends Celebration Day. Focus book: Friends Near and Far — — a joyful picture book celebrating friendship in many places (substitute any global friendship title on hand). Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: Friends Near and Far — — a joyful picture book celebrating friendship in many places (substitute any global friendship title on hand)

Language Arts — Goal: Retell our whole unit through its stories.
Activity: After our final book, children will use our unit photo and story wall to retell the friends we met — children everywhere, pen pals, a new girl and her name jar — and pick the story moment they loved most.
Materials: Focus book; unit story wall
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: The story wall does the remembering; children choose and point.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Review our handprint science: celebrate every print.
Activity: We will look back at our handprints from Monday, compare them once more with magnifiers, and add a new print beside the old to see how we have grown in just one unit.
Materials: Handprints from Day 1; magnifiers; ink pads
Grouping: Small groups — science table
Support: Prints compared side by side with a partner's help.

Social Science — Goal: Host a classroom 'friendship festival' with greeting stations.
Activity: Children will rotate through stations — say hello in three languages, stamp a name card, draw a pen-pal letter — practicing everything our unit taught in a joyful morning.
Materials: Station signs; greeting cards; stamps; letter paper
Grouping: Centers rotation — whole room; teacher-guided
Support: Station picture directions so children can move with confidence.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Graph our favorite way to greet a friend.
Activity: Children will vote with a name card — wave, high-five, hello in another language, a bow — and we will count the columns and celebrate every greeting as a winner.
Materials: Pocket chart graph; name cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Counting columns aloud together with pointing.

Creative Art — Goal: Finish our friendship mural: children holding hands around a globe.
Activity: Children will add their decorated self-portrait figure to a big paper globe mural, linking hands with classmates' figures in a ring around the world.
Materials: Paper globe mural; figure cutouts; crayons; glue
Grouping: Art center / shared project in shifts
Support: A defined spot on the ring for each child's figure.

Music / Movement — Goal: Perform our greeting songs and dances as a finale.
Activity: We will sing and move through our unit's favorites — the hello circle, world music dances, the name rhythm game — as a celebration performance for ourselves.
Materials: Recorded music; scarves; open rug space
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: Favorite parts chosen by vote so the finale belongs to the class.

Motor Activities — Goal: Complete a friendship obstacle course using the week's skills.
Activity: Children will carry a ball with a partner, post a letter in the mailbox, clap a friend's name rhythm at the rhythm station, and end with a greeting high-five.
Materials: Balls; mailbox; rhythm cards; course signs
Grouping: Small groups — movement area; teacher-supervised
Support: Stations untimed and repeatable; partners chosen with teacher support.

Technology — Goal: Create our class 'friends around the world' slideshow.
Activity: The teacher will show our unit's photos and recordings; children will help order them and dictate captions about friends near and far to share with families.
Materials: Projector; unit photos and recordings
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Caption dictation in pairs for children who want a co-author.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Take a celebration walk and deliver our pen-pal letters outdoors.
Activity: We will walk our friendship route one last time, greeting everyone we pass, and 'deliver' our drawing-letters to the office mailbox or a buddy class — real kindness, really delivered (teacher arranges).
Materials: Drawing-letters; school route; buddy class or office
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors and halls; teacher-led
Support: Buddy pairs; letters carried carefully in folders.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Learn that friendship is a choice we make every day, everywhere.
Activity: We will close by reading our class promise — whoever you are, you are welcome here — and each child will name one friendship skill they will keep: a greeting, an invitation, a name said with care.
Materials: Class promise chart; feelings chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: The teacher names one friendship strength she saw in each child this week.

title: My Body / Healthy Living: Our Amazing Bodies
subject: PE / Health
description: Preschool day plan from the 'My Body / Healthy Living' thematic week (January): Our Amazing Bodies. Focus book: From Head to Toe — Eric Carle. Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: From Head to Toe — Eric Carle

Language Arts — Goal: Name body parts and use them in a sentence.
Activity: We will read the focus book and move along with each animal, then play a naming round: the teacher points to a body part on our big body poster and children name it and say one thing it can do.
Materials: Focus book; large body-part poster; pointer
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Picture cards for children who need to point to the body part before saying its name.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Observe how the heart beats faster after movement.
Activity: Children will rest a hand on their chest to feel a calm heartbeat, march in place for one minute, then feel again and describe the change. We will chart the words they use: slow, fast, thump.
Materials: Chart paper; markers; timer
Grouping: Large group then pairs — rug; teacher-led
Support: A seated marching option for children who need a low-impact way to join in.

Social Science — Goal: Recognize that every body is different and every body can do many things.
Activity: We will compare hand sizes by tracing our hands side by side on a class poster and talk about how our bodies look different and can all run, build, hug, and help.
Materials: Poster paper; crayons; pencils for tracing
Grouping: Small groups — tables; teacher-guided
Support: A partner or teacher traces for children still building the hand control to trace their own hand.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Count body parts and match numerals to quantities up to 10.
Activity: Children will count features on a face chart — 2 eyes, 1 nose, 10 fingers — and place number cards beside each count, then count their own fingers and toes in socks.
Materials: Face chart; number cards 1–10; counting bears
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: A number line strip to touch while counting for children building one-to-one correspondence.

Creative Art — Goal: Draw a self-portrait with head, body, arms, and legs.
Activity: Looking in mirrors, children will draw themselves and try to include the body parts we named today. The teacher will visit and ask each child to tell about one part they drew.
Materials: Mirrors; drawing paper; crayons and skin-tone crayon set
Grouping: Independent/small group — art table
Support: Chunky crayons and a starting scaffold (a light head circle) for children who find a blank page hard.

Music / Movement — Goal: Follow directions to move named body parts to music.
Activity: We will sing and move to 'Head, Shoulders, Knees and Toes,' starting slowly and speeding up, then play a freeze round where children hold a pose when the music stops.
Materials: Recorded song; open rug space
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: A spot near the teacher and permission to sit for the fast rounds while still tapping the body parts.

Motor Activities — Goal: Build body awareness by copying poses and movements.
Activity: Children will play 'Mirror, Mirror' in pairs: one child makes a pose or slow movement with arms, legs, or whole body, and the partner copies it like a mirror, then they switch.
Materials: Open space; pose picture cards
Grouping: Pairs — movement area; teacher-supervised
Support: Pose cards showing seated poses for children who need a stable base while copying.

Technology — Goal: Use a digital microscope to look closely at skin and hair.
Activity: With the teacher, small groups will place a hand under the digital microscope, view their skin and fingerprints on the screen, and describe the patterns they see.
Materials: Digital microscope; screen or tablet display
Grouping: Small groups — science table; teacher-led
Support: Teacher operates the focus dial while children direct what to look at next.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Use the whole body in outdoor play: run, climb, balance, and jump.
Activity: Outside, children will move through a simple course — run to the fence, walk the low balance line, climb the structure steps, and jump from the low platform — naming the body parts doing the work.
Materials: Playground equipment; cones; chalk line
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-supervised
Support: A shorter course and a walking buddy for children still building confidence on equipment.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Learn to be thankful for what our bodies can do.
Activity: We will close circle by naming one thing we are glad our bodies can do — run, draw, sing, hug — and add it to our gratitude chart shaped like a big smiling sun.
Materials: Gratitude sun chart; sticky notes; markers
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Picture choices (run, draw, hug) to point to for children who need help thinking of an idea.

title: My Body / Healthy Living: Our Five Senses
subject: PE / Health
description: Preschool day plan from the 'My Body / Healthy Living' thematic week (January): Our Five Senses. Focus book: My Five Senses — Aliki. Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: My Five Senses — Aliki

Language Arts — Goal: Use describing words for what we see, hear, smell, taste, and feel.
Activity: After reading, we will build a five-senses word wall: for each sense picture, children offer a describing word from the story (loud, soft, sweet, rough) and the teacher writes it on the chart.
Materials: Focus book; senses chart; word cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Real objects to hold while naming the sense, for children who learn best by touching first.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Investigate materials using one sense at a time.
Activity: Children will rotate through sense stations: listening to shakers and guessing the filling, feeling hidden objects in a feely box, and smelling spice jars, recording a favorite discovery with a drawing.
Materials: Sound shakers; feely box with objects; spice jars (cinnamon, vanilla); drawing paper
Grouping: Centers — science area; teacher-guided
Support: A pass card for the smell station for children sensitive to strong scents; smelling is always a choice.

Social Science — Goal: Understand that people may experience the world differently (glasses, hearing aids).
Activity: We will look at photos of tools that help senses — glasses, hearing aids, a cane — and talk kindly about how they help people see, hear, and move safely.
Materials: Photo cards of sensory tools; spare dress-up glasses (no lenses)
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Simple, concrete language and extra think time before discussion questions.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Sort objects by a sensory attribute and explain the rule.
Activity: Children will sort a tray of objects by sound (quiet/loud shakers), then by feel (smooth/rough), telling a partner which rule they used each time.
Materials: Sorting trays; shaker eggs; texture objects
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: Two-category sorting with the rule shown as a picture for children new to classifying.

Creative Art — Goal: Create textured art to explore the sense of touch.
Activity: Children will make texture collages, gluing sandpaper, cotton, felt, foil, and bubble wrap onto cardboard and rubbing crayons over some pieces to feel the difference.
Materials: Texture scraps; cardboard; glue; crayons
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Glue sponges and pre-cut pieces for children building scissor and squeezing skills.

Music / Movement — Goal: Listen carefully and respond to sound cues.
Activity: We will play 'Sound Hunt Freeze': children move to music, and when a mystery sound plays (bell, drum, rain stick) they freeze and guess what made it before moving again.
Materials: Sound instruments; recorded music
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: A warning before loud sounds and a seat near the teacher for children startled by noise.

Motor Activities — Goal: Strengthen fingers with squeezing, pinching, and twisting.
Activity: At the fine motor table children will squeeze water droppers into cups, pinch pom-poms with tweezers, and twist lids onto matching jars — all 'sense tools' our hands use every day.
Materials: Droppers; cups; tweezers; pom-poms; jars with lids
Grouping: Centers — fine motor table
Support: Easy-squeeze droppers and larger lids for children developing hand strength.

Technology — Goal: Record and play back sounds with a voice recorder.
Activity: In pairs, children will record themselves making a classroom sound (tapping, crinkling, humming) on the voice recorder, then the class will listen and guess each sound.
Materials: Voice recorder or tablet recording app; sound-making objects
Grouping: Small groups; teacher-guided
Support: Teacher holds the recorder; children choose the sound and press the big button with hand-over-hand help if needed.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Use senses to observe nature closely.
Activity: On a senses walk outside, children will stop at marked spots to listen for birds, feel bark and grass, look for colors, and smell the air after rain or near the garden beds.
Materials: Senses walk cards; clipboards; crayons
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: A partner to walk and observe with; a picture checklist to mark instead of drawing.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Practice listening to others — really listening — as a way to show care.
Activity: We will practice 'whole-body listening' (eyes looking, ears listening, hands quiet) and use it while a partner tells us their favorite sound from today.
Materials: Listening poster; partner-talk timer
Grouping: Large group then pairs — carpet
Support: A shorter sharing turn and a sentence starter ('My favorite sound was...') for emerging speakers.

title: My Body / Healthy Living: Healthy Foods Fuel Us
subject: PE / Health
description: Preschool day plan from the 'My Body / Healthy Living' thematic week (January): Healthy Foods Fuel Us. Focus book: Gregory, the Terrible Eater — Mitchell Sharmat. evidence:
Focus book: Gregory, the Terrible Eater — Mitchell Sharmat

Language Arts — Goal: Retell a story and name the problem and how it was solved.
Activity: We will read about Gregory the goat who would not eat what goats eat, chart what his parents tried, and retell how the family found foods that worked for him.
Materials: Focus book; problem/solution chart; markers
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: First/then picture cards to support sequencing the retell.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Observe and compare real fruits and vegetables.
Activity: Children will examine a tray of produce with magnifiers — a pepper's seeds, an orange's peel, a carrot's top — and sort their observations into 'grows above ground' and 'grows below ground.' Foods are for looking only today, not tasting.
Materials: Whole produce (pepper, orange, carrot, apple); magnifiers; sorting mats
Grouping: Small groups — science table
Support: A hand lens with a handle and a picture sorting mat for children who need visual support.

Social Science — Goal: Learn where food comes from: farms, gardens, and stores.
Activity: Using picture cards, we will trace a carrot's trip from a farm field to a truck to a store to our table, and children will place each card in order on our journey board.
Materials: Farm-to-table picture cards; journey board
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Partner rehearsal before placing a card in front of the group.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Sort foods into groups and count each group.
Activity: Children will sort pretend foods into fruits, vegetables, grains, and proteins on a big 'MyPlate'-style mat, count each group, and say which group has the most.
Materials: Pretend food set; plate mat; number cards
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: Start with two groups only for children building sorting and counting stamina.

Creative Art — Goal: Print with vegetables to explore shape and pattern.
Activity: Children will dip cut vegetables (pepper halves, corn cobs, celery) into washable paint and print repeating patterns on paper placemats. Vegetables used for printing are art tools, not snacks.
Materials: Cut vegetables for printing; washable paint; paper placemats; smocks
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: A fork handle stuck in the vegetable as a grip for children who need more control.

Music / Movement — Goal: Sing a call-and-response song about foods that help us grow.
Activity: We will learn a simple chant — 'Crunch an apple, munch a carrot' — with stomping and clapping on the strong beats, then add verses children suggest for other crunchy foods.
Materials: Teacher-led chant; rhythm sticks
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: Rhythm sticks with grips and a slower tempo verse for children joining in.

Motor Activities — Goal: Practice serving skills: scooping, pouring, and carrying with two hands.
Activity: Children will practice at a serving station — scooping dry beans into bowls, pouring water from small pitchers, and carrying a tray with two hands across the room without spilling the pretend food.
Materials: Dry beans; scoops; bowls; small pitchers; trays
Grouping: Centers — practical life area
Support: A smaller scoop and a tray with raised edges for children still building steadiness.

Technology — Goal: Use a tablet to explore where foods grow (teacher-guided photo tour).
Activity: The teacher will project teacher-selected photos of farms and gardens, and children will call out what they notice growing, matching each photo to our farm-to-table journey board.
Materials: Tablet/projector with prepared farm photos; journey board
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Front-row seating for children who need to see the screen up close.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Observe a garden or outdoor plants and notice how food plants grow.
Activity: Outside, we will visit the school garden (or planters) to look for stems, leaves, and anything growing, and water the plants with small cans, talking about what plants need just like our bodies do.
Materials: Garden/planters; small watering cans; magnifiers
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-supervised
Support: A lightweight watering can and a buddy for carrying to the beds.

Activity: Like Gregory, we sometimes say no to new things. We will talk about being brave enough to try one small bite of a new food at home, and always being kind about foods other people enjoy.
Materials: Focus book (favorite page); feelings chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Permission to share by pointing to a picture food card instead of speaking.
