title: My Body / Healthy Living: Move, Rest, and Grow
subject: PE / Health
description: Preschool day plan from the 'My Body / Healthy Living' thematic week (January): Move, Rest, and Grow. Focus book: Move Your Body — — an active nonfiction picture book about exercise, rest, and growing strong (substitute any movement-and-health title on hand). Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: Move Your Body — — an active nonfiction picture book about exercise, rest, and growing strong (substitute any movement-and-health title on hand)

Language Arts — Goal: Learn action words and match them to movements.
Activity: After reading, children will draw an action word card (jump, stretch, rest, lift) and the class will do that movement, then we will build a sentence together: 'We jump with our legs.'
Materials: Focus book; action word cards with pictures; pocket chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet and rug; teacher-led
Support: Picture-supported cards so children can join the sentence building by choosing a card.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Investigate breathing: how our chest moves when we breathe in and out.
Activity: Children will place hands on their ribs, breathe slowly, and watch a tissue 'flag' flutter when they blow, learning that air moves in and out of our bodies all day.
Materials: Tissues on straws (flag demo); mirrors
Grouping: Small groups — science table
Support: A gentler blowing task (feather on a table) for children who find straws tricky.

Social Science — Goal: Identify people whose jobs help bodies stay healthy (doctor, dentist, coach).
Activity: We will match helper cards to their tools (stethoscope, toothbrush mirror, whistle) and share what each helper does for our bodies.
Materials: Helper and tool picture cards; matching board
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Fewer pairs per round (start with 3) for children building memory and matching skills.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Count jumps and record numbers up to 10 on a simple tally chart.
Activity: Each child will do star jumps while a partner counts aloud, and we will mark tallies on our class chart, then read the chart to see our biggest count.
Materials: Tally chart; markers; open space
Grouping: Pairs — movement area; teacher-supervised
Support: Counting with the teacher as a partner for children who need the numbers modeled.

Creative Art — Goal: Trace and decorate a life-size body outline.
Activity: In pairs, children will take turns lying on butcher paper while a teacher or partner traces around them, then decorate the outline with clothes, hair, and a big smile.
Materials: Butcher paper; thick markers; crayons
Grouping: Small groups — art area floor space
Support: The option to trace a large paper doll instead of lying down, for children who prefer not to be traced.

Music / Movement — Goal: Alternate moving and resting to feel how the body recovers.
Activity: We will dance fast to one song, then lie down with a stuffed animal on our bellies during a quiet song, watching the animal rise and fall with our breathing, and repeat.
Materials: Fast and slow recorded music; small stuffed animals
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: A cushion spot at the edge of the rug for children who want a calmer space to rest.

Motor Activities — Goal: Develop core strength and coordination on an indoor obstacle path.
Activity: Children will crawl through the tunnel, step over low hurdles, carry a beanbag on a scoop, and finish with three big stretches on the mat.
Materials: Play tunnel; low hurdles; scoops and beanbags; mats
Grouping: Small groups — gym area; teacher-supervised
Support: Stations can be done in any order with extra time; no racing.

Technology — Goal: Follow a guided movement video with a teacher.
Activity: We will follow a short, teacher-selected kids' movement video, pausing often to check that everyone has space and is moving safely, then cool down with the video's breathing finish.
Materials: Projector/screen; teacher-selected movement video
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: Seating near the teacher to copy her movements instead of watching the screen.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Practice running games with rules that keep everyone safe.
Activity: Outside we will play 'Red Light, Green Light' on the grass, practicing starting, stopping, and freezing — and walking back calmly when we wobble.
Materials: Red/green signal cards; open grass area
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: A shorter running distance and holding the signal cards as a helper job for children who tire quickly.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Understand that rest is part of being healthy, not a punishment or a race.
Activity: We will talk about how bodies grow during sleep and rest, share what helps us relax (a blanket, a story, quiet music), and practice a one-minute cozy rest together.
Materials: Rest mats; one soft blanket per child; quiet music
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: Choice of mat spot near a trusted adult for children who find group rest time hard.

title: My Body / Healthy Living: Keeping Clean, Staying Well
subject: PE / Health
description: Preschool day plan from the 'My Body / Healthy Living' thematic week (January): Keeping Clean, Staying Well. Focus book: Germs! Germs! Germs! — Bobbi Katz. Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: Germs! Germs! Germs! — Bobbi Katz

Language Arts — Goal: Sequence the steps of handwashing in order.
Activity: After reading, we will arrange handwashing step cards (wet, soap, scrub, rinse, dry) in order and read them together like a recipe our hands follow every day.
Materials: Focus book; handwashing step cards; pocket chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A personal step strip to keep at the sink for children learning the routine.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Observe how soap helps clean (glitter germ experiment).
Activity: Children will sprinkle a pinch of glitter 'germs' on their hands, try wiping with a dry towel, then wash with soap and water and compare. We will talk about what the soap did that water alone could not.
Materials: Glitter; towels; soap; sink access
Grouping: Small groups — sink area; teacher-supervised
Support: A glitter-free option (colored chalk dust) for children with sensory or skin sensitivities; adult checks for allergies first.

Social Science — Goal: Learn how we protect our friends: covering coughs and staying home when sick.
Activity: Using puppets, we will act out a character who coughs into an elbow, uses a tissue, and waves from home on a 'sick day,' and children will practice the elbow cough.
Materials: Puppets; tissues; feelings chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A puppet to hold and act with for children more comfortable speaking through play.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Count to 20 by ones while scrubbing (handwashing count).
Activity: We will practice our handwashing song-count: children count aloud to 20 while miming scrubbing, then count 20 real soap bubbles drawn on our counting mat.
Materials: Counting mat with bubbles; counters; number line
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: Counting in chunks with a partner (10 and 10) for children not yet counting to 20 alone.

Creative Art — Goal: Paint with soap-bubble prints (teacher-prepared mixture).
Activity: The teacher will prepare bubble-paint cups (soap, water, washable paint). Children will blow bubbles through straws onto the surface — teacher-supervised at all times, blowing out only — and press paper on top for a bubbly print.
Materials: Bubble paint cups (teacher-made); straws; paper; trays
Grouping: Art table, small groups; close teacher supervision
Support: A squeeze-bulb blower instead of a straw for children who might suck in instead of blowing out.

Music / Movement — Goal: Sing a handwashing song and perform its motions in time.
Activity: We will learn a 'Wash, Wash, Wash Your Hands' song to a familiar tune, acting out scrubbing palms, backs, and between fingers as we sing, then sing it at the real sink before snack.
Materials: Teacher-led song; sink access
Grouping: Large group — carpet, then sink
Support: Motion picture cards showing each scrubbing step as we sing.

Motor Activities — Goal: Build independence skills: turning taps, pumping soap, drying hands.
Activity: Children will rotate through our 'clean hands station': pump the soap dispenser, twist the tap handles on a practice board, and fold their own towel neatly after a real wash.
Materials: Practice tap board; soap dispenser; towels; sink
Grouping: Small groups — bathroom/sink area; teacher-supervised
Support: An adapted pump top and a step stool for children who need leverage or height.

Technology — Goal: Use a timer app to build a 20-second habit.
Activity: At the sink, children will start the visual timer on the tablet and scrub until the picture finishes — learning that the timer, not guessing, tells us when hands are clean.
Materials: Tablet with visual timer app; sink
Grouping: Pairs — sink area; teacher-guided
Support: Teacher starts the timer; child just watches and scrubs, for children who need one job at a time.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Notice how we keep our outdoor spaces clean and healthy too.
Activity: Outside, children will help tidy the playground — picking up litter with teacher-checked safety (gloves and grabbers, teacher handles anything sharp or unknown) — and wash hands right after, connecting the habit to real life.
Materials: Grabber tools; gloves; trash bags (teacher-held)
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-supervised
Support: Partner pairing and a small collection bucket for children who need a clear, simple job.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Feel proud of caring for our own bodies and our classroom community.
Activity: We will close the week by making a class pledge poster — 'We wash, we cover coughs, we rest, we eat foods that help us grow' — and every child will add a handprint to sign it.
Materials: Poster paper; washable paint for handprints; markers
Grouping: Large group — art table
Support: A stamp or sticker 'signature' option for children who do not want paint on their hands.

Grouping: Small groups — science table

Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: Counting with a partner and lining balls in a row to keep track.

Activity: Children will paint a snowy scene — white paint spattered and brushed over dark blue paper — adding a small figure in a red snowsuit like Peter's.

Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: A figure outline provided; thicker brushes for a comfortable grip.

Music / Movement — Goal: Pretend-play Peter's snow moves to music.
Activity: To gentle music, children will copy snow-day movements: toe-in-toe-out footprints, slow hill sliding (seated scoots), and snowball packing motions, freezing at the music's pause.

Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: A spot marker for children who need a home base to return to.

Grouping: Small groups — movement area
Support: A wider path and a partner's hand for children still building balance.

Technology — Goal: Listen to winter sounds at the listening center.

Grouping: Centers — pairs; child-led after setup
Support: Two picture choices per sound for a manageable match.

Support: Four core items in the first round for children new to sorting.

Social Science — Goal: Learn why dressing for weather keeps us safe and comfortable.
Activity: We will talk about how coats, hats, and mittens protect our bodies from cold, and practice checking the weather picture each morning to choose our gear.

Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: The morning weather check becomes a classroom job a child can lead.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Count and match pairs: mittens, socks, boots.
Activity: Children will find matching pairs in a clothing basket, clip each pair together, and count how many pairs we have — two make a pair.

Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: Pairs already partly sorted for children who need a head start.

Creative Art — Goal: Decorate a paper sweater with patterns.
Activity: Children will decorate a paper sweater with stripes, dots, and sponge-print patterns, choosing a repeating design down the sleeves and across the middle.

Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: A pattern starter strip to copy or extend.

Music / Movement — Goal: Sing a getting-dressed action song.
Activity: We will sing a call-and-response dressing song, acting out each item — stomp into boots, pull on mittens, zip the coat — faster each round like an excited Froggy.

Support: Adaptive zipper pulls and a larger dressing frame for easier gripping.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Count animals in the mitten and find 'one more.'
Activity: Children will add animal counters to a mitten mat one at a time, counting the growing crowd and saying how many there will be with one more animal squeezing in.

Grouping: Small group — math center

Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Pre-drawn stitch guides to trace for children building hand control.

Music / Movement — Goal: Move like the story animals in a movement parade.
Activity: We will move across the rug as each animal — mole tunneling low, hedgehog curling small, fox trotting, bear lumbering big — freezing in our animal shape at the signal.

Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led

Grouping: Small groups — gym area; teacher-supervised

Technology — Goal: Match recorded community sounds to their sources.

Grouping: Centers — pairs; child-led after setup
Support: Volume-limited headphones; teacher pre-loads the sounds so children only press play.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Spot the signs and tools that keep our school safe outdoors.
Activity: On a walk around the school grounds, children will spot safety features that helpers depend on — the crosswalk, the stop sign, our flag, the hydrant — and mark each on a picture checklist.
Materials: Picture checklists; clipboards
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: A clipboard with pictures instead of words for children tracking the hunt by matching.

Activity: Helpers keep us safe, and we help them by following safety rules and saying thank you. Each child will tell a partner one rule they follow that makes a helper's job easier.

Grouping: Pairs — carpet
Support: A stuffed animal to tell the thank-you idea to first, for shy children rehearsing.

title: Community Leaders: People Who Build and Fix
subject: Social Studies
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Community Leaders' thematic week (February): People Who Build and Fix. Focus book: Iggy Peck, Architect — Andrea Beaty. evidence:
Focus book: Iggy Peck, Architect — Andrea Beaty

Language Arts — Goal: Retell a builder's story and dictate a building idea.
Activity: We will read about Iggy, who builds with anything he can find, and chart his creations. Children will dictate a sentence about something they would love to build in our town.

Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Building word cards with pictures for children adding vocabulary at their own pace.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Test which bridge designs are strongest.

Grouping: Small groups — science/building table

Grouping: Large group — building center

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Measure height with cubes and compare (taller, shorter).
Activity: Children will measure their block towers with unifix cube trains, count and record the height, then try to build one exactly one cube taller.

Grouping: Small group — building center
Support: Cube snap-together strips pre-made in lengths of 5 for children learning to count on.

Creative Art — Goal: Construct a 3D building from recycled materials.
Activity: Children will build junk castles and bridges — boxes, tubes, and cups taped and glued into structures, then painted — and name their building like real architects name theirs.

Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Glue in a dish with a brush for children swapping squeeze bottles for control.

Music / Movement — Goal: Act out building-tool motions in a song.
Activity: We will sing and move to a building song: hammering (fists), sawing (arms), painting (big strokes), and resting when the whistle 'blows' — with children suggesting new tool verses.
Materials: Teacher-led song; tool picture cards
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: Motions shown at half speed first for children learning the sequence.

Motor Activities — Goal: Carry loads with balance along a beam path.
Activity: Children will carry blocks one at a time across the room to a building site — walking heel-to-toe on the tape 'plank' — and stack their delivered blocks into the class wall before it 'closes for the day.'
Materials: Blocks; tape plank path; hard hats
Grouping: Small groups — building/movement area
Support: Larger, lighter blocks for children whose arms tire with the big wooden set.

Technology — Goal: Document a building project in photo sequence.
Activity: Children will photograph the stages of our class build (plan, blocks going up, finished town hall) and we will arrange the photos in order as a slideshow of how builders work.

Grouping: Small groups; teacher-guided

Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: A clipboard with a simple one-shape checklist for children who need a focused search.

Materials: Focus book (bridge pages); feelings chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A 'try again' card to hold up when a tower falls, as a cue for the words.

title: Community Leaders: Caring for Our Town
subject: Social Studies
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Community Leaders' thematic week (February): Caring for Our Town. Focus book: Who Runs Our Town? — — a photo picture book about the people who run a town — mayor, librarian, road crew, and park keeper (substitute any town-helpers title on hand). evidence:
Focus book: Who Runs Our Town? — — a photo picture book about the people who run a town — mayor, librarian, road crew, and park keeper (substitute any town-helpers title on hand)

Language Arts — Goal: Learn town roles and what each person does for the community.
Activity: We will read about the people who care for a town — the mayor who helps make decisions with the community, librarians, road crews, and park keepers — and add each role and what it does to our town chart.

Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Photo cards of each place for children answering by pointing and naming.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Plant and plan to care for a living thing.

Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Role rotation kept short (two roles) for children who find many changes hard.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Make choices with a set of 10 tokens and count the results.
Activity: Playing 'town council,' children will give their group 10 tokens to 'spend' and choose between picture projects (new swings, more library books, flowers for the park), counting tokens into each choice jar.
Materials: Tokens; choice picture cards; jars
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: Budget cards in small numbers (1–5) for children working in that range.

Creative Art — Goal: Create a pop-up paper town scene.
Activity: Children will make a pop-up town card: a folded paper street with houses and one town building they choose (library, bakery, clinic), decorated and standing upright.

Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Pre-cut house shapes for children who want to spend their time decorating.

Music / Movement — Goal: March in formation behind a flag bearer.
Activity: We will hold a pretend town parade rehearsal: marching in a line behind our class flag to marching music, waving to 'neighbors' (stuffed animals lined up as watchers), and stopping neatly at the town hall mat.
Materials: Class flag; recorded marching music; stuffed-animal audience
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: Instrument shakers with handles for children joining the parade from seated spots.

Motor Activities — Goal: Practice caretaking jobs: sweeping, gathering, and watering.
Activity: Children will be the park crew: sweeping leaves (real brooms, child-size) into piles along the rug path, carrying litter to bins with grabbers, and watering our class plant with a small can.
Materials: Child-size brooms; grabbers; bins; watering can
Grouping: Small groups — rug and plant corner; teacher-supervised
Support: Sponges instead of brooms available for children who find long handles hard to manage.

Technology — Goal: See real town workers doing their jobs (teacher-selected video).
Activity: We will watch short teacher-selected clips of real town workers — a librarian reading to children, a road crew fixing a street — and match each clip to its role card.

Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Clips bookmarked and captioned; front seating for children following the captions with the teacher's pointing.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Care for a real shared outdoor space.
Activity: We will do a real caretaker walk: picking up litter on the playground with grabbers and gloves (teacher handles anything sharp or unknown), then washing hands and feeling proud of a cleaner park.

Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-supervised

Materials: Talking stone; question cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A turn with the talking stone shortened or passed with a smile — passing is always allowed.

Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led

Music / Movement — Goal: Perform our town parade in order with roles.
Activity: We will hold our town parade for real: flag first, then the band, then poster-carriers, marching one lap of the room while the class next door (or hallway staff) watches, and finish with a bow.

Grouping: Large group; teacher-led performance
Support: A marching spot in the middle of the line where the pace is steadiest.

Motor Activities — Goal: Cross a balance path and present an item with confidence.
Activity: Our closing obstacle course is 'Sofia's bridge': children cross the tape beam, carry a 'petition' clipboard to the town hall mat, present it with a bow, and lead the next friend across.

Grouping: Small groups — movement area; teacher-supervised
Support: A hand to hold across the 'bridge' beam for children still developing balance.

Technology — Goal: Narrate photos from our week in a class slideshow.
Activity: We will watch a slideshow of our leadership week — the flag, the meeting, the vote, the planting — and each child will narrate one photo in their own words, like news reporters of our own town.

Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Teacher runs the slideshow; children click the advance button when ready.

Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-supervised
Support: An adult escort and a simple one-item job list for children who need the task made concrete.

Activity: We will close the week by sharing our idea posters and naming the leadership in each one; the teacher will remind us that leaders are not the loudest — they are the ones who help.

Grouping: Large group — carpet; celebration circle
Support: The option to show their poster instead of speaking for children who prefer it.

title: Lunar New Year: Welcome, Lunar New Year!
subject: Social Studies
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Lunar New Year' thematic week (February): Welcome, Lunar New Year!. Focus book: Bringing In the New Year — Grace Lin. evidence:
Focus book: Bringing In the New Year — Grace Lin

Language Arts — Goal: Retell the events of a family's New Year preparations in order.
Activity: We will read how one family gets ready for the New Year — sweeping, cooking, wearing new clothes, watching fireworks — and build a 'getting ready' sequence chart from the story.
Materials: Focus book; sequence picture cards; chart paper
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Picture support cards for each part of the celebration so every child can retell one part.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Observe a citrus fruit closely: peel, segments, smell, and float test.
Activity: Children will explore oranges and tangerines with their senses — peeling (with help), smelling, counting segments, and floating a whole fruit versus a peeled one in water to see what changes.
Materials: Tangerines (teacher-checked for allergies; observation only if needed); water tub; magnifiers
Grouping: Small groups — science table
Support: An adult near the water station and aprons for children sensitive to wet sleeves.

Social Science — Goal: Learn where and how families celebrate Lunar New Year.
Activity: We will learn, factually and warmly, that Lunar New Year is celebrated by families in China and in many countries and neighborhoods around the world, with special food, family visits, and wishes for good luck.
Materials: Simple world map; celebration picture cards; focus book
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Children may answer by pointing to pictures of the customs as we discuss them.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Count to 12 and compare which group has more.
Activity: Children will count out 12 paper tangerines into a gift basket (tangerines are a traditional gift symbol of good luck), then compare two baskets to find the one with more.
Materials: Paper tangerines; baskets; number cards
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: A counting strip to touch for children building one-to-one correspondence up to 15.

Creative Art — Goal: Create red-and-gold door banners with paint and stamps.
Activity: Children will brush or stamp gold paint designs onto red paper banner strips, as red and gold are colors families use to welcome luck and happiness, and hang them around our door.
Materials: Red paper strips; gold paint; stamp shapes; brushes
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Pre-folded banner strips for children who find folding frustrating; extra glue time.

Music / Movement — Goal: Play welcome rhythms and freeze in celebration poses.
Activity: We will drum a welcome rhythm on hand drums — slow beats for the sweeping, quick happy beats for the fireworks — and children will freeze in a 'firework burst' pose at the end of each pattern.
Materials: Hand drums; open rug space
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: Movements demonstrated slowly first, with space markers for children who need a defined area.

Motor Activities — Goal: Use tongs and hand-over-hand pulling to build hand strength.
Activity: Children will use tongs to move red pom-pom 'berries' and stretch long paper 'noodles' hand-over-hand from a bin (noodles stand for long life in many New Year meals), sorting them onto plates.
Materials: Tongs; pom-poms; paper noodle strips; plates
Grouping: Centers — sensory/fine motor area
Support: A seated noodle-pulling option at a table for children who prefer not to stand at the bin.

Technology — Goal: Watch real celebration footage and describe what people are doing.
Activity: We will watch short, teacher-selected clips of real lion dancers and lantern displays, pausing to notice the costumes, instruments, and crowds celebrating together.
Materials: Projector/screen; teacher-selected celebration clips
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Front-row seats and a printed photo of the dancers for children who need to look longer.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Hunt outdoors for colors and shapes of the celebration.
Activity: Outside, we will look for signs of early spring and celebration colors around the school — red doors, round shapes, new buds — checking them off a picture hunt list.
Materials: Picture hunt lists; clipboards
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: A short looking list (just two items: red, round) for children who need a simpler hunt.

Activity: Families clean the house before the New Year to sweep away the old and make room for the new. We will name one old habit to 'sweep away' (like leaving toys out) and one fresh start for our classroom.
Materials: Class broom prop; fresh-start chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A sticky-note option to place their idea on the chart without speaking in front of the group.

Support: Gentle-volume testing first, with adult help for children startled by pops.

Social Science — Goal: Learn the 12 zodiac animals as a counting cycle.
Activity: We will look at the 12 zodiac animals in order and play a matching game with the animal cards; the teacher will share, as a fun fact, that each year is named for one animal in the cycle.
Materials: Zodiac animal cards; wheel chart; year chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Children choose a favorite animal card to hold up rather than choosing 'their year' aloud.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Count and sequence 12 items on the zodiac wheel.
Activity: On our zodiac wheel, children will count the 12 animal pictures in order, find the animal card that matches each space, and say the number as they place it.
Materials: Zodiac wheel mat; 12 animal cards
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: Pairs share one wheel for children who enjoy counting and matching with a partner.

Creative Art — Goal: Make a friendly monster mask with collage.
Activity: Children will make a friendly (not scary) paper Nian mask collage — gluing on big kind eyes, paper horns, and colorful mane strips — while we remember the story's lesson that noise and light scared Nian away.
Materials: Paper plates; collage scraps; glue; crayons
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: A potato masher or sponge shape for stamping, easier to grip than a small stamp.

Music / Movement — Goal: Make celebration music together with percussion instruments.
Activity: With instruments in hand and volume kept kind, we will make a joyful New Year noise parade around the rug — drums, shakers, and cymbals — because noise is traditionally said to scare away bad luck.
Materials: Drums; shakers; cymbals; ear defenders available
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: Ear defenders available and a spot at the circle's edge for children sensitive to loud sounds.

Motor Activities — Goal: Move, bang, and freeze along a celebration parade path.
Activity: Children will build a 'village parade' path: banging pot-lid cymbals (gently, at stations), stepping over 'firecracker' ribbon lines, and freezing when the big drum booms — the noises that sent Nian away.
Materials: Pot lids; ribbons on floor; big drum
Grouping: Small groups — movement area; teacher-supervised
Support: A drum pad to hold in the lap for children who prefer a seated role in the parade practice.

Technology — Goal: Record and identify celebration sounds by ear.
Activity: Using the voice recorder, each group will record their parade sounds, and we will play them back and guess which instrument made each sound.
Materials: Voice recorder or tablet app; instruments
Grouping: Small groups; teacher-guided
Support: Teacher holds the recorder; children take turns pressing the big button with support if needed.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Listen outdoors and map the sounds we hear.
Activity: Outside, children will sit for one quiet minute and draw or mark every sound they hear on a sound map (birds, wind, traffic, voices), learning the listening side of celebration sounds.
Materials: Sound map sheets; clipboards; crayons
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: A sound-map partner for children who like to listen with a friend and point instead of writing.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Learn that facing fears is easier together — courage with friends.
Activity: Nian was frightening, but the villagers solved the problem together. We will talk about fears children really have (loud noises, the dark) and the kind helpers and tools that make us brave.
Materials: Feelings chart; focus book
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: The choice to name a tool ('I can cover my ears / ask for help') rather than the fear itself.

title: Lunar New Year: Feasts, Family, and Sharing
subject: Social Studies
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Lunar New Year' thematic week (February): Feasts, Family, and Sharing. Focus book: The Runaway Wok — Ying Chang Compestine. Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: The Runaway Wok — Ying Chang Compestine

Language Arts — Goal: Retell a cumulative story and notice its sharing ending.
Activity: We will read the funny story of a wok that collects the whole village's New Year treats, chart its journey, and notice the happy ending: everything it gathered was shared back with everyone.
Materials: Focus book; journey chart; food picture cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A story map with three picture boxes (went / collected / shared) to fill during the retell.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Shape playdough dumplings and compare folded foods in pictures.
Activity: Children will roll playdough 'dumplings' and pinch the edges closed (a traditional New Year food shape), then compare real foods that are folded, rolled, or round across cultures using picture cards — playdough only, no tasting activity.
Materials: Playdough; rolling pins; trays; food picture cards
Grouping: Small groups — art/science table
Support: Adult checks all items first; children with food allergies observe only and use the pretend set.

Social Science — Goal: Set a table and host a pretend family feast.
Activity: In the home corner, children will set a round pretend table for a family feast — plates all around so everyone faces each other — and take turns serving pretend dishes and greeting 'guests.'
Materials: Play dishes; pretend food; round table mat
Grouping: Centers — dramatic play; child-led
Support: Children may 'serve' a picture dish instead of pretending with food pieces, as preferred.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Sort and count pretend feast foods up to 15.
Activity: Children will sort pretend feast foods into the runaway wok by color, then count how many treats the wok 'collected' on each page of our counting chart.
Materials: Pretend food; big bowl 'wok'; counting chart
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: Sorting into just two pots for children building classification skills.

Creative Art — Goal: Paint a feast platter with a patterned rim.
Activity: Children will paint a big round paper-plate 'feast platter,' decorating the rim with repeated red-and-gold patterns and drawing favorite family foods in the middle.
Materials: Paper plates; paints; pattern examples
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: A sponge brush and a big paper plate for children building brush control.

Music / Movement — Goal: Repeat a rhythm pattern in a celebration dance.
Activity: We will learn a simple celebration rhythm — two claps, two drum hits, spin — repeating it as a class 'feast dance' and adding a freeze whenever the gong sound rings.
Materials: Hand drums; gong or cymbal sound; recorded festive music
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: A defined drum spot and predictable pattern for children who join routines best with repetition.

Motor Activities — Goal: Carry a tray steadily and toss into a target bowl.
Activity: Children will practice gentle 'serving' movements: carrying a tray with two hands along a path and tossing soft balls into the big wok bowl from a floor line.
Materials: Trays; soft balls; big bowl; floor line
Grouping: Small groups — movement area
Support: Lightweight scarves instead of balls for children building throwing accuracy.

Technology — Goal: Sequence feast-day photos and describe family work.
Activity: We will look at teacher-selected photos of families preparing New Year feasts in different homes, and children will match the photos to the steps: shop, cook, set the table, share.
Materials: Projector; prepared photo set; sequence cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Front seating and the recipe card printed large for children who need big text.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Find round, orange, and red things in nature.
Activity: On a 'market walk' around the school grounds and garden planters, children will look for round and orange things in nature (a la tangerines and lanterns) and collect fallen leaves to press as feast-table decorations.
Materials: Collection bags; picture hunt cards
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: A shorter list (3 fruits) and pictures for children who need the hunt simplified.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Practice sharing and gratitude at the table.
Activity: The runaway wok reminds us that celebrations are about sharing, not keeping. We will share one pretend treat from our dramatic-play table with a friend and say what we are thankful for at family meals.
Materials: Pretend food from centers; gratitude cards
Grouping: Pairs — dramatic play area
Support: Sentence starter ('I can share ___') with picture options for emerging speakers.

title: Lunar New Year: Dragons, Lions, and Parades
subject: Social Studies
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Lunar New Year' thematic week (February): Dragons, Lions, and Parades. Focus book: Dragon Dance — Joan Holub. Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: Dragon Dance — Joan Holub

Language Arts — Goal: Enjoy rhyming words and collect parade vocabulary.
Activity: After reading this rhyming parade story, we will chant its rhythm together, then sort picture words into 'things we saw in the parade' piles and add them to the word wall.
Materials: Focus book; parade picture cards; word wall
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A lift-the-flap copy to handle for children who engage through touch and surprise.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Explore shiny and sound-making materials of costumes.
Activity: Children will examine real objects that shine and shimmer like parade costumes — sequined fabric, foil, mirrors, and bells — sorting them by 'sparkly / not sparkly' and testing which ones jingle.
Materials: Fabric and foil samples; bells; hand mirrors; magnifiers
Grouping: Small groups — science table
Support: A large knob magnifier for children who need an easier grip.

Social Science — Goal: Practice being respectful watchers and careful marchers.
Activity: We will talk about parade manners — watchers wave and cheer, marchers keep their space — and practice being both: half the class parades with instruments while half waves, then we switch.
Materials: Class dragon; instruments; wave ribbons
Grouping: Large group — rug and hallway
Support: A buddy beside a confident stepper for children still learning parade marching.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Count dragon segments and make a number pattern to 15.
Activity: Children will count the segments of our paper dragon as we build it, then make number patterns along its body with dot stickers, counting by pointing to each segment.
Materials: Paper dragon segments; dot stickers; number cards
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: Bead strings with colors chunked in fives for children counting beyond 10.

Creative Art — Goal: Decorate dragon segments as a team art project.
Activity: In teams, children will decorate long paper dragon segments with tissue scales, shiny foil, and streamer whiskers, then we will join the segments into one class dragon for the parade.
Materials: Long paper segments; tissue paper; foil; streamers; glue
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Pre-cut scale shapes for children still building scissor skills; glue sticks instead of liquid glue.

Music / Movement — Goal: Play a parade rhythm with assigned instrument parts.
Activity: We will practice the parade beat: strong drum hits for the dragon's steps, cymbal crashes for turns, and a shaker roll for its waves, taking turns as the 'band' and the 'dragon.'
Materials: Drum; cymbals; shakers
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: Body percussion instead of instruments for children who prefer quieter sound-making.

Motor Activities — Goal: Move as a team while holding a shared object (dragon parade practice).
Activity: Holding our class dragon's segments overhead in a line, children will practice moving together — forward, turning a corner, dipping and rising — keeping the dragon's body in one piece.
Materials: Class paper dragon; open space
Grouping: Large group — gym/hallway space; teacher-led
Support: A spot near either end of the dragon, where movement is slower and steadier.

Technology — Goal: Photograph our parade and choose display photos.
Activity: Children will help the teacher photograph our dragon parade practice; we will choose the best three photos together for our door display and dictate a caption for each.
Materials: Class camera or tablet; display board
Grouping: Small groups; teacher-guided
Support: Teacher holds the camera; children decide the moment and say 'cheese' to direct.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Hold our own dragon parade outdoors.
Activity: Weather permitting, our dragon will parade around the playground with the instrument band behind, stopping at the 'lantern tree' for a class photo, celebrating like real parade watchers and marchers.
Materials: Class dragon; instruments; camera
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: A flag to carry at the parade's end for a child who wants to join without holding the dragon.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Learn that big things happen when a team moves together.
Activity: Dragons in the parade are friendly symbols of good luck, not scary monsters — and the dancers work as one team under the costume. We will talk about how the dragon only moves when everyone cooperates.
Materials: Focus book (dragon pages); team jobs chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A calming corner option and noise warnings before the parade practice.

title: Lunar New Year: Lanterns and New Year Wishes
subject: Social Studies
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Lunar New Year' thematic week (February): Lanterns and New Year Wishes. Focus book: Ruby's Chinese New Year — Vickie Lee. Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: Ruby's Chinese New Year — Vickie Lee

Language Arts — Goal: Compose a kind New Year wish for someone we love.
Activity: We will read about Ruby's journey to deliver a card to her grandmother, then each child will dictate or draw a New Year wish for someone they love on a wish card for our lantern display.
Materials: Focus book; wish cards; crayons
Grouping: Large group then writing/art tables
Support: A wish card with picture choices to complete for children not ready to dictate a full sentence.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Explore how light shines through lantern materials (translucent test).
Activity: Children will test what glows: holding translucent papers, leaves, and hands before a lamp and a battery candle, discovering which materials let light shine through like a lantern's paper.
Materials: Lamp; battery candles; paper samples; leaves
Grouping: Small groups — science table; teacher-led
Support: Battery candles only — no flame; adult handles all lights for safety.

Social Science — Goal: Review the week's celebration customs in order.
Activity: We will look back at our whole week on the photo timeline — cleaning, feasting, parading, wishing — and children will place the photos in order and tell a partner their favorite celebration moment.
Materials: Week photos; timeline board
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Picture timeline cards for children who need the week's events in pictures to order them.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Order numerals 1–12 on a lantern line.
Activity: Children will hang paper lanterns on our string in number order 1–12, counting aloud as each is clipped on, then find and fix any lantern 'out of line' the teacher sneaks in.
Materials: Paper lanterns with numerals; string; clothespins
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: A numbered lantern strip to match for children building number recognition.

Creative Art — Goal: Make and decorate a paper lantern.
Activity: Children will build their own paper lanterns: decorating a red sheet with gold patterns, folding with teacher help, and adding a tassel — then carrying them carefully in our closing parade.
Materials: Red paper; gold crayons and stickers; tassels; glue
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5; teacher-guided folding
Support: A pre-assembled lantern form to decorate for children who find multi-step folding hard.

Music / Movement — Goal: Perform a group dance with props for an audience.
Activity: With ribbons flowing, we will perform our ribbon dance for another class (or the hallway teachers), holding our lanterns for the final pose as the music ends.
Materials: Ribbons; lanterns; recorded music; guest audience
Grouping: Large group — rug; celebration performance
Support: A scarf with a wrist loop for children whose hands open and drop props easily.

Motor Activities — Goal: Perform a simple ribbon dance sequence.
Activity: Children will learn a simple fan-and-ribbon dance pattern — open, close, wave, turn — practicing the slow steps together until the movements flow with the music.
Materials: Ribbons or scarves; recorded gentle festive music
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: Steps done sitting with hands and shoulders only, for children who join movement in their own way.

Technology — Goal: Watch a lantern festival and describe light and color.
Activity: We will watch a short, teacher-selected lantern festival clip at 'night' — lights low, lanterns glowing around the room — and say one beautiful thing we noticed before the week ends.
Materials: Projector/screen; teacher-selected lantern clip; class lanterns
Grouping: Large group — carpet, lights low; teacher-led
Support: Front-row seating; the option to hold a soft lantern while watching.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Celebrate with an outdoor lantern parade.
Activity: We will end the week outdoors: hanging our paper lanterns along the fence (weather permitting) and parading with them around the playground, wishing 'Happy New Year' to classes we pass.
Materials: Paper lanterns; fence line; playground route
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: An adult hand on the parade route for children who need support walking with the group.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Share good wishes — kindness is the point of the celebration.
Activity: We will close the week like families do: sharing good wishes. Each child may read or show their wish card, and we will end by wishing our class a year of health, kindness, and good friends.
Materials: Wish cards; lantern display; feelings chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; celebration circle
Support: The teacher helps scribe any wish privately for children who prefer not to share aloud.

title: Migration and Hibernation / Shadows: Animals in Winter
subject: Science
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Migration and Hibernation / Shadows' thematic week (February): Animals in Winter. Focus book: Over and Under the Snow — Kate Messner. Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: Over and Under the Snow — Kate Messner

Language Arts — Goal: Retell what animals do in winter using new words: den, burrow, hibernate.
Activity: We will read about the hidden world under the snow, stopping to wonder what each animal is doing, and children will add one 'under the snow' idea to our class window chart.
Materials: Focus book; window chart; animal word cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Picture word cards (snow, sleep, den) for children building story vocabulary.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Explore where animals live and rest during winter.
Activity: Children will explore a big winter habitat mat with toy animals and decide where each animal spends winter: under the snow, in a den, in a tree, or gone far away — then check their ideas against a picture poster.
Materials: Winter habitat mat; toy animals; habitat poster
Grouping: Small groups — science table
Support: Picture labels for each zone for children who need the idea in pictures first.

Social Science — Goal: Work together to map where animals spend the winter.
Activity: We will build a class 'winter map' mural: children place animal stickers on the sky, trees, ground, or under a white paper 'snow blanket' where they think each animal stays.
Materials: Mural paper; animal stickers; white paper strips
Grouping: Large group then small groups — art wall
Support: A partner to decide placements with, using point-and-show communication.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Count winter animals to 10 and match numerals.
Activity: Children will count animal picture cards (fox, hare, deer, owl) and place matching numeral cards beside each set, then add one more animal to a set and recount.
Materials: Animal picture cards; numeral cards 1–10; ten-frames
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: A ten-frame to place animals on for children building counting structure.

Creative Art — Goal: Print animal tracks in clay to explore pattern and size.
Activity: Children will press animal-track stamps into white clay discs to make 'tracks in the snow,' choosing tracks of different sizes and comparing their prints.
Materials: White air-dry clay discs; track stamps; rollers
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Pre-cut tracks stamps with handles for children who need a sturdier grip.

Music / Movement — Goal: Move slowly and freeze on cue, like animals in a quiet snowy forest.
Activity: We will listen to a quiet winter song and sway like snowy trees, freezing still each time the wind sound stops, then tiptoe as quietly as animals walking on snow.
Materials: Recorded winter song with wind sounds; open rug
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: Slower animal choices for children who want gentle movement.

Motor Activities — Goal: Move the body in animal ways: hop, stomp, crawl, and scurry.
Activity: Children will move like winter animals along a floor path: hop like a hare, stomp like a moose, and scurry low like a mouse under the snow tunnel (a blanket over chairs).
Materials: Floor path spots; blanket tunnel over chairs
Grouping: Small groups — movement area; teacher-supervised
Support: A shorter, flatter path for children building confidence in locomotor skills.

Technology — Goal: Watch a short nature video and describe animal winter behaviors.
Activity: We will watch a short, teacher-selected nature clip of animals in winter (a bear entering its den, geese flying south) and name what we noticed the animals doing.
Materials: Projector/screen; teacher-selected nature clip
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Front-row seating and the option to hold a soft toy animal while watching.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Look for real signs of animals outside in winter.
Activity: Outside, we will look for real signs of animals: tracks in mud or snow, holes in trees, chewed twigs, and feathers, sketching one find in nature journals.
Materials: Nature journals; crayons; magnifiers
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: A teacher hand for icy or uneven patches, and a shorter observation spot for children who chill quickly.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Learn that resting is a healthy, natural part of life.
Activity: Like winter animals, people have seasons of busy and seasons of rest. We will take three slow breaths together and name the gentle feeling of resting under a warm 'blanket of snow.'
Materials: Cozy blanket demo; feelings chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A soft blanket spot at the edge of the rug for children who need a cozy boundary to settle.

title: Migration and Hibernation / Shadows: Who Migrates? Traveling Animals
subject: Science
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Migration and Hibernation / Shadows' thematic week (February): Who Migrates? Traveling Animals. Focus book: The Long Trip South — — a simple nonfiction picture book about geese, butterflies, and whales on the move (substitute any migration title on hand). Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: The Long Trip South — — a simple nonfiction picture book about geese, butterflies, and whales on the move (substitute any migration title on hand)

Language Arts — Goal: Learn the word 'migration' and describe a long animal journey.
Activity: After reading, we will trace with a finger the long journeys on our map — geese flying south, monarch butterflies drifting to warm hills — and learn the word 'migrate' with a hand-motion arrow.
Materials: Focus book; large simple map; journey arrows
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A world map with picture icons so every child can follow the journey without reading words.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Explore why animals migrate: food, warmth, and safety.
Activity: Children will guide paper butterflies along a felt path, stopping at cards (cold wind, warm sun, flowers) and deciding if the butterfly keeps going or rests, learning why timing and weather matter.
Materials: Felt path; paper butterflies; weather picture cards
Grouping: Small groups — science table
Support: Fewer butterflies per round (start with 3) and the weather cards shown as pictures.

Social Science — Goal: Compare journeys and talk about distance (near and far).
Activity: We will compare journeys on our map wall: which animal travels farthest — the goose, the butterfly, or the whale? Children will place yarn strings to show each route and stand back to compare lengths.
Materials: Map wall; yarn; animal journey cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Children choose their traveler card, or a teacher pairs them with a confident reader of pictures.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Create a simple pattern and count a group up to 12.
Activity: Children will build a 'flying V' with bird counters in a simple repeating pattern (two forward, one point), then count how many birds are in their whole flock.
Materials: Bird counters or paper birds; pattern mats
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: A completed example arrow to copy for children new to continuing patterns.

Creative Art — Goal: Layer paper feathers to make a bird wing collage.
Activity: Children will cut and glue paper-strip feathers onto a large paper goose wing, layering the strips in rows the way real feathers overlap.
Materials: Paper strips; large wing outlines; glue; feathers (craft)
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: A pre-drawn large bird outline for children who want to focus on the wing patterns.

Music / Movement — Goal: Move like migrating birds to music — float, swoop, and land.
Activity: Holding scarves as wings, children will float and swoop to flowing music, landing softly in 'warm meadow' hoops each time the music pauses.
Materials: Scarves; hula hoops; flowing recorded music
Grouping: Large group — rug and open space
Support: Scarves to hold for children who engage better with a prop in their hands.

Motor Activities — Goal: Follow a leader and move in a group pattern like a flock.
Activity: In 'flocks' of four, children will follow a leader around a chalk path, flapping arms slowly like wings on the straight parts and gliding on the curves, then switch leaders.
Materials: Chalk path; open space
Grouping: Small groups — gym/outdoor area; teacher-led
Support: A walking-lane option beside the flapping lane for children who prefer steady movement.

Technology — Goal: Use a simple map app to follow a migration path.
Activity: Using a teacher-guided globe/map app on the tablet, we will zoom from our town to the warm places geese visit, following the lit-up path with our eyes.
Materials: Tablet with map app; projector
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Teacher manages the globe; children point to where they think animals go.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Observe real birds outdoors and notice their movements.
Activity: Outside, we will watch the real sky and trees with cardboard binoculars for birds, and listen for calls, noting arrows on a clipboard each time a bird crosses the sky.
Materials: Cardboard binoculars; clipboards; tally sheets
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: Binocular roles assigned in pairs so every child gets a turn to look and to point.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Learn that traveling together and taking turns helps the whole group.
Activity: Geese take turns leading the flock and honk to encourage each other. We will talk about how our class flock helps too — taking turns at the front of the line and cheering friends on.
Materials: Focus book (flock page); class jobs chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A thumbs-up/down picture option to answer questions about working together.

title: Migration and Hibernation / Shadows: Hibernation — The Long Sleep
subject: Science
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Migration and Hibernation / Shadows' thematic week (February): Hibernation — The Long Sleep. Focus book: Bear Snores On — Karma Wilson. Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: Bear Snores On — Karma Wilson

Language Arts — Goal: Retell a story and join in a repeated phrase.
Activity: We will read about the bear who sleeps through a whole party in his den, sequencing the animal visitors as they arrive and joining in on the repeated line each time Bear snores on.
Materials: Focus book; animal visitor cards; sequence strip
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Picture choice cards for the friends (mouse, hare, badger) for children joining the retell by pointing.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Investigate how dens and fat keep animals warm (insulation experiment).
Activity: Children will wrap two toy bears — one in a plain box, one in a box stuffed with cotton and leaves — leave both near the cold window, and later feel which bear stayed 'cozier,' discovering insulation.
Materials: Two boxes; cotton and leaves; two toy bears
Grouping: Small groups — science table; teacher-guided
Support: Adult proximity and a simple then/next picture strip for the experiment steps.

Social Science — Goal: Pretend-play caring for a hibernating friend.
Activity: In dramatic play, children will host Bear's tea party from the story — setting cups, pouring pretend honey tea, and taking turns keeping 'Bear' (a big stuffed animal) comfortable in his den corner.
Materials: Play tea set; big stuffed bear; blankets; pretend food
Grouping: Centers — dramatic play; child-led
Support: Role cards with pictures so each child can hold and keep their job.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Count and match quantities to number cards up to 10.
Activity: Children will count acorns and pinecones into Bear's store cups to match number cards up to 10, helping our pretend bear 'save food' the way real animals do before the long sleep.
Materials: Acorns and pinecones (large, teacher-checked); cups; number cards
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: Number cards sorted in order for children to match rather than recall the sequence.

Creative Art — Goal: Create a den scene with collage materials.
Activity: Children will build a cozy den picture: a torn-paper cave, cotton-ball snow on top, and a sleeping bear sticker tucked inside, talking about what makes the den warm and dark.
Materials: Brown paper; cotton balls; bear stickers; glue; crayons
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: A glue brush in a pot (instead of a squeeze bottle) for children building hand control.

Music / Movement — Goal: Sing softly and move quietly — controlling volume and speed.
Activity: We will sing a soft, slow 'sleeping bear' lullaby-style song — volume shrinking verse by verse — then tiptoe around the sleeping 'bears' (stuffed animals) without waking them.
Materials: Teacher-led song; stuffed bears
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: A designated quiet corner of the rug for children who need the volume low throughout.

Motor Activities — Goal: Curl, stretch, and climb — moving like a bear waking up.
Activity: Children will curl up small in a 'den' hoop for a slow count, then wake and stretch tall, waddle like a bear across the mat, and climb over a soft 'log' to find pretend berries.
Materials: Hula hoops; mats; soft tunnel/log obstacle
Grouping: Small groups — movement area; teacher-supervised
Support: A balance partner and a wider 'log' tape line for children developing balance.

Technology — Goal: Listen to a recorded story and identify animals in order.
Activity: At the listening center, children will enjoy a recorded winter-animal story and tap the picture of each animal as they hear it named, practicing listening for details.
Materials: Listening center; recorded story; animal picture board
Grouping: Centers — pairs; child-led after setup
Support: Headphones for children who prefer to listen without room noise.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Find where fallen leaves pile up thick — nature's blanket.
Activity: We will gather fallen leaves on the playground to make a thick 'leaf blanket,' comparing spots where leaves pile deep (cozy for animals) and where the ground is bare and cold.
Materials: Collection bags; leaf identification card
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: A leaf-rubbing frame to hold paper steady for children working on coordination.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Learn that kindness can be quiet and ask for nothing back.
Activity: Bear's friends throw him a party even though he sleeps through it — they care without expecting anything back. We will share one quiet, kind thing we could do for someone in our class this week.
Materials: Focus book (party pages); feelings chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: The option to whisper the caring idea to the teacher instead of the whole group.

Investigate how dens and fat keep animals warm (insulation experiment)
Pretend-play caring for a hibernating friend

title: Migration and Hibernation / Shadows: Groundhog Day and Shadows
subject: Science
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Migration and Hibernation / Shadows' thematic week (February): Groundhog Day and Shadows. Focus book: Groundhog's Big Day — — a friendly groundhog picture book about shadows and the first peek of spring (substitute any Groundhog Day title on hand). Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: Groundhog's Big Day — — a friendly groundhog picture book about shadows and the first peek of spring (substitute any Groundhog Day title on hand)

Language Arts — Goal: Learn new words: shadow, prediction, tradition.
Activity: After our story, we will learn the tradition kindly and factually: each February 2nd, people watch a groundhog and make a playful prediction about spring — a fun custom, not real weather science. Children will share if they hope for spring or more snow days.
Materials: Focus book; word cards; calendar
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Two picture answer cards to choose from for children who need support forming sentences.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Explore how shadows are made and how they change size.
Activity: At the lamp station, children will move a toy groundhog closer to and farther from the light, watching its shadow grow and shrink, and test which objects make dark shadows and which let light through.
Materials: Desk lamp; toy groundhog; translucent and opaque objects
Grouping: Small groups — science table; teacher-led
Support: A step-by-step picture strip at the lamp station for children who need the routine in pictures.

Social Science — Goal: Observe seasonal change over time as a class project.
Activity: We will build a class 'signs of spring' board across the month: children add drawings as they spot buds, birds returning, or warmer days — checking back on our groundhog prediction fairly, with facts.
Materials: Spring watch board; drawing supplies
Grouping: Large group — carpet; ongoing display
Support: Extra explanation and the animal cards for children who need the idea repeated in game form.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Make and count predictions (more, fewer, equal).
Activity: On our class chart wheel, each child will clip a clothespin to 'yes' or 'no' for the prediction; we will count the clips and write the numbers to see how our class voted.
Materials: Prediction chart; clothespins; markers
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Pairs can share wheels and counts for children who need a counting partner.

Creative Art — Goal: Trace a shadow outline to make silhouette art.
Activity: Children will trace around a toy animal placed on paper near the lamp to draw its shadow outline, then color only the shadow gray-black and add the animal beside it.
Materials: Desk lamp; toy animals; paper; crayons
Grouping: Art center, small groups; teacher-supervised
Support: Pre-traced animal silhouettes for children whose hands tire with long tracing.

Music / Movement — Goal: Follow a song's cues to crouch, peek, and pop up.
Activity: We will sing a groundhog peek-a-boo song: crouch down in our 'burrows,' peek up on the chorus, and pop up or stay hiding depending on the verse's pretend shadow.
Materials: Teacher-led song; burrow mats
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: A floor marker showing exactly where to stand for children who need a clear spot.

Motor Activities — Goal: Copy body shapes like a shadow follows a person.
Activity: In pairs, one child makes big slow shapes with their body and the partner 'is the shadow,' copying from behind; when the leader freezes, the shadow freezes too.
Materials: Sunny wall or lamp-lit wall; open space
Grouping: Pairs — movement area; teacher-guided
Support: Shadows matched slowly with the teacher as partner for children learning to control big movements.

Technology — Goal: Use a tablet camera to capture shadows (teacher-guided).
Activity: Working with the teacher, children will photograph playground shadows with the class tablet; we will print two favorites and add them to our Shadow Detective board.
Materials: Class tablet; printer; detective board
Grouping: Small groups; teacher-guided
Support: Teacher holds the tablet while the child directs the shot, for careful device handling.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Find and observe real shadows outdoors and notice they change.
Activity: Outside on a sunny day, we will find our own long playground shadows, stand on a partner's shadow 'toes,' and chalk around a friend's shadow feet before the shadow 'moves away.'
Materials: Sidewalk chalk; sunny playground
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: A clipboard with larger shadow outlines to match for children whose drawing is emerging.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Practice being a good sport about guesses that turn out wrong.
Activity: Making a prediction means sometimes we are wrong — and that is fine. We will practice saying 'Good guess!' to friends either way, and record our class prediction in a sealed envelope to open in six weeks.
Materials: Envelope; prediction card; class calendar
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A smaller recording job (holding the class camera timer) for children who want a role without the spotlight.

title: Migration and Hibernation / Shadows: Shadow Detectives
subject: Science
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Migration and Hibernation / Shadows' thematic week (February): Shadow Detectives. Focus book: Moonbear's Shadow — Frank Asch. Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: Moonbear's Shadow — Frank Asch

Language Arts — Goal: Predict and explain why a character's plan did not work.
Activity: We will read about Bear trying to get away from his shadow, predicting each new idea he tries, and finishing by acting out how Bear finally makes peace with his shadow at sunset.
Materials: Focus book; prediction cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Prediction picture cards ('He will run / He will fish / He will climb') to answer by pointing.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Investigate light: which materials block it and which let it pass.
Activity: Children will experiment with flashlights in our darkened science corner: shining through hands, leaves, and clear cups, and discovering which materials block light completely.
Materials: Flashlights; leaves; clear cups; fabric; darkened corner
Grouping: Small groups — science corner; teacher-guided
Support: A personal small flashlight so a child can work at their own pace beside the group.

Social Science — Goal: Teach a friend something you discovered — sharing learning.
Activity: Children will become shadow teachers: each pair demonstrates one shadow discovery (growing shadows, copying shadows, sun shadows) to another pair, using their shadow puppet or toy animal.
Materials: Shadow puppets; toy animals; lamp
Grouping: Pairs teaching pairs — rug
Support: An adult nearby to introduce a shy child's idea to the partner pair.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Compare and order shadows by length.
Activity: Children will order three shadow cards from shortest to longest, then stand three toy animals in a row and do the same with their real shadows at the lamp.
Materials: Shadow length cards; toy animals; lamp
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: A pre-marked sorting line for children who need the comparison made visible.

Creative Art — Goal: Make a final shadow artwork for our class show.
Activity: For our Shadow Art Show, children will trace a friend's hand shadow on dark paper and cut or tear the shape out (teacher pre-cuts for safety as needed), mounting it under the real handprint.
Materials: Dark paper; flashlights; glue; display board
Grouping: Art center, small groups; teacher-guided
Support: Hand-over-hand tracing help and a chunky marker for children building grip endurance.

Music / Movement — Goal: Review the week's movements in a final dance celebration.
Activity: We will revisit favorite songs from the week — bird swoops and bear tiptoes — and end with a shadow freeze dance, copying the teacher's shadow shapes on the wall.
Materials: Recorded music; lamp for wall shadows
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: A slower track choice and sitting_shadow option at the rug's edge for children who need less motion.

Motor Activities — Goal: Hop and land inside target shapes with control.
Activity: On the movement path, children will hop inside a chain of taped 'shadow footprints,' matching their feet to the prints, then freeze in the pose of the final shadow picture.
Materials: Taped shadow footprints; pose cards
Grouping: Small groups — movement area
Support: A defined follow path with footstep markers for children who need the route shown clearly.

Technology — Goal: Review and narrate our shadow photos as a class slideshow.
Activity: We will watch the week's shadow photos as a slideshow and children will narrate what each team found, then vote for the photo to print for our classroom door.
Materials: Tablet/projector; week's shadow photos
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Front-row seating for children who need the screen close.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Go on a shadow scavenger hunt and check off finds.
Activity: On our final shadow walk, teams will hunt a checklist of shadows: a tree shadow, a fence shadow, a long shadow, a round shadow — ticking each off and ending back at our meeting spot to share the best find.
Materials: Shadow hunt checklists; clipboards; pencils
Grouping: Whole class in teams — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: Partner pairing with a confident shadow-spotter; hats for children sensitive to glare.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Name a frustration and practice a calming strategy.
Activity: We will close the week talking about big feelings like frustration: Bear was annoyed by his shadow, and we can be annoyed by things we cannot change — and we can breathe, laugh, and carry on like Bear did.
Materials: Feelings chart; focus book
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: The chance to draw the feeling instead of telling it, for children who communicate best that way.

title: Post Office & Letter Writing (Preschool Unit)
subject: ELA / Reading
description: A 5-day preschool thematic unit on Post Office & Letter Writing (February), written as an Almanac Original. Each day is a full plan — literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor, technology, outdoor learning, and a life lesson — with goals, materials, groupings, and support strategies, plus four standing centers for the week. Days: Day 1: What Is Mail?; Day 2: Writing a Letter; Day 3: Stamps, Envelopes, and Addresses; Day 4: The Mail Carrier's Route; Day 5: Our Classroom Post Office Opens. Focus books: The Mail Must Go Through; The Jolly Postman; Dear Juno; A Day with the Mail Carrier; A Letter to Amy.

title: Post Office & Letter Writing: What Is Mail?
subject: ELA / Reading
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Post Office & Letter Writing' thematic week (February): What Is Mail?. Focus book: The Mail Must Go Through — — a simple nonfiction picture book showing how a letter travels from mailbox to doorstep (substitute any post office title on hand). Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: The Mail Must Go Through — — a simple nonfiction picture book showing how a letter travels from mailbox to doorstep (substitute any post office title on hand)

Language Arts — Goal: Learn letter words: envelope, stamp, address, mailbox.
Activity: We will read about how mail travels, then examine real (teacher-sanitized) mail together — envelope, stamp, address — naming each part on a big labeled envelope poster.
Materials: Focus book; sample envelopes; labeled envelope poster
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Real junk-mail pieces to hold and point to for children building print awareness.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Explore different papers: thick, thin, strong, and delicate.
Activity: Children will investigate paper with magnifiers: thick card, thin tissue, crinkly tracing paper — tearing a tiny corner of scrap to see fibers, and feeling which papers are strong enough for a rainy mailbox.
Materials: Paper samples; magnifiers; spray bottle of water for demos
Grouping: Small groups — science table
Support: Adult proximity and magnifiers for the whole group so everyone can join the close looking.

Social Science — Goal: Sequence how a letter travels from sender to receiver.
Activity: We will build a journey chart together — writer, mailbox, mail truck, post office, carrier, friend's door — and children will place a letter card along the path as we tell the story of one letter's trip.
Materials: Journey picture cards; chart; letter card
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Photo cards for children who need the jobs shown in pictures as we talk.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Sort mail by one attribute and count each group.
Activity: Children will sort a pile of pretend mail by color of envelope, count each stack, and stick the right numeral card on top of each pile.
Materials: Pretend envelopes in 3 colors; sorting mats; numeral cards
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: Two sets only for children building sorting stamina; the color rule shown on a card.

Creative Art — Goal: Decorate an envelope and make a name mark.
Activity: Children will decorate big paper envelopes with drawings and stickers — the first mail art of our week — and sign their name or name mark on the back flap.
Materials: Large paper envelopes; crayons; stickers
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Pre-drawn envelope outlines for children who find drawing the rectangle frustrating.

Music / Movement — Goal: March in time and stop on a visual cue.
Activity: We will sing a marching mail song ('Here comes the mail') as children walk the rug road carrying letters, freezing each verse to 'post' their letter when the mailbox picture is held up.
Materials: Teacher-led song; rug road tape; mailbox picture card
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: A mailbox prop to hold and post at their own speed for children who need a slower round.

Motor Activities — Goal: Carry and post oversized letters through a mail slot.
Activity: Children will play 'Post It': carrying one big soft envelope at a time, they walk the taped route and post it through the wide slot of our floor mailbox without bending the corners.
Materials: Big soft envelopes; floor mailbox with wide slot; floor tape route
Grouping: Small groups — movement area
Support: A larger target mailbox and a shorter standing distance for children building aiming skills.

Technology — Goal: Follow a recorded letter story with print in hand.
Activity: At the listening center, children will listen to a recorded read-aloud of a letter story and follow the printed postcard pages, turning at the chime.
Materials: Listening center; recorded story; printed postcard pages
Grouping: Centers — pairs; child-led after setup
Support: Volume-limited headphones and a big-print postcard page for the listening center.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Find a real mailbox and notice address numbers outdoors.
