title: Pets: Our Pet Parade and Show
subject: Social Studies
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Pets' thematic week (March): Our Pet Parade and Show. Focus book: Pet Show! — Ezra Jack Keats. Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: Pet Show! — Ezra Jack Keats

Language Arts — Goal: Introduce a pet to an audience with a name and a detail.
Activity: We will read how Archie enters his cat in the pet show, and then rehearse our own presentations: each child practices introducing their (stuffed or drawn) pet with its name and one best thing.
Materials: Focus book; stuffed/drawn pets; presentation frame cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A sentence frame ('My pet is best at ___') and their rosette to hold while presenting.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Review the week's pet-care learning with a checklist.
Activity: For our final review, children will 'certify' their stuffed pet's care: checking our week's care chart (food, water, shelter, gentle hands) against their pet home and adding anything missing — scientists checking their work.
Materials: Care checklists; pet homes from earlier in the week
Grouping: Small groups — around the room
Support: A picture checklist so children can verify their pet's needs by matching images.

Social Science — Goal: Present work and be a kind, attentive audience.
Activity: Our class pet show opens: children present in a friendly order (teacher hosts), classmates ask one kind question each, and everyone receives their rosette to warm applause — practicing being a good audience.
Materials: Stuffed/drawn pets; rosettes; comment star cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; celebration event
Support: Comment cards with a star stamp so every child can leave kind feedback without writing.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Count and sort award ribbons to match a group size.
Activity: We will award everyone at our pet show: children will count the ribbons and rosettes, sort them by color, and make sure the count matches our number of 'pets' so every entry gets one.
Materials: Paper ribbons/rosettes; stuffed pets; counting mat
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Counting with a cheerful partner and ribbons sorted by color first for children building stamina.

Creative Art — Goal: Make an award rosette for a pet's best quality.
Activity: Children will craft award rosettes with layered paper circles and streamer tails, writing or drawing their pet's 'best thing' in the center, for this afternoon's show.
Materials: Paper circles; streamers; glue; crayons
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Pre-made rosette centers for children whose hands tire with folding.

Music / Movement — Goal: Parade and perform a pet trick in a movement celebration.
Activity: Our celebration is a pet parade dance: children parade with stuffed pets to bouncy music, freeze for 'judging,' show their pet's trick (a spin, a bow), and parade on.
Materials: Recorded bouncy music; stuffed pets; rosettes
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: A ribbon wand instead of a pet to carry for children who want hands freer for dancing.

Motor Activities — Goal: Walk a show ring with posture and a pose stop.
Activity: Children will walk the pet show ring: a slow lap of the tape oval carrying their stuffed pet proudly, stopping at the judge's mat to pose, then trotting the short home stretch.
Materials: Tape oval; judge's mat; stuffed pets
Grouping: Small groups — movement area; teacher-supervised
Support: A wide tape path and a stuffed pet that can be carried in two arms for stability.

Technology — Goal: Photograph our pet show and narrate the slideshow.
Activity: Children will help photograph the pet show with the class tablet — one portrait per pet with its rosette — and we will watch the slideshow to close the week, narrating each pet's award.
Materials: Class tablet; projector
Grouping: Large group; teacher-guided
Support: Teacher holds the camera while children frame and direct each photo.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Hold our pet show parade outdoors.
Activity: Weather permitting, our pet show moves outdoors: families of stuffed pets will circle the playground ring, and we will finish with a picnic-blanket 'audience' story time under the tree.
Materials: Stuffed pets; rosettes; blanket; focus book for reread
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: An adult shadow for the ring walk for children who need a partner nearby.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Celebrate that everyone has something to be 'best' at.

title: Restaurants: Welcome to Our Restaurant
subject: Social Studies
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Restaurants' thematic week (March): Welcome to Our Restaurant. Focus book: Froggy Eats Out — Jonathan London. Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: Froggy Eats Out — Jonathan London

Language Arts — Goal: Identify print that carries meaning in the environment (signs and menus).
Activity: We will read the focus book and laugh about Froggy's silly table manners, then hunt through our classroom restaurant for words and pictures that tell people something — the OPEN sign, the menu, and the specials board.
Materials: Focus book; menu samples; OPEN sign; chart paper
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Picture-and-word cards for children who are just beginning to connect print with meaning.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Use the senses to describe foods by color, smell, and texture.
Activity: Children will explore a tray of real fruits and vegetables, describing how each looks, smells, and feels, and we will chart their describing words under 'crunchy,' 'smooth,' and 'bumpy.'
Materials: Washed produce tray; magnifiers; sense-words chart
Grouping: Small groups — science table; teacher-guided
Support: Smell and look only, no tasting, for children with food sensitivities; words offered on picture cards.

Social Science — Goal: Name the jobs people do in a restaurant.
Activity: We will look at photos of a real restaurant and match job cards — cook, server, cashier, dishwasher, host — to what each person does, and talk about how the jobs fit together.
Materials: Restaurant photo set; job picture cards; pocket chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Partner rehearsal before whole-group answers so every child has an idea ready.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Count out sets to match a numeral up to 10.
Activity: Children will 'set the table' by counting paper plates, cups, and napkins onto placemats printed with numerals, checking that each setting matches its number card.
Materials: Placemats; paper plates and cups; napkins; numeral cards
Grouping: Centers — math area; child-led after demo
Support: A completed example setting to copy for children still building one-to-one counting.

Creative Art — Goal: Design and decorate a sign for a purpose.
Activity: Children will decorate a big sign for our classroom restaurant, choosing a name together first, then adding letters, shapes, and drawings of food around the words.
Materials: Cardboard sign; paint; markers; food picture cut-outs
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Chunky crayons and stencils for children who need support forming letters.

Music / Movement — Goal: Carry an object steadily while walking to a beat.
Activity: We will practice being careful servers: children walk a short path carrying a tray with a beanbag 'cup,' moving slowly when the music is slow and freezing when it stops so nothing 'spills.'
Materials: Trays; beanbags; recorded music
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: A lighter tray and a shorter path for children developing balance and grip.

Motor Activities — Goal: Strengthen hand muscles by squeezing sponges.
Activity: At the washing station, children will wash plastic dishes in soapy water, squeezing sponges over each dish — just like the dishwasher's job.
Materials: Water tub; mild soap; plastic dishes; sponges; towels
Grouping: Centers — sensory/science area; teacher-supervised
Support: A stool to reach comfortably and extra time at this popular station.

Technology — Goal: Listen to a recorded story and answer a question about it.
Activity: At the listening center, children will hear a recorded restaurant story and afterward tell their partner one job from the story they would like to try.
Materials: Listening center; recorded story; headphones; job cards
Grouping: Centers — pairs; child-led after setup
Support: Volume checked by the teacher first; a partner to share the listening with.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Observe signs and symbols in the world outside school.
Activity: On a short walk around the school grounds, children will spot signs (stop, exit, arrows, our school sign) and count how many signs we pass that give people information.
Materials: Clipboards; crayons; school grounds route
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: A buddy partner for the walk and a picture checklist of signs to look for.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Practice welcoming others warmly, like a good host.
Activity: We will talk about how a host makes guests feel welcome — a smile, a greeting, showing them where to go — and practice greeting a partner at our classroom door.
Materials: Feelings chart; doorway space
Grouping: Large group — carpet then doorway practice
Support: The option to wave or offer a high-five instead of speaking for shy children.

title: Restaurants: Taking Orders
subject: Social Studies
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Restaurants' thematic week (March): Taking Orders. Focus book: The Doorbell Rang — Pat Hutchins. Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: The Doorbell Rang — Pat Hutchins

Language Arts — Goal: Listen for details and recall who wanted what.
Activity: We will read the focus book and talk about sharing the cookies fairly, then play 'Waiter, Waiter': a child gives a two-item food order and a partner listens and repeats it back before 'serving' the play food.
Materials: Focus book; play food; order pads; pencils
Grouping: Large group then pairs — carpet/tables
Support: Picture order cards to point to for children building listening memory; start with one-item orders.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Sort foods by the part of the plant we eat.
Activity: Children will sort real and picture foods into roots (carrot), leaves (lettuce), fruits (apple), and seeds (peas), using a real carrot with its tops on to see the parts.
Materials: Carrot with tops; produce pictures; sorting mats
Grouping: Small groups — science table
Support: Two sorting choices at a time for children who need a smaller field.

Social Science — Goal: Practice polite requesting and thanking in a pretend setting.
Activity: In the restaurant center, children will practice the words servers and guests use: 'May I take your order?' 'I would like..., please,' and 'Thank you,' with the teacher modeling first at a demo table.
Materials: Restaurant center set; menus; order pads
Grouping: Centers — dramatic play; teacher models, then child-led
Support: Sentence-frame cards at the table for children who need help starting a request.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Write and count orders using tally marks to 10.
Activity: Servers will take class orders for two snack choices at morning meeting, tallying each request on the chart, and we will count the tallies to see which choice our class ordered most.
Materials: Chart paper; order pad; markers
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A tally partner to count with for children unsure of grouping by fives.

Creative Art — Goal: Make a menu by combining pictures, print, and prices.
Activity: Each child will create a page for our class menu: draw a dish, write or dictate its name, and add a price using numeral stamps, then we will staple the pages into one big menu.
Materials: Paper; markers; numeral stamps; food magazines for ideas
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Numeral stamp set and a name card to copy for children working on writing their words.

Music / Movement — Goal: Follow a sequence of movements in a song (first, then, last).
Activity: We will act out making a sandwich to music — spread, stack, slice, serve — freezing between steps while the teacher calls them out of order to check who's listening.
Materials: Recorded music; step picture cards
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: Step cards placed on the floor as a path to follow for visual support.

Motor Activities — Goal: Use a pincer grasp to pick up and place small items.
Activity: Children will use tweezers to move pom-pom 'grapes' and 'peas' from a serving bowl onto plates, filling each plate to match the number on its order ticket.
Materials: Tweezers; pom-poms; bowls; plates; number tickets
Grouping: Centers — fine motor table
Support: Easy-squeeze tongs and larger pom-poms for children developing grasp strength.

Technology — Goal: Record and play back our own voices with a purpose.
Activity: Using the class voice recorder, children will record their restaurant greeting or their order, then listen back and say what they hear themselves saying clearly.
Materials: Voice recorder or tablet recording app; quiet corner
Grouping: Small groups; teacher-guided
Support: A partner to record with and as many tries as needed — no first-take pressure.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Deliver 'orders' while navigating an outdoor path.
Activity: Outside, children will carry a covered tray from the 'kitchen' cone to the 'table' cone along a chalk path, walking heel-to-toe on the line when the path narrows.
Materials: Cones; chalk path; trays with lids; beanbags
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors, in small groups
Support: A wider chalk path and a walking partner for children building balance.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Learn that listening carefully is a way to be kind.
Activity: We will talk about how the children in our story listened and shared so everyone was included, and practice 'whole-body listening' — eyes watching, ears listening, body still — for our next read-aloud.
Materials: Focus book; listening rules poster
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Specific praise naming exactly what careful listening looked like.

title: Restaurants: In the Kitchen
subject: Social Studies
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Restaurants' thematic week (March): In the Kitchen. Focus book: Pancakes, Pancakes! — Eric Carle. Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: Pancakes, Pancakes! — Eric Carle

Language Arts — Goal: Retell a process in sequence using first, then, next, and finally.
Activity: After reading how the pancake gets made step by step, children will arrange recipe-step cards in order and retell the process, noticing how many steps come before eating.
Materials: Focus book; recipe-step cards; pocket chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Fewer step cards (four) for children building sequencing skills, with the book open for reference.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Observe how dry and wet ingredients change when mixed.
Activity: Children will explore flour and water at the science table — touching the dry flour, adding water spoon by spoon, and describing how the mixture changes to a paste (no eating; hands washed before and after).
Materials: Flour; water; bowls; spoons; smocks; hand-washing supplies
Grouping: Small groups — science table; teacher-supervised
Support: Gluten-free rice flour option and a stirring tool instead of hands for children who avoid textures or have sensitivities.

Social Science — Goal: Understand that food comes from many places and people before it reaches a kitchen.
Activity: We will trace one pancake ingredient — flour — backward on a picture path: bakery, truck, mill, farm, wheat field — and thank each worker along the way.
Materials: Picture path cards; world map or globe
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: The path stays on display so children can retrace it with a partner later.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Use measuring cups to compare amounts (more, less, equal).
Activity: At the 'kitchen math' station, children will fill recipe cards that call for cups of pretend ingredients (dry beans), counting scoops and comparing two bowls to say which has more.
Materials: Measuring cups; dry beans; bowls; recipe cards
Grouping: Centers — math/science area; child-led after demo
Support: Recipe cards with picture amounts for pre-readers; spill tray under the work.

Creative Art — Goal: Use printmaking with kitchen tools to make patterns.
Activity: Children will print with potato mashers, fork tines, and cup rims dipped in paint, naming the shape each tool leaves and choosing their favorite print.
Materials: Kitchen tools (clean); washable paint; large paper; smocks
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Tools with built-in handles and a shallow paint tray for more control.

Music / Movement — Goal: Keep a rhythm while pretending to cook.
Activity: We will chant and move through a cooking rhythm — stir the pot (big arm circles), flip the pancake (jump and turn), pour the milk (tip side to side) — speeding up and slowing down together.
Materials: Teacher-led chant; open rug space
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: A seated version of each motion for children who need it, keeping the same rhythm.

Motor Activities — Goal: Build wrist strength and coordination by pouring without spilling.
Activity: Children will pour water from a small pitcher into cups up to a marked line at the pouring station, practicing the slow wrist control cooks use (water only; towels ready).
Materials: Small pitchers; cups with fill lines; tray; towels
Grouping: Centers — practical life area; teacher-supervised
Support: A lighter, half-full pitcher and a funnel for children building pouring control.

Technology — Goal: Use a digital timer to understand waiting and turns.
Activity: We will use the class visual timer during our kitchen centers so children can see how long something 'cooks' and when their turn ends, practicing checking the timer themselves.
Materials: Visual countdown timer (tablet or standalone)
Grouping: Centers — guided by teacher at start
Support: A personal sand timer for children who find the big timer hard to track.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Carry and sort natural 'ingredients' on a garden hunt.
Activity: Outside, children will gather fallen natural items — leaves, sticks, pebbles (no picking live plants, nothing goes in mouths) — and sort their 'ingredients' by kind at our outdoor table.
Materials: Baskets; sorting trays; outdoor table
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors, in small groups
Support: A shorter hunt area near the door for children who tire quickly.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Practice patience while waiting for something we want.
Activity: We will talk about how the boy in our story had to wait through many steps before his pancake, and practice a waiting strategy together — count slowly, watch kindly, ask 'Is it ready yet?' just once.
Materials: Focus book; feelings chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A fidget option during waiting practice for children who find stillness hard.

title: Restaurants: Paying and Money
subject: Social Studies
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Restaurants' thematic week (March): Paying and Money. Focus book: A Chair for My Mother — Vera B. Williams. evidence:
Focus book: A Chair for My Mother — Vera B. Williams

Language Arts — Goal: Connect story events to a goal the characters work toward.
Activity: We will read how a family saves coins in a jar after the waitress mother brings them home, and chart how the jar fills over the story; children will share one thing they would save up for and why.
Materials: Focus book; chart paper; jar picture
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Thinking time with a partner before sharing with the whole group.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Investigate coins safely: observe, sort, and rub (no money in mouths).
Activity: Children will examine real coins with magnifiers (washed hands after), sort them by size and color, and make crayon rubbings to see the pictures pressed on each coin.
Materials: Real coins (teacher's set); magnifiers; paper; crayons
Grouping: Small groups — science table; teacher-led
Support: Oversize play coins for children who still mouth materials.

Social Science — Goal: Understand that people earn money by doing jobs and use it to buy things.
Activity: We will follow a paper dollar on its trip: the cook earns it, spends it at the market, the market pays the farmer — passing the dollar child to child as we act out the trip.
Materials: Large play dollar; job and shop picture cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A picture strip of the dollar's trip to follow along during the telling.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Count pennies to match a price up to 10 cents.
Activity: In our classroom store, menu items have prices of 1–10 pennies; children will count out the right number of pennies to 'buy' a snack card and check their count with a partner cashier.
Materials: Play pennies; priced menu cards; cash register toy
Grouping: Centers — math/dramatic play; child-led after demo
Support: A ten-frame mat to count pennies onto for children building accuracy.

Creative Art — Goal: Design play money with symbols and numerals.
Activity: Children will design their own class dollars — drawing a food picture in the middle and writing numerals in the corners — to use in our restaurant this week.
Materials: Green paper rectangles; markers; numeral stamps
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Numeral stamps provided so design, not numeral formation, is the focus.

Music / Movement — Goal: March and stop on cue while carrying 'coins.'
Activity: Children will march in a parade line carrying a beanbag 'coin jar,' freezing when the music stops and shaking their jars (beanbag rattles) only when the music plays.
Materials: Clear jars with beanbags inside (sealed); recorded marching music
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: A spot near the teacher in line for children who need a model close by.

Motor Activities — Goal: Use finger strength to pick up coins one at a time and drop them in a slot.
Activity: Children will feed play coins into bank slots, using just their fingers, then shake and count how many they saved; slots get narrower for a challenge round.
Materials: Play coins; banks with slots; counting mats
Grouping: Centers — fine motor table
Support: A wide-slot bank and chunky coins for children developing finger control.

Technology — Goal: Use a toy register/scanner to connect numbers with actions.
Activity: Children will scan barcoded menu cards at the register, hear the beep, and match the price that appears to the numeral on the card, with the teacher guiding the first rounds.
Materials: Toy scanner/register; barcoded menu cards; play money
Grouping: Centers — dramatic play; teacher-guided intro
Support: Fewer cards in the pile (prices 1–5) for children new to numeral matching.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Cooperate to transport 'groceries' along a relay path.
Activity: Outside, teams will carry one soft grocery item at a time from the 'store' to the 'restaurant' along our path, practicing careful hands and waiting for their turn at the start line.
Materials: Soft play groceries; baskets; cones marking the path
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-supervised
Support: Carrying two-handed items and a shorter path for children who need a quicker success.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Understand saving and waiting for something that matters to the whole family.
Activity: We will revisit the jar in our story and talk about how everyone helped fill it; children will name one way they can help at home that doesn't cost money, like setting the table.
Materials: Focus book (jar pages); chart paper
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Picture choices of helping jobs for children who can't think of one to say.

subject: Social Studies
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Restaurants' thematic week (March): Our Class Restaurant Opens. Focus book: Curious George Makes Pancakes — Margret and H. A. Rey. Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: Curious George Makes Pancakes — Margret and H. A. Rey

Language Arts — Goal: Use new theme vocabulary in pretend play (order, menu, special, check).
Activity: Before our restaurant opens, we will review our class menu and practice reading it together; during the opening, children will use the menu to order and to tell guests what today's special is.
Materials: Class menu (from Day 2); focus book for a closing read
Grouping: Large group then centers — dramatic play
Support: A menu copy with picture cues for every item so all children can 'read' it.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Plan and carry out a simple taste-free smell investigation.
Activity: Children will predict which covered smell jar (cinnamon, lemon peel, vanilla, mint leaf) is which using only their noses, then check and record their guesses with stickers (smell only — no tasting).
Materials: Covered smell jars; prediction cards; stickers
Grouping: Small groups — science table; teacher-supervised
Support: The choice to observe a partner's turn instead for children sensitive to strong smells.

Social Science — Goal: Take on a community role and cooperate to run our restaurant.
Activity: Today our restaurant is open: children will choose job badges — host, server, cook, cashier — and run the restaurant for classmates in two seatings, switching jobs halfway so everyone tries two roles.
Materials: Job badges; menus; order pads; play food; register; class dollars
Grouping: Whole class in two groups — dramatic play; teacher facilitates
Support: Job choice cards with pictures and a teacher-held 'helper' role for children who want to join alongside an adult.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Count and compare the day's 'sales' using a picture graph.
Activity: After the restaurant closes, we will count how many of each dish was ordered using the order tickets, graph the results with stickers, and find which dish was ordered most and fewest.
Materials: Collected order tickets; graph paper; stickers
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Counting in pairs with a five-frame for children who need the structure.

Creative Art — Goal: Create table decorations for a celebration meal.
Activity: Children will fold and decorate paper placemats for our restaurant tables, adding a drawn 'plate' in the center and patterns around the border.
Materials: Large paper; markers; pattern stampers
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Pre-folded placemats for children who find the folding step frustrating.

Music / Movement — Goal: Perform a welcoming song with actions for our guests.
Activity: We will sing our practiced restaurant welcome song — greeting, seating, serving, thanking — with hand motions, performing it to open our class restaurant.
Materials: Teacher-led song; action cards
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: A place holding the welcome sign for children who prefer not to sing.

Motor Activities — Goal: Set a real table correctly: one plate, cup, and napkin per setting.
Activity: Children will set our snack table using a placemat outline as a guide, placing each item in its spot for their classmates — real practice with a real purpose (teacher handles all food).

Support: The option to show a badge or photo instead of speaking for children who prefer it.

title: Our Earth: Our Beautiful Earth
subject: Science
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Our Earth' thematic week (April): Our Beautiful Earth. Focus book: The Earth Book — Todd Parr. Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: The Earth Book — Todd Parr

Language Arts — Goal: Describe favorite things in nature using describing words.
Activity: We will read the focus book and start a chart called 'Things We Love About Our Earth.' Each child will draw one favorite thing (a tree, the ocean, a flower) and dictate a describing sentence for our chart.
Materials: Focus book; chart paper; drawing paper; crayons
Grouping: Large group then independent — carpet/tables
Support: A picture word bank (sun, tree, water, flower) for children to point to when choosing what to draw.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Use senses and tools to observe natural materials closely.
Activity: Children will explore a discovery tray of soil, smooth stones, bark, and leaves with magnifiers. We will sort our finds into 'once alive' and 'never alive' and share one thing we noticed.
Materials: Discovery tray; magnifiers; natural materials; sorting mats
Grouping: Small groups — science table
Support: Larger magnifiers with handles and a partner to explore with for children who need support.

Social Science — Goal: Identify people whose jobs care for the Earth.
Activity: We will look at picture cards of Earth helpers — gardeners, park rangers, recycling workers, farmers — and match each helper to the tool they use. Children will name one job they would like to try.
Materials: Helper and tool picture cards; pocket chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Partner talk before sharing, so every child rehearses an answer first.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Count natural objects one-to-one up to 10.
Activity: Children will count collections of leaves, stones, and sticks onto numbered mats, then line their mats up in order and find which collection has the most.
Materials: Leaves; stones; sticks; number mats 1–10
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: A number-line strip on the table for children who need a visual anchor while counting.

Creative Art — Goal: Use collage to represent the Earth.
Activity: Children will glue blue and green tissue paper onto a large paper circle to make our planet, pressing and overlapping pieces to show oceans and land.
Materials: Paper circles; tissue paper; glue sticks; trays
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Pre-cut tissue pieces and a glue sponge for children still building hand strength.

Music / Movement — Goal: Move like living things in nature in response to music.
Activity: We will listen to gentle nature music and move as the teacher calls out: grow like a flower, sway like a tree, flutter like a butterfly, and freeze like a stone.
Materials: Recorded nature music; open rug space
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: A personal space spot marked on the rug for children who need a clear boundary.

Motor Activities — Goal: Strengthen hand muscles by squeezing and pouring.
Activity: Children will water our class plant using small pitchers and squeeze spray bottles, aiming carefully at the soil and taking turns being the plant helper.
Materials: Class plant; small pitchers; spray bottles; water tray
Grouping: Small groups — science area; teacher-supervised
Support: Two-hand squeeze bottles and a marked fill line for children building control.

Technology — Goal: Use a digital microscope to see natural objects up close.
Activity: With the teacher, small groups will place a leaf and a stone under the digital microscope and describe the patterns and lines they see on the screen.
Materials: Digital microscope; leaves; stones; screen
Grouping: Small groups; teacher-led
Support: Teacher places the object while the child directs where to look next, for children still learning to handle equipment.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Observe and record living things in our schoolyard.
Activity: On a nature walk we will look for living things without picking them — birds, bugs, plants, trees. Children will make tally marks on their clipboards each time they spot something alive.
Materials: Clipboards; tally sheets; pencils; playground
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: Buddy pairs so no child walks and records alone.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Feel and show gratitude for the Earth.
Activity: We will close circle by each naming one thing about the Earth we are thankful for, and the teacher will record our thanks on a leaf shape for a gratitude tree display.
Materials: Paper leaves; marker; display branch or board
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Picture choices (water, trees, animals, sun) to point to for children who find speaking in the group hard.

title: Our Earth: Reduce, Reuse, Recycle
subject: Science
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Our Earth' thematic week (April): Reduce, Reuse, Recycle. Focus book: Michael Recycle — Ellie Bethel. evidence:
Focus book: Michael Recycle — Ellie Bethel

Language Arts — Goal: Learn and use new vocabulary: recycle, reuse, sort.
Activity: After reading, we will add our three new words to the word wall with pictures. Children will practice using 'recycle' and 'reuse' in sentences about things in our classroom.
Materials: Focus book; word cards; word wall
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Picture-supported word cards and time to point-and-name for emerging talkers.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Sort materials by what they are made of.
Activity: Children will handle clean items (paper, cans, plastic tubs, cloth) and sort them by material, testing cans with a magnet to discover that metal is special.
Materials: Clean recyclable items; magnet; sorting trays
Grouping: Small groups — science table
Support: Fewer items per round (start with six) for children building sorting stamina.

Social Science — Goal: Take responsibility for our classroom recycling job.
Activity: We will set up our classroom recycling station with picture labels and practice: after snack (using clean pretend items), everyone will sort their items into paper, plastic, or trash.
Materials: Three labeled bins; clean pretend snack items; picture labels
Grouping: Large group then practice — classroom; teacher-guided
Support: A photo step strip above the bins showing rinse, sort, done.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Sort, count, and graph by category.
Activity: Children will dump our practice recycling bin, sort everything by material, count each group, and build a bar graph with the counts to see which material we use most.
Materials: Practice recyclables; floor graph mat; number cards
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: Counting with a partner and touching each item for children building one-to-one correspondence.

Creative Art — Goal: Create a sculpture from reused materials.
Activity: Children will build robots, animals, or buildings from clean boxes, tubes, and lids, joining pieces with tape and glue and naming what their sculpture used to be.
Materials: Clean boxes and tubes; lids; tape; glue; markers
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Pre-cut tape pieces and a sturdy base box for children who need a stable start.

Music / Movement — Goal: Keep a steady beat with homemade instruments.
Activity: We will play teacher-made sealed shakers (bottles filled with beans) along to a recycling song, shaking loud and soft and stopping on the signal.
Materials: Sealed bottle shakers (teacher-made); recorded song
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: A shaker with a handle grip and a visual start/stop sign for cue support.

Motor Activities — Goal: Develop coordination carrying and tossing with control.
Activity: In our recycling relay, children will carry a soft recyclable down the path and toss it into the correct bin from a marked line, then walk back and tag the next friend.
Materials: Soft recyclable props; three bins; floor markers
Grouping: Small groups — movement area; teacher-supervised
Support: A shorter tossing distance and larger bins so every child can succeed.

Technology — Goal: Record and listen back to our own voices with a purpose.
Activity: Each child will record one line of our class recycling pledge ('I can recycle paper!') on the voice recorder, and we will play the pledge back together at closing circle.
Materials: Voice recorder or tablet (teacher-operated); pledge chart
Grouping: Small groups; teacher-led
Support: The option to record with a partner speaking together for children who are shy alone.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Care for our playground by cleaning it safely.
Activity: We will take a cleanup walk around the playground: children point out litter, and the teacher (wearing gloves) picks it up while children tally what was found. We will talk about why litter hurts animals.
Materials: Gloves and grabber (teacher only); tally sheet; trash bag
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: An assigned buddy and a small section of the yard for children who need a defined job area.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Understand that small jobs done by everyone make a big difference.
Activity: We will talk about how our whole class sorting recycling together fills a bin in a week, and each child will choose one small Earth job to be in charge of this week.
Materials: Job chart; name cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Job choices shown as pictures so children can choose by pointing.

title: Our Earth: Planting and Growing
subject: Science
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Our Earth' thematic week (April): Planting and Growing. Focus book: The Tiny Seed — Eric Carle. Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: The Tiny Seed — Eric Carle

Language Arts — Goal: Sequence a growth story in order: seed, sprout, plant, flower.
Activity: After reading, children will arrange four life-cycle picture cards in order and retell what happens at each step, using the words first, next, then, last.
Materials: Focus book; life-cycle cards; pocket chart
Grouping: Large group then pairs — carpet
Support: Sentence-starter strips ('First the seed...') for children who need language support.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Plant a seed and identify what it needs to grow.
Activity: Each child will plant a bean seed in a clear cup with soil, water it gently, and label the cup. We will predict what will happen and place our cups by the window.
Materials: Bean seeds; clear cups; soil; water; labels
Grouping: Small groups — science table
Support: A scoop with a handle and a pre-marked soil line for children developing pouring control.

Social Science — Goal: Identify gardeners and farmers and how they help us.
Activity: We will look at photos of people growing food and match foods to the plants they come from, talking about how many hands help a seed become our snack.
Materials: Photo cards of growers and foods; matching mats
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Fewer matching pairs (start with four) for children new to matching games.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Count seeds one-to-one and compare amounts.
Activity: Children will count seeds onto flowerpot mats (1–10), then play 'whose pot has more?' with a partner, counting again together to check.
Materials: Large seeds; flowerpot number mats; partner cards
Grouping: Centers — math area; child-led after demo
Support: Larger seeds and tweezers-free scooping for children working on fine control.

Creative Art — Goal: Explore color blending with a coffee-filter flower craft.
Activity: Children will color coffee filters with markers, watch the teacher spritz them with water so the colors spread like petals, and when dry, twist them into flowers with pipe-cleaner stems.
Materials: Coffee filters; washable markers; spray bottle (teacher); pipe cleaners
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Chunky markers and a pre-flattened filter for children who need easier gripping.

Music / Movement — Goal: Use whole-body movement to act out a growth sequence.
Activity: To gentle music, children will curl up small like seeds, push up like sprouts, stretch like stems, and open their arms like flowers, following the teacher's cues.
Materials: Recorded gentle music; open space
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: Movements demonstrated at a slower pace with the option to grow from a chair.

Motor Activities — Goal: Build hand strength digging, scooping, and filling.
Activity: In the soil bin, children will dig holes with scoops, drop in pretend seeds, cover them, and pat the soil flat, filling a whole row of pots.
Materials: Soil or sand bin; scoops; small pots; pretend seeds (beans)
Grouping: Centers — sensory/science area
Support: Deeper pots that stay steady and larger scoops for children building bilateral coordination.

Technology — Goal: Use the class camera to document our seeds on day one.
Activity: With the teacher, each child will take the first photo of their seed cup for our growth journal; we will view all the day-one photos together and notice that the cups look the same — for now.
Materials: Class camera or tablet (teacher-held); projector
Grouping: Small groups; teacher-led
Support: Teacher holds the camera while the child presses the button, for children learning careful handling.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Plant and care for a real flower outdoors.
Activity: We will visit our school garden bed where the teacher has loosened the soil; each child will place a flower start in a hole, cover the roots, and help water our new garden row.
Materials: Flower starts; watering cans; garden bed
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: A pre-dug hole and a small watering can for children who need a lighter load.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Practice patience and gentle care for living things.
Activity: We will talk about how seeds grow slowly and cannot be rushed, just like learning something new. Children will share one thing they are learning to do that takes practice.
Materials: Feelings chart; a planted seed cup to observe
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Specific praise naming the effort ('You kept trying') for children who share.

evidence:

Language Arts — Goal: Contribute ideas to a group poster using complete sentences.
Activity: After reading, we will brainstorm a class poster, 'We Use Water For...' and 'We Can Save Water By...,' with each child dictating one idea for the teacher to write.
Materials: Focus book; poster paper; markers
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Picture prompts (brush teeth, wash hands, drink) for children choosing an idea.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Compare amounts of water and observe how we use it.
Activity: The teacher will let a tap drip into a cup for one minute while we watch and count drips, then we will compare it to a full cup and talk about how drips add up.
Materials: Sink or water bin; clear cups; timer
Grouping: Small groups — science area; teacher-led demo
Support: A front spot for children who need to see the drips up close; counting together aloud.

Social Science — Goal: Recognize that everyone shares the water in our community.
Activity: We will trace a drop's journey on a simple picture map — from rain, to river, to our classroom sink — and name everyone along the way who needs the same water: people, animals, plants.
Materials: Water journey picture map; drop pointer
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: The drop pointer passed hand to hand so each child can follow one step of the journey.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Measure and compare capacity: more, less, full, empty.
Activity: At the water table, children will fill containers using cups, count how many cups each holds, and order the containers from 'holds least' to 'holds most.'
Materials: Water table; assorted containers; counting cups
Grouping: Centers — science/math area; child-led
Support: Two containers only (big and small) for children starting with simple comparisons.

Creative Art — Goal: Paint with shades of one color family.
Activity: Children will mix white and black into blue paint to make light and dark blues, then paint a river or ocean scene using all their shades.
Materials: Blue, white, and black tempera; brushes; paper; smocks
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Pre-mixed shade cups for children who need to focus on painting rather than mixing.

Music / Movement — Goal: Create a rainstorm with body percussion in a sequence.
Activity: Following the teacher's lead, we will build a rainstorm: rubbing hands (wind), patting knees (drizzle), clapping (rain), stomping softly (thunder far away), then quiet down in reverse.
Materials: Open rug space; teacher cue cards
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: Picture cue cards shown before each sound layer for children who need warning of louder parts.

Motor Activities — Goal: Strengthen hands and arms squeezing sponges to move water.
Activity: Children will soak sponges in one tub and squeeze them out into another, moving as much 'rain' as they can and watching the water line rise.
Materials: Two tubs; sponges of different sizes; water
Grouping: Small groups — water table area
Support: Smaller, softer sponges for children still developing squeeze strength.

Technology — Goal: Identify water sounds and match them to pictures.
Activity: Children will listen to short recorded sounds (rain, a river, a faucet, ocean waves) on the tablet and tap the matching picture on our sound board.
Materials: Tablet with teacher-selected sound clips; picture board
Grouping: Small group — listening area; teacher-guided
Support: Headphones and a two-choice display for children who need fewer options.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Use water carefully for a real outdoor job.
Activity: We will check our rain gauge, record what we find, and use watering cans to water only the garden plants that are dry, checking the soil with a finger first.
Materials: Rain gauge; watering cans; garden bed
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: A half-filled watering can and a partner for the walk to the garden.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Understand sharing resources: taking what we need and leaving some for others.
Activity: We will talk about the water in our classroom water table — if one friend uses it all, none is left. Children will practice naming a time they shared something that could run out.
Materials: Feelings chart; focus book pictures
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A sentence frame ('I shared the ___') for children who need a starting structure.

Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led

title: Plant Study: A Seed's Journey
subject: Science
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Plant Study' thematic week (April): A Seed's Journey. Focus book: The Tiny Seed — Eric Carle. Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: The Tiny Seed — Eric Carle

Language Arts — Goal: Follow a seed's journey through a story and sequence the seasons.
Activity: We will read how a tiny seed travels on the wind through the seasons, pausing to name where it lands and what it needs; children will act out the journey path with scarves as they listen a second time.
Materials: Focus book; journey picture cards; scarves
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Story map cards kept visible during the read for children following the journey.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Find seeds inside real plants and compare where seeds grow.
Activity: Children will open real seed pods and a pumpkin or sunflower head (teacher-cut) to find the seeds inside, count them, and compare where different plants keep their seeds.
Materials: Sunflower head or pumpkin (teacher-prepared); pods; trays; magnifiers
Grouping: Small groups — science table; teacher-supervised
Support: Teacher pre-tears the tough pods; children handle the soft parts.

Social Science — Goal: Identify what plants need to grow (sun, water, soil, air).
Activity: We will chart what a seed needs — soil, water, sun, space, time — and children will test the chart against a sad droopy plant picture and a thriving one, deciding what each plant is missing.
Materials: Needs picture cards; healthy/droopy plant photos; chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Picture cards pairing each condition with a plant picture for matching practice.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Sort seeds by attributes and count one group.
Activity: Children will sort a mixed bean-and-seed collection into groups (big, small, striped, smooth), then count the seeds in one group and record it on our chart.
Materials: Mixed beans and large seeds; sorting trays; chart; pencils
Grouping: Small groups — science/math table
Support: Bigger beans and a partner counter for children building one-to-one accuracy.

Creative Art — Goal: Create designs with seeds as a collage medium.
Activity: Children will make seed mosaic pictures, arranging beans and lentils in patterns and shapes on a flower outline and gluing them in place.
Materials: Assorted beans and lentils; flower outlines; glue; trays
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Glue in a squeeze bottle with a helper opening for children who tire of glue sticks.

Music / Movement — Goal: Move through a plant growth sequence (seed, sprout, stem, flower).
Activity: We will grow like seeds to slow music: curl up tiny on the floor, sprout arms up, sway as stems, and open hands as flowers when the music brightens.
Materials: Recorded gentle music; open rug space
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: Growing motions can be done seated, curling and stretching from a chair.

Motor Activities — Goal: Dig, plant, and pat soil using hand tools.
Activity: At our garden table, children will dig small holes in soil tubs with trowels, drop in a bean 'seed,' cover it, and pat the soil smooth.
Materials: Soil tubs; trowels; large beans; watering can props
Grouping: Centers — science/sensory area; teacher-supervised
Support: A shorter digging row and a kneeling pad for children who need either support.

Technology — Goal: Use the tablet camera to photograph and zoom in on seeds.
Activity: With a teacher nearby, pairs will photograph seeds, pods, and garden finds with the class tablet, then zoom in together to see details our eyes missed.
Materials: Class tablet; seed collection; display screen
Grouping: Pairs; teacher-guided
Support: A buddy photographer paired up so both direct and both tap on turns.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Find seeds outside on a nature walk.
Activity: On our garden walk, children will look closely at the ground and plants for seeds: dandelion fluff, maple helicopters, acorns if the season offers them — collecting only what has already fallen.
Materials: Collection cups; magnifiers; garden route
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors, in small groups
Support: A magnifier on a neck cord for children who need hands free for balance.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Learn patience: growing takes time and waiting can be peaceful.
Activity: The tiny seed waits through winter before it can grow — we will talk about how good things take time, and each child will name one thing they are waiting for and one kind thing to do while waiting.
Materials: Focus book; feelings chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A picture strip of the seed's long journey for children who grasp time better visually.

title: Plant Study: Parts of a Plant
subject: Science
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Plant Study' thematic week (April): Parts of a Plant. Focus book: The Reason for a Flower — Gail Gibbons. Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: The Reason for a Flower — Gail Gibbons

Language Arts — Goal: Learn and use plant-part vocabulary: petals, stem, leaf, roots.
Activity: We will read the focus book's simple explanations, then examine a real flower together and name its parts — petals, stem, leaves, roots — as children hold and point to each part.
Materials: Focus book; real flowers; word cards; chart paper
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Real flower in hand to touch while labeling, making the words concrete.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Dissect a flower and observe its inside parts.
Activity: With magnifiers, children will gently take apart a large flower (teacher-guided), laying petals, stem pieces, and the center in a row, and draw what the inside looks like.
Materials: Large flowers; magnifiers; trays; science journals
Grouping: Small groups — science table; teacher-guided
Support: Step cards with photos of each dissection step for children following along.

Social Science — Goal: Match plants to the ways they help people and animals.
Activity: Children will match flowers and plants to their uses in picture cards: food (tomato), medicine picture (herb), shade (tree), beauty (bouquet), and home for animals (bush) — plants help people and animals.
Materials: Plant-use picture cards; sorting mat
Grouping: Small groups — tables
Support: A label card to hold and match for children learning the gift words in a home language too.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Count petals and compare numbers of parts.
Activity: Children will count petals on real and paper flowers, write or stamp the number, and order flower cards from fewest petals to most.
Materials: Real flowers (allergy-checked); paper flowers; numeral stamps; chart
Grouping: Small groups — math/science table
Support: Counting in pairs, one partner counting aloud and the other pointing.

Creative Art — Goal: Arrange real plant parts in a pressed-flower design.
Activity: Children will arrange pressed leaves and petals between contact paper and a card frame to make a plant bookmark, choosing each part's place (this uses already-fallen and spent flowers only).
Materials: Pressed leaves and petals; clear contact paper; card frames
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Pre-pressed leaves available for children joining when pressing time is short.

Music / Movement — Goal: Move and sing the parts of a plant in order from roots to flower.
Activity: We will sing a plant-parts song with motions — roots below (crouch and wiggle fingers down), stem grows up (rise), leaves spread (arms out), flower opens (hands bloom).
Materials: Teacher-led song; plant part cards
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: Printed action words to read along for children who process cues visually first.

Motor Activities — Goal: Lace parts in order to build a flower (sequence and threading).
Activity: Children will lace paper petals onto a pipe-cleaner stem in the order shown on a card, building a whole flower from roots to bloom.
Materials: Pipe cleaners; paper petals, leaves, roots; sequence cards
Grouping: Centers — fine motor table
Support: Petals strung on a fat pipe cleaner that stands up without holding.

Technology — Goal: Use a digital microscope to see tiny plant structures.
Activity: Children will look at a leaf, a petal, and a seed under the digital microscope, seeing the tiny veins and textures, and compare the screen view with holding the real thing.
Materials: Digital microscope; leaf; petal; seed; screen
Grouping: Small groups — science table; teacher-led
Support: Teacher holds the microscope; the child tells the class what they notice on screen.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Observe and draw a real plant's parts outdoors.
Activity: Children will choose one outdoor plant, sit with it, and draw exactly what they see — how many leaves, what shape, any flowers — then trade drawings and try to find their partner's plant.
Materials: Clipboards; paper; crayons; garden beds
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors, in small groups
Support: A seated plant-drawing spot by the garden beds for children who prefer it.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Learn that every member of a group has an important part.
Activity: Every part of the flower has a job and the plant needs them all — we will talk about how our class is like a plant: everyone has something important to do, and we will name each other's helpful jobs.
Materials: Focus book; flower part chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A role card for children who feel more confident with an assigned part.

title: Plant Study: We Plant Our Garden
subject: Science
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Plant Study' thematic week (April): We Plant Our Garden. Focus book: Planting a Rainbow — Lois Ehlert. evidence:
Focus book: Planting a Rainbow — Lois Ehlert

Language Arts — Goal: Name flower colors and sort them in rainbow order.
Activity: We will read the focus book and chant the colors of the flowers as they bloom on the page; children will sort flower cards by color and 'read them' in rainbow order like the book does.
Materials: Focus book; flower color cards; color word cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Fewer color word cards (four) for children building color vocabulary at their pace.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Set up a seed-growing experiment we can observe over time.
Activity: Each child will plant bean seeds in a clear cup (soil, seed against the side, water) and draw Day One in a growth journal; cups will live on the windowsill for daily checks.
Materials: Clear cups; soil; bean seeds; water; growth journals
Grouping: Small groups — science table; teacher-led
Support: Daily photo card for children to place in sequence instead of writing observations.

Social Science — Goal: Make a group plan (garden map) and vote on what to grow.
Activity: We will plan our class garden like real gardeners: children will vote with stones on what to plant in each row — beans, flowers, or herbs — and place plant markers on the plan.
Materials: Garden plan chart; stones for voting; plant picture cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A picture map of the garden plan to point to while deciding as a group.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Plant 'seeds' at positions one through ten in order.
Activity: Using a long paper 'garden row,' children will plant a paper seed in every numbered spot to 10, then count backward as we 'pick' each one.
Materials: Paper garden row with numbered spots; seed cards
Grouping: Centers — math area; child-led after demo
Support: A number line to check against after placing each seed card.

Creative Art — Goal: Paint a rainbow garden using color order red to purple.
Activity: Children will paint garden flowers in rainbow order — red, orange, yellow, green (leaves), blue, purple — using the book's color parade as inspiration.
Materials: Paint in rainbow colors; large paper; brushes; smocks
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: A dot guide for each petal position for children who lose track while painting.

Music / Movement — Goal: Respond to color cues with movement (stand, bloom, rest).
Activity: We will do the color parade: when the teacher holds up a color card, flowers of that color stand and swirl like blossoms, sitting when their color goes down.
Materials: Color cards; recorded music; scarves
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: Scarf provided to make movements bigger and easier to follow.

Motor Activities — Goal: Carry and pour water carefully to our growing seeds.
Activity: Children will carry cups of water from the barrel to our bean cups, pouring slowly at soil level, and record their cup on the watering chart — the most important garden job.
Materials: Cups; water barrel; bean cups; watering chart
Grouping: Small groups — science area; teacher-supervised
Support: A water level mark to aim for and a stool for steady footing.

Technology — Goal: Take a 'before' photo of our experiment to compare later.
Activity: We will set up the visual timer to 'watch' our seeds' watering schedule and take a class photo of Planting Day; tomorrow we will compare the cups to the photo to spot any change.
Materials: Class tablet; planted cups; visual timer
Grouping: Small groups; teacher-guided
Support: The timer set for a short, achievable count for children practicing waiting.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Plant real seeds in our garden bed together.
Activity: Out in our garden spot (or large planter), children will help dig rows, place big bean seeds, cover them, and mark the spot with a name stake they decorated.
Materials: Child trowels; bean seeds; planter or garden bed; name stakes
Grouping: Whole class outdoors, in small groups
Support: A trowel with a chunky grip and a pre-started hole for children building digging strength.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Understand that caring for living things is an everyday responsibility.
Activity: The gardeners in our book care for their garden for months before the rainbow blooms — we will talk about how caring for something every day is different from helping just once, and choose one class plant job.
Materials: Focus book; job chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Picture choices of caretaking jobs to pick a favorite from.

description: Preschool day plan from the 'Plant Study' thematic week (April): Watching It Grow. Focus book: My Garden — Kevin Henkes. evidence:
Focus book: My Garden — Kevin Henkes

Language Arts — Goal: Distinguish real plants from pretend ones in a story (fantasy vs. reality).
Activity: We will read about the girl's imaginary garden and play 'Real or Pretend?': jelly-bean trees (pretend), carrots underground (real), seashells that grow (pretend), sorting the book's ideas onto two charts.
Materials: Focus book; real/pretend charts; picture cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Real-versus-pretend picture choices to hold up for children answering in their own way.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Compare plant growth with and without sun and water (fair test).
Activity: Children will compare our windowsill beans (watered, sunny) with a teacher-kept cup from a dark cupboard and one unwatered cup, drawing all three and telling what made the difference.
Materials: Three comparison bean cups; growth journals; crayons
Grouping: Small groups — science table; teacher-led
Support: Extra beans planted by the teacher as backups so every child has data to observe.

Social Science — Goal: Take responsibility for a caretaking job in our shared garden.
Activity: Children will take Plant Keeper jobs for the day — waterer, leaf checker, weed spotter (pulling only teacher-marked weeds), and sprout counter — wearing job badges and reporting back at closing circle.
Materials: Job badges; watering cups; garden beds
Grouping: Small groups, indoors and outdoors
Support: A quiet corner of the garden to care for alone for children who prefer a calm job right now.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Measure sprout height with cubes and compare heights.
Activity: Children will measure our bean sprouts with cube towers, compare heights, and place the plants in line from shortest to tallest, adding numbers to our growth chart.
Materials: Bean sprouts; unifix cubes; growth chart
Grouping: Small groups — science/math table
Support: A ruler strip with photos of our own past sprouts to compare sizes visually.

Creative Art — Goal: Paint an imaginary garden, mixing real and pretend ideas.
Activity: Inspired by the book's pretend garden, children will dream-paint their own imaginary gardens — giant flowers, chocolate rabbits, seashells that bloom — saying one real thing and one pretend thing in their painting.
Materials: Paint; large paper; brushes; focus book pictures
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Photos of our own real sprouts to paint from if imagining feels hard today.

Music / Movement — Goal: Grow gradually through movement levels and freeze on a cue.
Activity: We will play Growing Statues: music plays while 'seeds' wiggle and grow taller and taller; when the rain sound stops, everyone freezes at their height until the 'sun' returns.
Materials: Recorded music with pause; sun/rain cue cards
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: A taped star spot marking their growing place so no one is squeezed.

Motor Activities — Goal: Build scissor control by snipping along edges.
Activity: Children will snip paper 'grass' along the top edge of the garden fence strip, using two hands together — one holds, one cuts — keeping fingers on the safe side of the line.
Materials: Paper fence strips; safety scissors; grass-green crayons
Grouping: Centers — fine motor table
Support: Snips instead of full cuts — pre-scored strip — for children new to scissors.

Technology — Goal: Compare time-lapse photos of our own plants and describe change.
Activity: Children will use the tablet photos from Planting Day and today to build a two-photo 'then and now' page for our class garden book, dictating one change they can see.
Materials: Tablet with date-stamped photos; class book pages
Grouping: Small groups; teacher-guided
Support: A finished example sequence book to flip through first as a model.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Inspect our garden rows and record growth changes.
Activity: Children will check our outdoor bean rows for sprouts, count leaves on the biggest plant, and dig fingertips gently near (not in) the soil to feel how watering changed it — washing hands after.
Materials: Garden rows; counting cards; hand-washing station
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors, in small groups
Support: A damp towel in case of accidental mouthing of garden soil; hands checked after.

Activity: The girl in the story tends her garden every single day — we will talk about how caring for a plant (or a pet, or a friend) means showing up again and again, and each child will sign our Plant Keeper promise chart with a handprint.
Materials: Handprint promise chart; paint for prints
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Sentence starter ('I can take care of...') for children organizing their idea.

title: Plant Study: Harvest and Thank You, Plants
subject: Science
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Plant Study' thematic week (April): Harvest and Thank You, Plants. Focus book: The Carrot Seed — Ruth Krauss. evidence:
Focus book: The Carrot Seed — Ruth Krauss

Language Arts — Goal: Retell a cumulative story about a seed that finally grows.
Activity: We will read how a boy plants one small seed and — despite everyone's doubts — weeds, waters, and waits until a giant carrot grows; children will join the repeated pattern of his care and predict the ending.
Materials: Focus book; care-action cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: The weed-and-water action cards to hold while listening to track the repetition.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Discover seeds inside the foods plants make.
Activity: At the teacher's table, children will open and examine harvested or store vegetables (washed carrots, snap peas, green beans) to find where their seeds hide, sorting seeds by plant (no tasting today; separate allergy-aware snack rules apply at snack time).
Materials: Washed vegetables; trays; magnifiers; seed sorting cups
Grouping: Small groups — science table; teacher-supervised
Support: Butter knives only, at the teacher's table, for children ready for supervised cutting practice.

Social Science — Goal: Pretend-play a farmers market (grower, seller, shopper roles).
Activity: We will run a pretend farmers market with our harvest: farmers price their paper vegetables, shoppers carry baskets, and everyone practices trading turns and saying where each food grew.
Materials: Paper vegetables; baskets; play money; market signs
Grouping: Centers — dramatic play; teacher facilitates
Support: A market shopping list with pictures so every child can complete a full 'shop' independently.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Estimate, count, and check a harvest collection.
Activity: Children will count our harvested or pictured vegetables into groups, estimate first ('How many carrots in the bucket?'), then count to check, celebrating how close our guesses came.

Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Counting into labeled cups (1s, 2s, 5s) for children who need containers to organize a count.

Creative Art — Goal: Make harvest prints with vegetable shapes.
Activity: Children will print with vegetable halves — carrot tops, pepper rings, celery moons — making a harvest picture and naming each print's shape (teacher cuts all vegetables).
Materials: Cut vegetables (teacher-prepared); paint pads; paper; smocks
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: A handled stamp grip for children who need more control pressing prints.

Music / Movement — Goal: Perform a harvest song with coordinated actions.
Activity: We will sing and dig through the harvest song — dig (pretend shovels), pull (lean back), shake the dirt off (wiggle), and hold up our carrot (arms high) on the last verse.
Materials: Teacher-led song; action cards
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: A rhythm stick pair for children who anchor better with an instrument in hand.

Motor Activities — Goal: Pull a loaded wagon and unload items one at a time.
Activity: Children will take turns pulling a wagon 'harvest cart' loaded with soft vegetables along the garden path, unloading carefully into the market basket at the end.
Materials: Wagon; soft toy vegetables; basket; path cones
Grouping: Small groups — movement area; teacher-supervised
Support: A shorter pull distance and lighter load in the bucket for a satisfying success.

Technology — Goal: Create a closing slideshow and voice recording of our garden story.
Activity: We will watch our garden slideshow from seed to sprout to garden rows, and record each child naming one thing they did to help the plants grow, saving it for families.
Materials: Tablet with dated photos; voice recorder; projector
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A printed photo set to hold while the slideshow plays for children who follow better with a tangible copy.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Explore roots in soil and help care for our garden.
Activity: Children will dig gently around our bean plants' roots with spoons to peek at how roots hold the plant, then carefully cover them back — learning plants live below ground too — and give the garden a final thank-you watering.
Materials: Spoons; garden beds; watering cans
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors, in small groups
Support: Gloves available for children who dislike the feel of soil on hands.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Celebrate persistence and believe in our own growing.
Activity: The boy believed in his seed even when everyone said it wouldn't grow — we will each draw the plant or project we are proudest of this week and share it, celebrating everyone's different way of growing.
Materials: Children's growth journals; feelings chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Adults will name one specific patient thing they saw each child do this week.

title: Rain, Clouds, and Wind: Where Rain Comes From
subject: Science
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Rain, Clouds, and Wind' thematic week (April): Where Rain Comes From. Focus book: Listen to the Rain — Bill Martin Jr.. Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: Listen to the Rain — Bill Martin Jr.

Language Arts — Goal: Listen for descriptive sound words and contribute our own.
Activity: We will read the focus book slowly, listening to its rain sounds — the soft sprinkle, the patter, the downpour — and add our own sound words for rain to a class list.
Materials: Focus book; sound word chart; markers
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Sound word cards (pitter, patter, roar) to hold up while listening.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Measure collected water and compare amounts.
Activity: Children will catch and measure 'rain' from our spray-bottle storm in measuring cups, comparing amounts collected under a leaf umbrella versus out in the open.
Materials: Spray bottles; measuring cups; leaf umbrella prop; trays
Grouping: Small groups — science table
Support: A clear cup to watch alongside for children who observe best at eye level.

Social Science — Goal: Practice helping a partner stay 'dry' — cooperation in pairs.
Activity: We will practice sharing shade and shelter: two friends under one (teacher-held) umbrella prop, walking slowly together, learning how people help each other stay dry.
Materials: Umbrella prop (teacher-managed); floor path
Grouping: Pairs — rug area; teacher-led
Support: A real umbrella demonstrated by the teacher first for children unfamiliar with opening one safely.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Count water drops to match numerals to 10.
Activity: Children will squeeze droppers to make raindrops on coffee-filter clouds, counting drops to match numeral cards up to 10, and notice how the filter soaks after many drops.
Materials: Droppers; coffee filters; water cups; numeral cards
Grouping: Centers — math/science area; child-led after demo
Support: Counting drops into a ten-frame drawn on the tray for children who need the frame.

Creative Art — Goal: Create drip paintings where colors run and blend.
Activity: Children will drip watercolor 'rain' down paper held nearly upright, watching colors run and mix at the bottom like puddles forming under a rainy sky.
Materials: Watercolors; droppers; heavy paper; easel or tilted trays
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: A short-handled dropper for small hands; results celebrated while still wet so colors show best.

Music / Movement — Goal: Build and fade a rainstorm using body sounds and dynamics.
Activity: We will make a rainstorm with body percussion: rub hands (wind), tap fingers (sprinkles), clap thighs (rain), stomp gently (downpour), then calm back down as the storm passes.
Materials: Teacher-led cues; open rug space
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: Softer sound options (fingertips on thighs) for children who find loud sounds hard.

Motor Activities — Goal: Jump over and navigate around pretend puddles.
Activity: Children will hop over blue tape 'puddles' with two feet, step carefully around the big puddle, and tiptoe through the 'drizzle' lane between them.
Materials: Blue tape puddles; floor lanes
Grouping: Small groups — movement area; teacher-supervised
Support: An adult hand nearby for the jumps; a walk-around-the-puddle option that still practices big leg moves.

Technology — Goal: Listen to and sort weather sounds by intensity.
Activity: Children will listen to recorded rain and thunder sounds (gentle, teacher-selected and previewed) and sort picture cards into 'sounds of a soft rain' and 'sounds of a big storm.'
Materials: Listening center/recordings; sound picture cards
Grouping: Small groups; teacher-guided
Support: Volume checked first; the wooden rain stick offered as an alternative sound-maker.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Observe water and creatures after rain outdoors.
Activity: Children will examine the wet world after rain (or after watering can 'rain' on a dry day): sparkle drops on leaves, worms on the path, drips from the roof edge — looking closely with magnifiers.
Materials: Magnifiers; garden and path; rain boots
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors, in small groups
Support: Extra time with the magnifier back at the door for children who walk slowly.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Name our feelings about rain and see its good side.
Activity: Rainy days can feel cozy or gloomy — we will name how rain makes each of us feel, and talk about how rain is a gift the garden waits for, even when we wish for sun.
Materials: Feelings chart; focus book
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A choice to share a rain joy instead of a rain worry for children who find storms frightening.
