Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Sentence frame ('I see bugs at...') for support.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Count story foods one-to-one and match numerals 1–5.
Activity: Using story pictures, children will count what the caterpillar ate each day (1 apple, 2 pears, 3 plums...) and place the matching number of fruit counters on our week chart.
Materials: Story food picture cards; fruit counters; week chart
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: Food cards limited to one day at a time (start with two days) for children building counting stamina.

Creative Art — Goal: Paint a caterpillar model choosing colors and count of parts.
Activity: Children will paint egg-carton sections green (and one red head) to make a caterpillar, choosing how many body bumps their caterpillar will have.
Materials: Egg carton sections (teacher-cut); green and red paint; brushes; smocks
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Pre-cut egg carton sections and fat-handled brushes for easier gripping.

Music / Movement — Goal: Move through a life-cycle sequence to music.
Activity: To the music, we will move through the caterpillar's life: crawl and munch, sleep still in our cocoons, then stretch and flutter as butterflies when the music blooms.
Materials: Recorded music; scarves for wings
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: A teacher-modeled movement beside them for children copying a partner's actions.

Motor Activities — Goal: Crawl and wiggle through an obstacle path.
Activity: Children will crawl through the tunnel like caterpillars, wiggle through the 'leaf' (a hoop with green streamers), then rest curled in the 'cocoon' blanket spot.
Materials: Play tunnel; hoop with streamers; blanket
Grouping: Small groups — movement area; teacher-supervised
Support: A shorter tunnel and a teacher at the exit to greet each caterpillar.

Technology — Goal: Use a digital microscope to observe small things closely.
Activity: With the teacher, children will look at a feather, a leaf, and a toy insect under the digital microscope, describing the patterns and tiny details the screen reveals.
Materials: Digital microscope; leaf; feather; toy insect
Grouping: Small groups; teacher-led
Support: Teacher places objects while the child narrates what they see for the group.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Search for insects outdoors and record what we find.
Activity: We will take magnifiers outside for our first insect hunt: looking under leaves and near flowers (teacher guiding where to look), observing without touching, and tallying each kind we find.

Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: A defined search square (hula hoop on the ground) for children who need a boundary.

Activity: We will talk about how even a tiny caterpillar matters and grows. Children will practice gentle hands with a toy insect — holding it on an open palm and putting it back carefully.

Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A stuffed caterpillar to hold while sharing for children who need comfort to speak.

Support: Specific praise for children who name a change they have made this year.

title: Insects: Busy Bees and Ants
subject: Science
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Insects' thematic week (May): Busy Bees and Ants. Focus book: Are You a Bee? — Judy Allen. Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: Are You a Bee? — Judy Allen

Language Arts — Goal: Learn bee vocabulary and give simple directions.
Activity: We will read the focus book's bee facts and collect busy words (hive, pollen, worker, dance). Children will practice 'bee talk' — telling a partner one flower's location with words, like bees 'dance' directions.
Materials: Focus book; word cards; flower cards
Grouping: Large group then pairs — carpet
Support: New words echoed chorally before individual use.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Model how bees carry pollen between flowers.
Activity: The teacher will dust a fuzzy toy bee with colored chalk 'pollen,' then children will pass it flower to flower, watching the pollen travel — learning how bees help flowers make seeds.
Materials: Fuzzy bee model; paper flowers; colored chalk dust (teacher-handled)
Grouping: Small groups — science table; teacher-led demo
Support: Teacher handles the chalk dust; children only pass the bee model hand to hand.

Social Science — Goal: Identify jobs in a bee colony and compare to our class jobs.
Activity: We will match hive jobs (queen, worker, drone — in simple words: mother bee, helper bee, and the bees who fly out) to pictures, then compare to jobs in our classroom family.
Materials: Bee job picture cards; class job chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Fewer job cards (three main jobs) for children starting the concept.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Count and order ants matching numerals 1–10.
Activity: Children will read a number card and 'march' that many toy ants into line on our ant trail, then order the trail cards from 1 to 10 with the group.
Materials: Toy ants; ant trail mat; number cards
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: Number cards 1–5 range offered first for children mastering smaller sets.

Creative Art — Goal: Print a honeycomb pattern and add fingerprint bees.
Activity: Children will press bubble wrap into yellow paint and stamp hexagon honeycomb patterns, then add thumbprint bees with drawn wings and stripes.
Materials: Bubble wrap; yellow paint; paper; markers
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Bubble wrap pieces with handles taped on for easier stamping.

Music / Movement — Goal: Control voice volume like a conductor game.
Activity: We will hum and buzz like bees, flying our sound loud and soft as the teacher's hand rises and falls, then sing a simple busy-bee song with finger actions.
Materials: Teacher-led song; hand signal cues
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A kazoo-like hum with the teacher beside them for children unsure of humming pitch.

Motor Activities — Goal: Cooperate to carry an object along a path with a partner.
Activity: In our ant parade, children will carry a soft 'crumb' (ball) together with a partner along a winding trail line back to the 'anthill,' then join the end of the line.
Materials: Soft balls; trail line; anthill mat
Grouping: Small groups — movement area; teacher-supervised
Support: A lighter 'crumb' and a partner to share the carrying for children who need it.

Technology — Goal: Discriminate nature sounds at the listening center.
Activity: At the listening center, children will hear recorded buzzing, birdsong, and rain, pressing the matching picture for each — learning that the loudest buzz means the bees are near.
Materials: Listening center; recorded sounds; picture choices
Grouping: Centers — pairs; child-led after setup

Grouping: Small groups — movement area; teacher-supervised
Support: Hoops in three sizes so every child can find their success size.

Grouping: Centers — pairs; child-led after setup

Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led

Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Practice done in pairs so children rehearse before any group sharing.

Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led

Grouping: Small groups — movement area; teacher-supervised

Grouping: Centers — art/math area; child-led
Support: Cookie templates with dot guides for children who want to count placement precisely.

Activity: Children will decorate big paper gingerbread people with collage frosting — yarn squiggles, button eyes, and ribbon smiles — each one different, for our bakery window display.

Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Pre-cut gingerbread shapes and large collage pieces for children building scissor skills.

Music / Movement — Goal: Move and freeze to a story chase song.
Activity: We will dance the 'Run, Run' chase song: jogging in place during the refrain, freezing in a cookie pose whenever the music stops, and tiptoeing when the fox verse plays.
Materials: Recorded playful music; open space
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: A walking-pace lane for children who enjoy the dance without the chase speed.

Motor Activities — Goal: Run, hop, and 'wade' through a story obstacle course.
Activity: Our chase course follows the tale: run the farm path, hop the fence line, wade (high-knee) through the 'river' (blue mat), and stop safely at the bridge mat — no fox tricks needed.

Grouping: Small groups — movement area; teacher-supervised

Grouping: Large group; teacher-led

title: Oh, The Places You'll Go!: Our Journey Begins
subject: ELA / Reading
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Oh, The Places You'll Go!' thematic week (June): Our Journey Begins. Focus book: Oh, the Places You'll Go! — Dr. Seuss. evidence:
Focus book: Oh, the Places You'll Go! — Dr. Seuss

Language Arts — Goal: Listen to a longer story and share a dream destination.
Activity: We will read selected pages of our anchor book about the journeys ahead, pausing to wonder: where would YOU go? Children will dictate one dream place for our 'Places We Will Go' banner.
Materials: Focus book (selected pages); banner paper; markers
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Preferential seating up front so the book's pictures are easy to see during the long-ish reading.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Observe that warm air rises (teacher demonstration).
Activity: The teacher will demonstrate warm air rising using a hair dryer and a tissue-paper balloon shape (teacher only, at a safe distance): children will predict, watch it lift, and describe why it rose.
Materials: Hair dryer (teacher only); tissue-paper balloon; heat-safe setup
Grouping: Large group — science area; teacher-led demo
Support: Front-row spots and a prediction hand-signal (up/down) so everyone answers at once.

Social Science — Goal: Compare places near and far and how we reach them.
Activity: We will look at photos of places near and far — our town, the beach, the mountains, a big city — sort them into 'we can walk there / we need a ride / we need a plane,' and find our town on the map.
Materials: Place photo cards; simple map; globe
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A desk globe at child height for hands-on finding with a partner.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Sort vehicles by where they travel and count groups.
Activity: Children will sort vehicle cards by where they travel — land, water, or air — then count how many go each way and build a quick floor graph.
Materials: Vehicle cards; three sorting mats
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: Sorting mats with big vehicle silhouettes to match for children who need the visual.

Creative Art — Goal: Create a hot air balloon with ourselves in the basket.
Activity: Children will decorate a big paper balloon with patterns and colors, glue on a basket, and add a drawing of themselves inside — ready to fly.
Materials: Paper balloon circles; baskets; crayons; glue
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: A photo option (their printed picture) or a drawn face for children choosing how to appear in the basket.

Music / Movement — Goal: Change movements to match music and vehicle cues.
Activity: We will travel to music: drive with steering arms, fly with wide arms, sail with rowing arms, changing vehicles each time the music changes style.
Materials: Recorded music (varied tempos); open space
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: Motion picture cards for children choosing their vehicle by picture.

Motor Activities — Goal: Complete a journey obstacle course with climbing and crossing.
Activity: Our journey course begins: climb the 'mountain' (ramp), cross the 'river' (blue mat) on stepping stones, crawl through the 'tunnel,' and wave from the 'summit' mat.
Materials: Ramp; blue mat; stepping stones; tunnel
Grouping: Small groups — movement area; teacher-supervised
Support: A shorter mountain ramp for children still building climbing confidence.

Technology — Goal: Explore famous places through guided photographs.
Activity: We will view projected photographs of famous places (teacher-selected) — a lighthouse, a desert, snowy mountains, a rainforest we remember — and try to name where each traveler is.
Materials: Projector; teacher-selected place photos
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Children vote for the next place by pointing together with a partner.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Walk carefully outdoors holding a balloon against the wind.
Activity: Outside, each child will carry a balloon (inflated and tied by the teacher) on a careful walk around the playground path, holding tight so it doesn't fly away and noticing how the wind tugs it.
Materials: Balloons (teacher-inflated); playground path
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: A grip-helper ribbon tied to the balloon string and a walking buddy.

Activity: The book tells us new places can feel exciting and a little scary. We will name both feelings and practice saying our brave sentence: 'I can try new things.'
Materials: Feelings chart; focus book (favorite page)
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Sentence frame ('I feel brave when I...') for support.

subject: ELA / Reading
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Oh, The Places You'll Go!' thematic week (June): Ways to Travel. Focus book: The Airport Book — Lisa Brown. evidence:

Activity: We will read about a family's airport trip, then sequence a journey with picture cards: pack a bag, ride to the airport, check in, fly, arrive and hug hello.

Grouping: Large group then pairs — carpet

Grouping: Small groups — gym/science area
Support: A pre-folded glider to decorate and fly for children whose folds are still developing.

Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Job badge pictures worn during play to make roles clear.

Activity: Children will fly paper gliders from our start line, measure each flight in footsteps, and record the flights on our chart to find which glider flew farthest.

Grouping: Small group — movement area/gym
Support: A marked measuring strip so counting footsteps stays organized.

Creative Art — Goal: Construct a vehicle from recycled materials.
Activity: Children will build their own travel vehicle from boxes, tubes, and wheels — a plane, bus, boat, or rocket — and tell the teacher its name and where it goes.
Materials: Boxes; tubes; bottle-cap wheels; tape; glue
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: A junk box sorted by shape so children can find the piece they imagine faster.

Music / Movement — Goal: Sing a vehicle song with sounds and motions at two speeds.
Activity: We will sing a vehicle sounds song — honk-honk, chugga-chugga, zoom, splash — adding each vehicle's motions and trying the song fast like a plane and slow like a boat.
Materials: Teacher-led song; vehicle cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Sound picture cards to choose which vehicle sound to make first.

Motor Activities — Goal: Follow a leader and stop/start on signal.
Activity: We will play a travel follow-the-leader: the 'conductor' leads the line driving, flying, and rowing around the room, freezing everyone at 'stations' when the whistle card is raised.
Materials: Whistle picture card; open space
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: The conductor role offered to a child who prefers leading to following some rounds.

Technology — Goal: Match travel sounds to vehicles at the listening center.
Activity: At the listening center, children will hear recorded travel sounds (train whistle, airplane hum, boat horn, car vroom) and hold up the matching vehicle card.

Grouping: Centers — pairs; child-led after setup
Support: Headphones and a two-choice screen for children who need fewer options.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Observe and tally real vehicles passing our school.
Activity: From our fenced yard, children will be vehicle watchers: tally every car, bus, truck, and bicycle that passes our school, then count our tallies and crown the busiest vehicle.

Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: A clipboard with the tally boxes pre-drawn big for easier marking.

Support: A 'waiting job' choice card (look at a book, count planes) for children practicing the skill in the moment.

Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Question prompt cards ('What is your favorite center?') for children thinking of what to ask.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Count collections up to 20 with a strategy.
Activity: To celebrate how much we have learned, children will build 'counting collections' of up to 20 objects, counting carefully in groups of five or ten and sharing their strategy with a partner.

Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: Collections capped at 10 for children consolidating smaller numbers first.

Creative Art — Goal: Draw a detailed self-portrait for a keepsake.
Activity: Children will draw 'Me, Now!' self-portraits for their keepsake folders, choosing details that show who they are today — hairstyle, favorite shirt, a big smile — and compare with a first-week drawing if one was saved.
Materials: Drawing paper; crayons; mirrors; keepsake folders
Grouping: Independent/small group — tables
Support: A September-style template offered for children who want a starting outline.

Music / Movement — Goal: Act out growing through a slow movement sequence.
Activity: To gentle music we will 'grow' like our whole year: curled tiny like our first days, then sprouting taller and taller until we stretch up as the big kids we are now.
Materials: Recorded gentle music; open space
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: The growth sequence done from a chair for children who need it.

Motor Activities — Goal: Practice independence skills for the next class.
Activity: Our 'big kid skills' stations will practice: carrying a tray with two hands, zipping and snapping dress-up clothes, opening lunch-style containers, and walking with a backpack.
Materials: Tray and cups; dressing frames/clothes; containers; backpacks
Grouping: Centers — classroom; teacher-guided
Support: Practice stations without time pressure and a teacher at the zipper board.

Technology — Goal: Record a proud 'I can' statement for families.
Activity: Each child will record an 'I can...' message on the voice recorder — 'I can count to twenty!' 'I can write my name!' — and we will save the recordings to share with families at the celebration.
Materials: Voice recorder or tablet (teacher-operated)
Grouping: Small groups; teacher-led
Support: The choice to record with a partner for children nervous to speak alone.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Visit and become familiar with next year's spaces.
Activity: We will walk the route to the next classroom's door and playground (if on site), peek at where we will play next year, and practice lining up at the new spot — making the new place feel friendly.

Grouping: Whole class — outdoors/school grounds; teacher-led
Support: A buddy from our own class to walk the route with for reassurance.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Hold two feelings at once and name a trusted adult.
Activity: Moving up can feel exciting AND wobbly — both feelings can live together. We will share one excited feeling and one wobbly feeling about next year, and name a grown-up we can always talk to.

Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: The feelings faces on the chart available to point at for children choosing their feeling.

Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led

Support: A front-row place where the words and actions are easy to follow.

Activity: Our celebration dance party will replay the year's favorite movement games — freeze dance, animal parade moves, the blast-off countdown — with children taking turns choosing the next game.

Grouping: Large group; teacher-led
Support: Free-dance zones and a quiet coloring corner for children who need a break from the party energy.

title: Rainforest: Welcome to the Rainforest
subject: Science
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Rainforest' thematic week (June): Welcome to the Rainforest. Focus book: The Great Kapok Tree — Lynne Cherry. evidence:
Focus book: The Great Kapok Tree — Lynne Cherry

Language Arts — Goal: Retell a cumulative story and give reasons in sequence.
Activity: We will read how a man comes to cut the kapok tree and the animals visit him one by one. Children will help list each animal and its reason the tree must stay, in the order they appeared.
Materials: Focus book; animal picture cards; chart paper
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Animal cards to hold for children who retell in the animals' voices with support.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Observe how leaves catch and slow rainwater.
Activity: We will test 'rainforest weather': the teacher will spray water over a leafy plant and over a bare tray to show how leaves catch and drip rain slowly, and children will describe what happens to each.
Materials: Spray bottle; leafy plant; tray; magnifiers
Grouping: Small groups — science table; teacher-led demo
Support: A hand lens for children and teacher narration describing each spray result.

Social Science — Goal: Locate the rainforest and understand it is a home for people and animals.
Activity: We will find the Amazon rainforest on our globe, talk about the people and animals who live there, and why the man in the story had a hard decision to make.
Materials: Globe; focus book
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: 'Far away' shown on the globe with a ribbon from our school to the forest for a concrete picture.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Count animal groups in a scene and compare amounts.
Activity: Using the focus book's tree scene, children will count the visiting animals one group at a time (monkeys, birds, frogs) and order their count cards from fewest to most.
Materials: Focus book scene; counters; number cards
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: Picture-by-picture counting with a partner for children building one-to-one skills.

Creative Art — Goal: Begin a group mural painting a great tree.
Activity: We will begin our week-long kapok tree mural: paint a huge trunk with wide branches on butcher paper, sponge bark texture, and leave the top empty for the canopy we will add each day.
Materials: Butcher paper; brown paints; sponges; smocks
Grouping: Large group in shifts — art area
Support: A stencil trunk for children who want to begin with the tree shape given.

Music / Movement — Goal: Build a group rainstorm soundscape with instruments.
Activity: We will create the sounds of rain in the forest with rain sticks, shakers (soft rain), and drums (distant thunder), starting quiet and growing as the 'storm' arrives.
Materials: Rain sticks; shakers; drums
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: A rainstick with two-handle grips for children who need a secure hold.

Motor Activities — Goal: Imitate rainforest animal movements with control.
Activity: Children will move like kapok animals: slither like the boa, creep like the anteater, swing arms like monkeys, and freeze tall like the tree itself.
Materials: Animal movement cards; open space
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: Each movement demonstrated slowly and a floor spot for a 'home tree' rest between animals.

Technology — Goal: Identify rainforest sounds and their sources.
Activity: Children will listen to real recorded rainforest sounds (rain, frogs, birds, monkeys) on the tablet and match each to its picture on our rainforest sound board.
Materials: Tablet with teacher-selected sounds; picture board
Grouping: Small group — listening area; teacher-guided
Support: Headphones and a two-choice animal board for children who need fewer options.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Measure a real tree and compare its size to our mural.
Activity: We will find the biggest tree at our school, try to hug all the way around its trunk with a chain of friends, measure it with a rope, and compare it to our mural kapok tree.
Materials: Rope; clipboards; school tree
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: A measuring partner and an 'arm's length' alternative for children who cannot reach around.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Practice listening and respecting the homes of living things.
Activity: The animals taught the man to listen. We will practice listening to nature — sitting quietly for ten slow breaths, then sharing one sound we noticed — and talk about protecting homes that are not ours.
Materials: Feelings chart; focus book (closing pages)
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Sentence frame ('The tree gives ___ a home') for children joining the discussion.

title: Rainforest: Layers of the Rainforest
subject: Science
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Rainforest' thematic week (June): Layers of the Rainforest. Focus book: Over in the Jungle: A Rain Forest Rhyme — Marianne Berkes. Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: Over in the Jungle: A Rain Forest Rhyme — Marianne Berkes

Language Arts — Goal: Count along with a rhyme and name the forest's layers.
Activity: We will read the counting rhyme, calling out the numbers as the animal families grow, and add layer words to our chart: forest floor, understory, canopy, emergent — simplified as bottom, middle-bushes, top leaves, and tallest trees.
Materials: Focus book; layer chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: The repeated counting line said together, giving every child the words.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Model the rainforest's four layers and test light at each level.
Activity: Children will build a layer model in a clear box: soil and toy beetles at the bottom, plants and frogs in the middle, leaves and monkeys up top — then test with a flashlight how dark the floor stays under the 'canopy.'
Materials: Clear boxes; soil; plants; toy animals; flashlight
Grouping: Small groups — science table
Support: A completed example layer box standing beside them to copy.

Social Science — Goal: Learn how scientists study the rainforest layer by layer.
Activity: We will talk about scientists who study the forest one layer at a time (some even sleep in the canopy!), and compare the tools of a rainforest scientist with our explorer tools at centers.
Materials: Scientist photo cards; explorer tools
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Partner comparisons so children decide similarities together first.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Count animals per layer and compare quantities by level.
Activity: Children will build a layer tower (floor, understory, canopy, emergent) with stacking blocks, count the animals they placed on each level, and compare which layer holds the most.
Materials: Layer stacking model; toy animals; number cards
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: Stacking rings provided as a model for children ordering the layers by size.

Creative Art — Goal: Add a printed-leaf canopy to the group mural.
Activity: Children will print leaf patterns onto green papers with real leaves and paint, cut or tear their favorites (teacher assists cutting), and glue them onto the mural's canopy layer.
Materials: Real leaves; green paints; paper; glue
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Pre-cut leaf shapes for children arranging rather than cutting.

Music / Movement — Goal: Change body levels to match each forest layer.
Activity: We will sing and move a layers song: crouch low for the forest floor, sway in the bushes, reach in the canopy, and stretch on tiptoes for the emergent layer, led by the teacher's hand signals.
Materials: Teacher-led song; layer cards
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: Layer picture cards held up before each change so children can prepare their bodies.

Motor Activities — Goal: Travel through movement layers: crawl, step, climb, stretch.
Activity: Our layer course travels the forest: crawl in the dark 'forest floor,' step over logs in the understory, climb the low platform 'canopy,' and stretch tall on the 'emergent' mat.
Materials: Tunnel; logs (foam); low platform; mats
Grouping: Small groups — movement area; teacher-supervised
Support: A floor-level 'floor layer' route for children who should not climb.

Technology — Goal: View the canopy layer in a guided video clip.
Activity: We will watch a short teacher-selected clip filmed high in a rainforest canopy, noticing the light, the leaves, and the animals that never come down to the ground.
Materials: Projector; teacher-selected clip
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A front seat for the best view of the canopy scenes; narration kept simple by the teacher.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Observe and sketch the layers of a real tree outdoors.
Activity: Outside, we will study one schoolyard tree in layers: what grows on the ground beneath it, what lives in its bushes, what nests in its branches, and what flies above its top. Children will sketch their tree's layers.
Materials: Journals; crayons; school tree
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: A clipboard sketch frame for children who draw more easily with a border.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Appreciate that everyone has a place where they belong.
Activity: Every layer of the forest is somebody's home, and every place in our classroom family matters too. Children will share which layer they would live in and one kind thing about a friend's 'place' in our class.
Materials: Layer chart; feelings chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A home-layer picture card to point to when sharing their feeling.

description: Preschool day plan from the 'Rainforest' thematic week (June): Rainforest Animals. Focus book: Animals of the Rainforest — — a picture book introducing rainforest animals and their colors, patterns, and hiding places (substitute any rainforest-animals title on hand). Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: Animals of the Rainforest — — a picture book introducing rainforest animals and their colors, patterns, and hiding places (substitute any rainforest-animals title on hand)

Language Arts — Goal: Share an animal fact with the group.
Activity: We will read our animal book and collect one wow-fact per animal on our fact wall. Each child will choose an animal, hold its card, and share its fact with the class like a scientist.
Materials: Focus book; fact cards; fact wall
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A fact card with the animal's photo to hold while sharing.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Find camouflaged animals and explain how colors hide them.
Activity: We will set a 'jungle corner' scene of plants and paper animals hidden by camouflage, and children will hunt for each hidden creature, checking off a list and describing what made it hard to see.
Materials: Plant display; paper animals; checklists
Grouping: Small groups — science area
Support: A seek-together partner for children overwhelmed by the busy jungle picture.

Social Science — Goal: Connect animals in a simple food web.
Activity: We will connect an animal web: the frog eats the fly, the snake eats the frog, the jaguar watches them all. Using yarn between picture cards, children will see how every animal depends on the others.
Materials: Yarn; animal picture cards
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Web strings limited to three connections for children building the idea.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Sort animals by movement and count each group.
Activity: Children will sort rainforest animal cards by how they travel — fly, climb, swim, walk — then count each travel group and say which way of moving has the most animals.
Materials: Animal cards; movement sorting mats
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: A move-only sorting round (no counting) for children who need one step at a time.

Creative Art — Goal: Paint an animal and place it in the right mural layer.
Activity: Children will draw and paint their chosen rainforest animal, then glue it into the mural at the correct layer — toucans in the canopy, jaguars stalking below, frogs near the floor.
Materials: Paper; paints; glue; mural
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Toucan outline provided for children who draw with a starter shape.

Music / Movement — Goal: Echo animal calls matching volume and rhythm.
Activity: We will play an echo game: the teacher calls like a howler monkey or croaks like a frog, and the class echoes the call back with matching volume and rhythm.
Materials: Animal call cards; open space
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: Call cards with pictures so the responding group knows its turn visually.

Motor Activities — Goal: Perform a sequence of four animal movements in a relay.
Activity: Our animal relay crosses the rug: frog leaps to the pond spots, sloth-slow reaches along the beam, monkey swings (arm motions) to the tree mat, and toucan 'flies' back.
Materials: Floor spots; balance beam; mats
Grouping: Small groups — movement area; teacher-supervised
Support: A shorter relay with the teacher stationed at the slither mat.

Technology — Goal: Zoom into animal photos to study camouflage patterns.
Activity: With the teacher, children will zoom into real close-up photos of rainforest animals on the tablet to study patterns — spots, stripes, and bright colors — and name what camouflage each pattern gives.
Materials: Tablet with teacher-selected photos
Grouping: Small groups; teacher-guided
Support: Teacher holds the tablet steady while the child chooses the next animal to zoom.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Find camouflage color matches in nature.
Activity: Outside, children will play camouflage seekers: each holds a colored cloth square and searches for nature that matches it exactly, learning how animals blend into their homes.
Materials: Colored cloth squares; schoolyard plants
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: Color-square partners for children who want to hunt in pairs.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Celebrate differences as strengths.
Activity: A poison-dart frog's bright colors and a sloth's mossy green both help their owners survive — different, and perfect for each. We will celebrate how our differences help our class too.
Materials: Animal photos; feelings chart
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Sentence frame ('I am special because I...') with examples first from the teacher.

title: Rainforest: Plants and Products
subject: Science
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Rainforest' thematic week (June): Plants and Products. Focus book: Gifts from the Rainforest — — a picture book about the fruits, plants, and useful gifts that come from rainforests (substitute any rainforest-products title on hand). Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: Gifts from the Rainforest — — a picture book about the fruits, plants, and useful gifts that come from rainforests (substitute any rainforest-products title on hand)

Language Arts — Goal: Sort foods by where they grow and learn their plant names.
Activity: We will read about bananas, pineapples, cocoa (chocolate!), and vanilla that begin in rainforests. Children will sort food picture cards into 'grows in the rainforest' and 'grows near us.'
Materials: Focus book; food picture cards; sorting mats
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Cards with photos and large print for children reading by picture.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Use smell to identify rainforest products and compare leaf sizes.
Activity: Children will smell sealed jars of rainforest scents — vanilla, cinnamon, cocoa — and match each smell to its picture, then examine a big banana leaf (or houseplant leaf) and compare its size to their own body.
Materials: Sealed sniff jars (teacher-prepared); large leaves; measuring cubes
Grouping: Small groups — science table
Support: Sniff jars labeled with big picture stickers for children matching by sight as well as smell.

Social Science — Goal: Trace how food travels from far away to us.
Activity: We will trace a banana's journey on a simple map — rainforest farm, boat, truck, our store, our snack table — and act out each stop passing the banana hand to hand.
Materials: Journey map; a real banana (teacher-held prop)
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: A simple two-stop map for children who need the journey shortened (farm, store).

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Vote, graph, and count favorite rainforest fruits.
Activity: Children will taste-with-eyes (look and smell only) our rainbow of rainforest fruits on picture cards, vote for the one they most want to try, and build our fruit graph, counting each column.
Materials: Fruit picture cards; floor graph
Grouping: Small group — math center
Support: Counting votes with a partner and graph rows color-coded for clarity.

Creative Art — Goal: Collage flowers and fruits into the group mural.
Activity: Children will make bright paper orchids and fruit shapes and glue them into the mural's middle layers, filling our forest with the gifts it grows.
Materials: Colored paper; glue; mural; scissors (teacher-assisted)
Grouping: Art center, groups of 4–5
Support: Flower petal shapes pre-cut for children assembling rather than cutting.

Music / Movement — Goal: Dance a harvest celebration with instruments and freezes.
Activity: We will shake maracas and dance a harvest celebration, moving fast for the 'picking' parts and freezing to 'load the baskets' when the music pauses.
Materials: Maracas; recorded lively music
Grouping: Large group — rug; teacher-led
Support: Shakers with secure lids and a defined dancing spot.

Motor Activities — Goal: Carry a loaded basket along a winding balance path.
Activity: Children will carry harvest baskets (filled with soft fruit) along a winding 'jungle trail' path, over a log step and around the river cone, delivering them to the market mat.
Materials: Baskets; soft fruit props; floor path; cones
Grouping: Small groups — movement area; teacher-supervised
Support: Lightweight baskets and a short path section for children building stamina.

Technology — Goal: Record a spoken thank-you message as a group.
Activity: Each child will record one line for our thank-you audio card — 'Thank you for the bananas!' — and we will play the whole card back at snack time (no food recording near allergies; audio only).
Materials: Voice recorder or tablet (teacher-operated)
Grouping: Small groups; teacher-led
Support: The recorder passed hand to hand so no child has to hold it long.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Identify plant parts and which parts people eat.
Activity: In our school garden, children will hunt for plant parts — a leaf we could eat, a root in the soil, a flower, a fruit — and sort their finds (photos/picture cards where picking isn't allowed) into our parts chart.
Materials: Garden beds; parts chart; picture cards
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: Sorting done with a partner pair so every plant part gets checked twice.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Show gratitude to faraway farmers who grow our food.
Activity: Many hands far away grow the bananas in our snack. We will practice thanking farmers we will never meet by making a thank-you drawing to hang by our snack table.
Materials: Drawing paper; crayons
Grouping: Large group then independent — carpet/tables
Support: A sentence frame ('Thank you for growing...') for support.

title: Rainforest: Protecting the Rainforest
subject: Science
description: Preschool day plan from the 'Rainforest' thematic week (June): Protecting the Rainforest. Focus book: We Can Help the Rainforest — — a picture book about children and animals working to protect the rainforest (substitute any conservation title on hand). Ten connected activities across literacy, science, social studies, math, art, music and movement, motor skills, technology, outdoor learning, and a life-lesson moment — each with a goal, materials, grouping, and a built-in support strategy so every child can join in.
evidence:
Focus book: We Can Help the Rainforest — — a picture book about children and animals working to protect the rainforest (substitute any conservation title on hand)

Language Arts — Goal: Dictate promises for a class pledge poster.
Activity: We will read our protection book and write a class pledge poster together: 'We Can Help the Rainforest By...' with each child dictating one promise to add.
Materials: Focus book; pledge poster; markers
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Pledge sentence starters ('I can help by...') with picture choices.

Science / Nature Studies — Goal: Explain three ways trees help and check a plant's needs.
Activity: We will review how trees help everyone — shade, animal homes, clean air — and inspect our class plant's needs with a picture checklist before our ceremony: light? water? room to grow?
Materials: Picture checklist; class plant; focus book
Grouping: Small groups — science table
Support: A checklist with pictures for children inspecting the seedling's needs.

Social Science — Goal: Teach guests about the rainforest as expert guides.
Activity: Children will become rainforest guides: our guest class (or a neighboring teacher) will visit the finished mural, and each guide will share one fact or promise at their station.
Materials: Finished mural; fact cards
Grouping: Large group — art area; teacher-supported
Support: A practiced single sentence and a partner beside them for the sharing.

Cognitive Skills & Math — Goal: Count a large display in teams and combine totals.
Activity: Our grand count: teams will count everything on the finished mural — animals, leaves, fruits, flowers — recording their totals and adding the counts together with the teacher's help.
Materials: Finished mural; tally sheets; number cards
Grouping: Large group — art area; teacher-led
Support: Counting in teams so the big mural count is shared, with a teacher tallying.

Creative Art — Goal: Complete and sign the group rainforest mural.
Activity: Children will finish the mural by pressing green handprint leaves all around its border, then each artist will sign their name (or mark) on our rainforest masterpiece.
Materials: Green paint; mural; name cards; smocks
Grouping: Large group in shifts — art area
Support: A sponge leaf stamp for children who want to add leaves without hand paint.

Music / Movement — Goal: Perform a soundscape with dynamic control for an audience.
Activity: We will perform our rainstorm soundscape for our guest class: starting with one rainstick's drizzle, building to full storm drums, and calming back to silence, conducted by the teacher's hands.
Materials: Rain sticks; shakers; drums
Grouping: Large group; teacher-led
Support: A quiet role (rain starter) for children who prefer gentle sounds to storm sounds.

Motor Activities — Goal: Complete the full rainforest layers course.
Activity: Our rainforest explorer finale course crosses all layers: tunnel floor crawl, log steps, platform climb, vine-swing arms, and a quiet tiptoe past the 'sleeping jaguar.'
Materials: Tunnel; logs; platform; mats
Grouping: Small groups — movement area; teacher-supervised
Support: Course sections can be skipped or shortened on request — success is finishing their way.

Technology — Goal: Review and celebrate the week's learning via slideshow.
Activity: We will watch the Rainforest week slideshow — layer models, camouflage hunts, mural days — and the kapok mural's growth from trunk to finished canopy, celebrating how our work grew like a forest.
Materials: Projector; week's photos (teacher-assembled)
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: Front seats for the screen; children can point out their mural section instead of speaking.

Outdoor Education — Goal: Hold a pledge ceremony and care for a living plant.
Activity: We will hold our pledge ceremony at our school tree: read our promises aloud, the teacher will tie the first ribbon, and we will water a newly planted class plant (or our garden bed) as our first act of protection.
Materials: Pledge poster; ribbon (teacher-tied); watering cans; plant
Grouping: Whole class — outdoors; teacher-led
Support: A partner to help carry the watering can between them.

Life Lesson Library — Goal: Make and keep a promise to care for nature.
Activity: We will close Rainforest week by making our promises real: each child will say or show their rainforest promise, and the teacher will tie our promise ribbons (kept for our school tree tomorrow) as a symbol that small hands can protect big places.
Materials: Promise ribbons (kept by teacher); pledge poster
Grouping: Large group — carpet; teacher-led
Support: The option to make their promise with a picture drawing instead of words.
